EquityBrief: a nightly level engine over the S&P 500, with deep research produced only when you open a name

Written to be read by someone who does not invest and has not seen the code. Every figure has a plain-language key (see: Every figure carries a plain-language key), every term is defined in section 3, every rule sits next to the reason it exists, and no component, decision or check carries a code number. This document is the specification: the report it describes is defined in section 4, and nothing outside these pages is authoritative.

1. Purpose and boundaries

What it is for. To select, every evening, the stocks worth buying or paying attention to as of that day, and then to produce a full research report on any name you choose to open. The operator's goal is that tonight's list holds the best stocks at a buy point for a swing trade of a few weeks, and that any name in the index still opens to its report. The list is chosen by the swing filter's gates, each a fact about the chart or the plan, and drawn improving businesses first, by the direction of each company's reported quarters, and the improvement loop in section 13 exists to make it select better. (see: Tonight's list selects the stocks worth buying or paying attention to that evening, and the improvement loop exists to make that selection better) (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it) Four of the six conditions detect arrival at a price the evening's arithmetic has an instruction for, one detects a break on unusual volume, and one is a calendar fact, and the six are computed for every name every night and stand beside the list as context. The arithmetic the gates read is not authored in advance and is not carried over from a previous night: the levels and the plan are recomputed from the chart every evening, so a name arriving at a level and the plan naming that level are the same night's work. Whether a listed name's setup succeeds is measured by the loop over time rather than asserted, and section 13 is how. The universe is the S&P 500, 400 and 600, each member tagged with its index, and their membership is fetched rather than maintained by hand, the 500's from the provider and the 400's and 600's from their funds' holdings files. (see: The universe is the S&P 1500's three indices with each member tagged by its index, and membership is fetched) The report it produces, specified in section 4, (see: Section 4 of the architecture defines the report region by region, and nothing outside the corpus does) carries a narrative verdict, how the stock got here with the causes of its biggest moves, what the company sells, the numbers over five quarters, the industry cycle it sits in, the bull and bear cases side by side, a chart with levels and a volume profile, a staged entry and exit plan in two books, a risk table where every risk names the number that would confirm it, and a dated calendar.

The constraint that shapes everything. Nightly work must be free and fast, and paid work must happen only when you ask for it. So the nightly run is arithmetic over price bars with no model calls and no per-name network calls, and everything expensive happens when you open a name and is then stored permanently with the date it was written.

What it is not. The universe is a published index membership, not a filtered set, and tonight's list is chosen on the chart and the plan alone, with no model in the decision. The one reading of the fundamentals it uses is the direction of each company's reported quarters, sales and operating margin against a year earlier, which orders the names the chart and the plan chose and removes none. (see: Four readings of a member's reported quarters are worked out every night by rules the measured split settled, and its state is read from sales and operating margin alone) It does not trade, sizes a position only on a pick's card from the account the operator keeps on its own page, and produces no short or options ideas. (see: The plan places a position and never sizes one) (see: A pick's card sizes its plan from the operator's own settings, and the report's plan still sizes none)

Rules choose the stocks, and a language model writes only the reports. Every stock a list draws, and the order it draws them in, comes from rules over stored prices, filings, counts and dates, and no language model's output decides, filters, ranks or orders a pick, a family, a variant, a gate or a record. A language model writes the research reports, and labels the news for the reader and for the reports alone. The reason is the test the picks are held to: a rule can be replayed over the stored history as each night stood and scored, and gives the same answer when it is run again, where a language model's judgment can be neither replayed as it stood nor reproduced. A statistical model fitted by code to the ledger passes that test, so it is a rule, and it orders a list only as a rule's registered setting the operator approved (see: Rules choose the stocks, and a language model writes only the reports) (see: A fitted statistical model is a rule)

Who runs it. Program in .NET, with a local model on and an EODHD subscription.

2. The shape in one paragraph

After the US close, one bulk call fetches the day's bars for the whole exchange. For all 500 names the system computes indicators, swings, a volume profile, level bands, a trend label, an entry and exit ladder, the six reasons as context, the four readings of its reported quarters and the state they give it, and each name's answer at the swing filter's five gates. That is seconds of arithmetic and it costs nothing. The result is stored. After it, the provider is asked for the quarters of the members that reported since the last night, which the next night reads (see: A member's reported quarters are fetched on the night after it reports, and asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that until the quarter is posted). When you open the app you see tonight's list, the names the swing filter passed, improving businesses first and each state in the filter's order (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it). When you open a name, the computed sections of its report appear immediately from the store, its fundamentals fill from the provider, and if no research record exists for it a research pass runs once, reads filings and news, writes the narrative sections, and stores them with an as-of date and every source it read. Opening that name again shows the stored research with its date. A new pass runs only when a filing appears, an earnings date passes, the name's news feed moves materially, or you press refresh. (see: Research is a stored document with an as-of date, not a cache)

3. Vocabulary

Every specialist word used later in this document. Market words first, then the project's own words.

WordMeaning here
TickerThe short code for a listed company. MU is Micron Technology.
Daily barOne trading day as five numbers: opening price, highest price, lowest price, closing price, and shares traded. A candlestick chart draws one per day.
Moving averageThe average closing price over the last n days, recalculated daily. It smooths noise. Price above a rising average is the simplest definition of an uptrend.
Support, resistancePrices where the stock has repeatedly stopped falling, or stopped rising. They matter because many participants watch the same prices, so the behaviour repeats.
Swing high, swing lowA local peak or trough: a day whose high or low is more extreme than the days on either side of it.
BandA level given as a range rather than one price, because several reasons for a level usually cluster within a few points. The report writes "900 to 940" rather than claiming a precision it does not have.
Fibonacci retracementFixed fractions (23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 78.6%) of the distance between a swing high and a swing low. Widely watched, so bounces often stall there.
Volume profile, volume at priceHow many shares changed hands in each price band over a period. Where a lot traded, many holders have that price as their cost, so they defend it on the way down and sell at breakeven on the way up. Where little traded, price moves through quickly.
ATR, average true rangeHow far the stock moves on a normal day, averaged over 14 days. The report calls it "a typical day's move". It sets how far a stop must sit so ordinary noise does not trigger it.
RSIA momentum score from 0 to 100. Near 50 is balanced, above 70 stretched upward, below 30 stretched downward.
MACDThe gap between a fast and a slow average, with a signal line. A shrinking positive histogram means a rally is losing pace rather than reversing.
Trend stateA one-word label for the chart, uptrend, downtrend or range. It decides which ladder shape applies and how stops are placed.
TrancheOne step of a staged purchase. The plan buys at successively lower support bands rather than all at once.
StopThe price at which an entry is admitted to be wrong. This system uses daily-close stops: the exit triggers only if the day ends beyond the line, because intraday dips through a level are routine.
InvalidationThe single price below which the whole position, not just one tranche, is wrong.
Reward to riskDistance from entry to target divided by distance from entry to stop, which on the swing filter's list is read from the swing plan entered at the night's close.
The print, guidanceThe quarterly results announcement, and the company's own forecast for the next quarter given with it. Stocks move most on those days.
Base rateWhat happens to an average name on an average night. Any claim that a signal predicts something must beat it, because most stocks rise over a month regardless.
Break-evenThe share of the time a plan must reach its target before its stop simply to come out level. It is arithmetic on the plan's own numbers: risk divided by risk plus reward. A plan with a distant target and a tight stop needs to be right rarely; one with a near target and a wide stop needs to be right often.
Computed sectionA part of the report produced by arithmetic over stored bars and provider data. No model is involved and every number is reproducible.
Researched sectionA part of the report produced by a model reading filings, news and theme material. Written once, stored with an as-of date, and never rewritten on a timer.
Facts fileThe JSON for one name on one night holding every number the computed sections may use, each with its source. It is what the model is allowed to see and what the fixture is diffed against.
Research recordThe stored output of one research pass for one name: the prose of each researched section, the as-of date, the model used, and every source document read.
Theme recordResearch about an industry rather than a company, for example memory-chip contract pricing. One record serves every name in that industry.
Tonight's listThe names the swing filter passed tonight, drawn in its order with no fixed length, and on an evening before the switch the names where one of the six reasons fired.
ReasonOne of the six stated conditions, which chose tonight's list before the swing filter did and stand beside its names as context from it.
ListingThe record of one member on one night, holding which reasons fired and the plan as it stood that night, written for every member every night whether or not the evening's rule listed it and kept forever (see: Your own listing history is kept forever) (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it).
SetupOne listing considered as a prediction: an entry, a stop and a target that will eventually be right or wrong. A setup starts on the first close at or below its entry zone's top edge and is resolved when the target is reached, the stop is closed through, or the time cap expires; a target reached before it starts is never entered, and never a win.
ShadowScored and stored exactly like a live thing but acting on nothing, its picks drawn on the Run page alone and its results nowhere until a look reads them. A shadow condition accumulates a record of how it would have done, so a decision to adopt it later rests on evidence rather than on the idea.
FixtureA frozen, committed set of inputs with expected outputs beside them, so a run is checked by diff rather than by opinion.
HarnessThe one command that reads this document's tables, checks the code against them, runs the fixture, and reports every claim as PASS, FAIL or UNEXAMINED.
BlockFor judging a candidate, a run of 63 consecutive trading sessions keyed on the session its setup was read on, the unit its test counts because setups inside one block can share the bars they resolve over.
LookOne of the few points, fixed when a candidate is registered, at which its verdict is read: at 8, 12 and 16 non-empty blocks. Between looks the verdict does not move.
Information fractionHow far a candidate is through the evidence it was registered to gather, the blocks it holds over the blocks at its last look. The looks sit at 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0.
Null win probabilityThe chance a setup with no edge reaches its target before its stop, simulated from its own plan, costs and the name's volatility. It replaces the planned break-even as the bar a setup is scored against.
Design effectHow much the clustering of setups inflates the variance of a record over what the same number of independent setups would give. At 2, a record of 250 carries the information of 125.
Sign-flip testThe test a candidate is judged by: each block's excess of wins over null probabilities is flipped in sign in every combination, and the p-value is the share of combinations at least as extreme as the one observed.
Futility guidelineA rule, read only at the first two looks, that retires a candidate whose record is running below its bar. It binds nothing: the promotion boundary is computed as if it did not exist.
Monitoring figureThe running figure the run page shows every night for a candidate, labelled so. It is not the verdict, which only a look changes.
Closed windowA setup whose whole outcome window has passed, so its result can no longer change. A look counts only these.
Swing filterThe five gates, the trigger's arrival and the exclusions that choose tonight's list, each a stated condition read off the chart and the plan.
GateOne question the swing filter asks of every member each night, in order the market, the name's trend and strength, a setup, a trigger and a trade.
BreadthThe share of the index's members closing above their own 200-day average, which the market gate reads against its floor.
Relative strengthA member's place among the index's members by its return over 63 and over 126 sessions, the mean of the two places.
Pullback, depthHow far the close sits below the highest high of the last 20 sessions, counted in typical days' moves.
Dry-upThe median volume of the sessions since that high against the fifty-day average, which a pullback wants low.
Tight base, tightnessA range whose last ten sessions move less than its last fifty, the base a breakout leaves from.
BreakoutA close above a band that sat at or above the previous close, on volume above its multiple of the fifty-day average.
Trigger, arrivalThe setup's event, a close above the previous session's high or back inside its band, which arrives when it first happens inside the arrival window.
Swing planThe trade the swing filter reads, section 10's plan applied to it: entered at the night's close, stopped below the setup band's low edge, or below the next support band's where that is less than a typical day's move below the entry, and targeting the lowest band two typical days' moves or more above; the plan at the nearest bands, stopped below the setup band's low edge and targeting the nearest band above, is scored beside it for the variant that reads it.
ExclusionA reason a name passing every gate is still left off the list, being earnings inside the holding window, a suspect series or a gap.
Filter versionOne set of the swing filter's settings, opened by your shape command and named on every row a night stores under it.
Shape clockThe count of ordinary nights under one filter version that proposes a setting once a gate's median count sits outside its band.
Event night, ordinary nightA night one cause pushes a usually quiet gate or reason far past its own normal share is an event night that no median reads, and every other night is ordinary.
Gate bandThe range each gate's median count through the funnel is held against, a third to three times what the ruled filter passed.
Edge clockThe swing family's records read at looks over blocks, which can retire a candidate at its first look and promote one no earlier than its second.
Swing familyThe live filter and eight variants, each a whole rule with one thing moved, the sixth leaving off a member whose reported quarters read deteriorating, the seventh reading a member's standing in its sector in place of the trend and strength gate and the eighth keeping the night's best three in the list's own order, judged together as one family of nine.
Near missA setup one gate or one exclusion alone rejected while everything else passed, read against its own break-even and null.
List ruleThe rule an evening's list was drawn by, the six reasons before the switch and the swing filter from it, which every surface names.

4. The report, section by section, and where each part comes from

A name's report is the page drawn for it: up to twenty-three regions, in the order of this table, each a card that the contents at the head of the page names as the first column does and links to. A page draws a region only where it has something to draw: why the name is here only when it is on the night's list, its swing readings, its member readings and its gates where the night stored them, its group where it has one, its earnings reactions where the calendar holds a print, the nights the live list picked it before where there were any, the industry cycle where its industry's theme has been written, and each written region only where that region has been written, save the short version, which code writes where no accepted one stands. This table is the specification and the contract: it says what produces each region, whether it costs money, and how often it changes. Read the last two columns together, because they are the whole cost argument. Six regions are written by the paid model when a report is asked for. The other sixteen need no paid call to be drawn, though two of them carry a part the paid model writes, the causes of the moves and the dated items the research read, and fourteen of the sixteen change every night, the numbers in what they say first. (see: Section 4 of the architecture defines the report region by region, and nothing outside the corpus does)

Key. A region is "free" when it needs no paid model call and no per-name network request to be drawn. The free regions are recomputed for all 500 names every night, so opening any name shows a current chart, a current level map and a current plan even if nobody has ever asked for its report. The written regions exist only for names whose report has been asked for, and once written they are read from the store and written again only when a report is asked for again (see: Nothing expires on a timer). (see: Facts are declared once and cited by descriptive name)

A name whose report has never been asked for therefore still has a complete short report: every region but the six the paid model writes, with the moves table's cause column empty and no dated items beside the calendar, and a last region saying the written regions have not been written, with the control that asks for them.

What the numbers say, pattern by pattern

What the numbers say is written by code from these patterns and no model. A slot in braces is filled from the night's stored reading and nothing else: a percentage to one decimal place, a ratio to two, a multiple to one, a count whole and a quarter by the date it ended. The heading carries the state, and the sentences follow in the order of the rows: the quarter awaited where a newer one is, then the trajectory, the record, the quality and the valuation, one sentence for each reading, and a member holding no quarter is given the last row alone. The sales row's two changes are each written as one of the three rows after it. Each pattern describes the business and none advises buying or selling, and the heading says which readings the state is read from, so a state of improving beside earnings that ran ahead of cash says why both can stand (see: Four readings of a member's reported quarters are worked out every night by rules the measured split settled, and its state is read from sales and operating margin alone). The read-surface check holds this table and the patterns the renderer writes from to each other word for word, in both directions.

PatternWritten as
headingWhat the numbers say: {state}, read from sales and operating margin alone
awaitedThe quarter to {quarter} is awaited, so these read the quarter to {quarter}.
salesSales {change} on a year earlier in the quarter to {quarter}, and {change} in the quarter to {quarter}.
sales roserose {percent}
sales fellfell {percent}
sales heldheld level
pace fasterThe newer quarter's growth was faster than the {percent} the same quarter showed a year before.
pace slowerThe newer quarter's growth was slower than the {percent} the same quarter showed a year before.
pace sameThe newer quarter's growth matched the {percent} the same quarter showed a year before.
margin widerThe operating margin was {percent} against {percent} a year earlier, wider for {count} quarter(s) in a row.
margin narrowerThe operating margin was {percent} against {percent} a year earlier, narrower for {count} quarter(s) in a row.
margin unchangedThe operating margin was {percent}, where it stood a year earlier.
trajectory too fewSales and the operating margin cannot be read against a year earlier over the two newest quarters.
recordAgainst the analysts' estimates over its last {count} quarters it beat {count}, met {count} and missed {count}, met meaning within a cent or 1% of the estimate.
record too few{count} of the {count} quarters a record needs carry both an actual and an estimate, so no record is stated.
quality aheadOperating cash flow over the last four quarters was {ratio} times net income: earnings ran ahead of cash.
quality in lineOperating cash flow over the last four quarters was {ratio} times net income: in line.
quality backedOperating cash flow over the last four quarters was {ratio} times net income: more than backed by cash.
quality lossNet income over the last four quarters was a loss, so cash is not compared against it.
quality missingThe last four quarters do not all carry operating cash flow and net income, so earnings quality is not read.
valuation cheapAt tonight's close it trades at {multiple} times its last four quarters' earnings, the cheap end of the {multiple} to {multiple} range of its last {count} quarters.
valuation middleAt tonight's close it trades at {multiple} times its last four quarters' earnings, the middle of the {multiple} to {multiple} range of its last {count} quarters.
valuation expensiveAt tonight's close it trades at {multiple} times its last four quarters' earnings, the expensive end of the {multiple} to {multiple} range of its last {count} quarters.
valuation too few{count} of the {count} quarters a range needs carry a multiple, so the valuation position is not read.
valuation no earningsIts last four quarters' earnings are not above nought, so no multiple is read.
valuation no basisTonight's close cannot be set on the price basis the quarters were fetched on, so no multiple is read.
noneNo reported quarter is stored for it yet, so nothing is read.

5. System overview

Key. Orange boxes are things outside the system. Blue boxes with a top rule are stores the system owns. Green boxes compute, and every number in a report is born in one of them (see: Code owns every number). Purple boxes are the only ones that spend money, and they sit below the line because nothing above it can trigger them. Teal boxes serve pages. The red box decides whether a phase is finished.

The important property of the picture is the line across the middle. Nothing in the top half calls a model or makes a per-name network request, so a night costs one bulk download and a few seconds of arithmetic no matter how large the index is (see: The nightly run is arithmetic only). Nothing in the bottom half runs unless you open something (see: Nothing expires on a timer).

The news pulse counter sits in the top half deliberately. Judging whether stored research has gone stale needs to be free, or the system would have to spend money to discover that it does not need to spend money.

6. The layers, one at a time

6.1 Sources outside

Prices, index membership, company financials, the earnings calendar and news all come from EODHD, which is already subscribed. Bars arrive through the bulk end-of-day endpoint, which returns the whole exchange in one request, so the nightly fetch does not grow with the size of the universe. The S&P 500's membership comes from the index constituents endpoint, which carries join and leave dates, and the S&P 400's and 600's from their funds' holdings files on iShares' own site, one request a fund at no weight on the allowance, so membership is fetched rather than maintained by hand (see: The universe is the S&P 1500's three indices with each member tagged by its index, and membership is fetched) (see: The S&P 400's and 600's members are read each night from their funds' own holdings files). News arrives through one dated query for the whole exchange, paged until the day is covered, and is attributed to names in code rather than asked for per name (see: News is one dated query, paged to cover the day, and attributed to names locally).

Filings come from the regulatory archive, which is free, needs no key, and returns reported financials as structured data. Three things are taken from it. Segment revenue and margin by business unit, which the segment commentary and the numbers' segment table in section 4 need. Management's own guidance, published as the earnings press release exhibit to a results announcement rather than as structured data. And, where a company chooses to file one, the verbatim call transcript as a second exhibit to the same filing.

That third item is opportunistic and the design does not depend on it. Some companies file a transcript and most do not, so the two-cases section is written from the press release and the filings for most names and gains the analysts' questions for the few that file them. No transcript provider is required, and the report omits what it does not have rather than guessing. (see: Transcripts are opportunistic, never a dependency)

Two kinds of model are used for different jobs. A local model on the operator's GPU writes prose from numbers, which is a small job it does well and free. A hosted model does research, which is a large-context job a local model does badly. Which hosted model a job uses is configuration and not code: the settings file holds one profile per model, naming its wire format, its address, the model, the section of the secrets file its key sits under, the options it is asked with, the rates it is priced at and the earliest date its provider publishes for retiring it, and each paid job names the profile it uses by one word. Which profile the research job names is the operator's to switch, and switching its model is changing that word and nothing else; a job whose profile names a key the secrets file does not hold stops, and no other profile answers for it. The research job also maps each section to a profile word, so one section can be written by another model while the rest stay on the job's, and a Claude profile states its thinking as off or an effort level. A trial asks a second profile for named sections after a report over a stated number of reports, and records its drafts beside the report on the run log and never in it; it ships naming none. Report generation asks DeepSeek alone, on the operator's ruling of 2026-09-30, so no research setting names a Claude profile. The report footer always says which model wrote what, with the options it was asked with. (see: Research names a profile per section as well as per job, and a Claude profile states its thinking) (see: A trial asks a second profile for named sections beside a report, and ships naming none) (see: Report generation asks DeepSeek alone, and no research setting names a Claude profile) (see: A local model writes prose from numbers and each paid job names the hosted model the operator chooses in configuration) (see: A paid job names its model profile in one word the operator switches, and a profile is priced at its configured rates at its call's own timestamp) (see: A paid model is one interface with an implementation per wire format, and a job never falls back from the profile it names) (see: A research record is written and dated per section, not as a whole)

A paid model on the OpenAI format is asked to stream its answer, and the pieces are read into the answer the provider would have sent whole, so one reader reads both. An answer asked for whole carries nothing until the model has finished reasoning, and a connection silent for a minute is cut on the way: every answer that took longer was lost, and none that answered had taken longer. A stream that ends before the provider says it is done is an answer cut short and is not stored. (see: A paid model on the OpenAI format is asked to stream its answer, because a connection silent for a minute is cut)

One consequence shapes the research runner. The research model is given no web search of its own, whichever provider serves it, so the model cannot go and find things; it can only read what it is handed through tool calls (see: The model never fetches; components fetch and hand it documents). For a per-name pass that costs nothing, because the documents it needs are filings and news the system already fetches. For a theme record it matters, because an industry's own pricing cycle is published by research firms rather than filed with a regulator, and that is section 22's second question.

The shipped provider's rates carry a peak and off-peak split, with peak at double, and the configuration states both. In Eastern time the peak windows fall late at night, so the market session and the hours just after the close are off-peak and interactive reading is never billed at the peak rate. Anything queued rather than interactive is scheduled into off-peak deliberately (see: Queued work runs off-peak, and every schedule is written in UTC). A queued pass starts only where the longest pass the store holds would end before the next peak window opens, because a pass's paid calls come at its end, so the night's own report, asked after the overnight queue, can wait until the window ends (see: A pass starts only where the longest pass the store holds would end before a peak window opens).

6.2 Store owned

One SQLite file. The bar store keeps one year of bars per name for every night's work, and the history the operator pulls for the years before it sits beside it in tables of its own that no night, score or page reads (see: The bar store holds one year for every night's work, and the history pulled beside it is read by measurements alone). One year for 500 names is about 10 MB, and the whole store, the history pulled back to 2018 and the research among it, is about half a gigabyte, so it is copied into a fixture, diffed and backed up by hand (see: The whole system is a checkout and one database file). Section 16 lists the tables.

6.3 Compute deterministic, nightly

This layer holds the stages that compute and the fetchers that feed them, and the property the fixture rests on belongs to the first group. Every stage that computes is a pure function of stored data: given the same bars it produces the same facts file byte for byte, which is what makes the fixture diff possible. The fetchers are not pure and nothing but this sentence ever said they were, which it did by calling every component in the layer pure and giving a count of eleven that the catalogue passed during phase 4 and that nothing read. A fetcher's property is a different one and is asserted elsewhere: one request for the whole index whatever its size, every page counted, and a payload refused rather than stored where it is not the answer that was asked for. The four carrying the most logic are opened up in sections 8 to 11.

6.4 Research on demand, paid

A pass runs for one name when it is opened and no valid record exists. It reads that name's filings and recent news, reads or triggers its theme record, and writes the narrative sections. Everything it read is stored with the record. The claim checker then rejects numbers not present in the facts file and claims whose source is not in the store. What survives is written once and read from then on.

6.5 Serve pages

A local web application serves a read-only API over the store and hosts the single-page app. Reports are rendered in the browser from stored data rather than written to disk nightly, so a layout change costs nothing and nothing goes stale on disk. The exporter renders one name through the same code path into a self-contained file, because handing a single report to someone is a stated use. (see: A single report can still be exported as a self-contained file)

6.6 Check sign-off

The harness is what makes a phase finished. It has no opinion of its own; it reads the claims this document makes and tests them. Section 19.

The name is the key. The harness looks for a class of this exact name with spaces removed, and asserts it reads and writes only what is listed here. A component touching a store not listed fails its row. There are no code numbers; cite a component by its name, spelled exactly.
