The green dot is its best close, read as how far it went in risks and how many sessions after the buy it came; the red dot is where it ended, at a close under its stop, and its worst close. The trade closed a risk up before its stop ended it, which is the count the autopsy keeps of the stop's trades.

The teal square is the same path under the menu's exit that raises the stop to the buy once a close is a risk up: from the session after that close, the first close under the buy sells the trade. Whether that exit is better is never read off one path or off the autopsy's figures; the tester reads it over every trade, on the years it never saw.

13.14 The learned score

The third engine is a score: one sum over the readings the night hands a rule's hooks, each times a weight fitted to the ledger's finished setups, a higher sum standing for a setup whose edge over the same plan on every member that session ran further (see: A fitted statistical model is a rule). It is fitted by ridge regression. Each reading is put on one scale over the rows it is fitted on, and a penalty fixed before any row is read pulls every weight toward nothing, so a reading earns weight only by what it does over many setups; the S&P 400's and 600's shifts from the S&P 500's are fitted beside the readings with no penalty, since the rows are pooled across the three indices. The label is each setup's edge in typical moves with the risk floored at one move, so a setup whose stop sat close counts for no more than its move, clipped at the rows' first and ninety-ninth hundredths so a handful of runaway trades cannot set the weights. A reading held by fewer than nineteen rows in twenty is not weighed, a row missing a reading that is weighed is left out, and the weekdays to the next report are never weighed, since the history reads them from the day each report came. The fit is solved in closed form in a fixed order and draws nothing at random, so the same rows give the same weights, and its parameters, the hash of their canonical text, the setups it learned on, the session its window was cut at and the pin of the code that fitted it are stored with every run.

Inside the tester each fold fits the score on the family's setups on all three indices whose paths ended before its year, and brings three proposals: the rule's list ordered by the score, highest first, and the same with the setups under the fold's lowest fifth or lowest two fifths of the scores it learned on, on the index, left off. Each is walked through the hooks a registration would set, exactly as the night orders and keeps a hooked rule's candidates, against the rule as it stands over the fold's year; a fold holding too few setups fits no score and its year reads the rule today. The score fitted on all finished data names the proposal, with its importances in words: the readings weighing most, which way each pushes, and the share of the weight the business readings carry.

A score reaches a pick in two ways, both beneath the rule's record on the card. The setups like the pick under its rule are matched each night from the ledger on the readings weighing most in the index's newest score and drawn with their mean edge, its interval and the rule's own mean beside it. The pick's rank under the score, its place in hundredths among the setups the score learned on on its index, is drawn only once one of the score's proposals has passed the tester on that index, and until then the card, the Loop page and the stock's page each read "Score not yet validated on this index" (see: A pick's card draws the setups like it under its rule beneath the rule's record, and the score's rank only once the score passed on its index). No rule standing is ordered by a score: that waits on a proposal passing and the operator approving it.

13.15 The fundamentals-first family

The fundamentals-first family reads the business first and the chart second, on all three indices (see: The fundamentals-first family buys an improving business in an uptrend at the pullback's buy point). The S&P 400's and 600's step reads it, from 17.8 reading the S&P 500 first for this family alone, so no source an S&P 500 family's version pins moves; on each index its card stands after the index's own families', one trade a stock across every card of every index, and the S&P 500's list of it holds back a stock the S&P 500's own families listed that night. Its candidates are the members the pullback's base lists on the night, at the base's buy point, stop, target and cap and in its order, held to the index's floors, and each is read through five checks in turn, the first it fails named on its row: its profit in the index's form, its revenue, its margins, its cash and its trend. Every reading is the setup ledger's, read through its catalogue as it stood on the session, the business readings from the facts the company filed with the SEC before the session as first filed, so a filing stored before the night and filed before its session moves the member's answer that night, and one filed on the session is read from the next (see: The SEC's facts are stored as first filed in a table the night reads, and a setup's business readings read those filed before its session). A reading the night does not hold passes no check, and a night that reads none lists nobody under the family and says why on every row. It lists on its provisional setting, revenue growing at all, either margin widening on the year and cash from operations at least the year's net income, until the operator rules on its search.

Profit in the index's form. The four newest quarters filed before the session sum their net income above nothing and the newest of them is above nothing, the quarters as the night's quarters fetch stored them. Evidence: S&P Dow Jones Indices (2020) set this test for a company joining the S&P 600 and credit it with much of that index's lead over a small company index that holds unprofitable companies. Judgement: the same test on the S&P 500 and 400, whose own rules ask it of a company joining them, rather than the profit gate's four quarters alone.

Revenue. The newest quarter's revenue as first filed before the session is above the same quarter's a year before by more than the setting's floor, and that growth is above the growth the quarter before had on its own year before. Evidence: Jegadeesh and Livnat (2006) find a revenue surprise predicts returns beyond the earnings surprise it comes with; Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok (1996) find prices take in earnings news gradually, over the months after it. Judgement: the floor at nothing, five or ten per cent, and growing faster than the quarter before as the reading of rising, neither of which a study sets.

Margins. The newest quarter's gross margin, its operating margin or both, as the setting names, is above the same quarter's a year before, each margin its profit over its revenue as first filed. Evidence: Novy-Marx (2013) finds gross profitability predicts returns about as well as book to market does; Asness, Frazzini and Pedersen (2019) find companies that are profitable, growing and safe earn more for their risk, growth in profitability among what they measure. Judgement: a margin widening on the year in place of the level of profit the studies sort on, so a company improving from a low margin can pass.

Cash. The newest fiscal year's cash from operations is at least the setting's multiple of its net income, both as first filed before the session, read only where that income is above nothing. Evidence: Sloan (1996) finds earnings resting on accruals rather than cash persist less, and that prices read them as though they persisted; Green, Hand and Soliman (2011) find the returns to trading on accruals faded after the finding was published, so the check stands as a test of the earnings' quality and not as a signal of its own. Judgement: the multiple's three levels, below, at and above the income, none of which a study sets.

Trend. The close is above its 200-session average and the 50-session average above the 200-session average. Judgement: no study sets this gate for a screen of businesses; it holds the family to companies the market is already carrying up, as the operator's brief asked.

The buy. A member passing every check is bought at the pullback's buy point at the base's settings, its plan the pullback's own, and post-earnings drift is no trigger. Evidence: Martineau (2022) finds the drift after an earnings surprise gone from large companies since 2006 and more recently from smaller ones. Judgement: the pullback's buy point is the one entry every index already replays and records, so the business chooses which stock and the pullback chooses when.

The search. The family's search on an index is a grid of 27 settings written in the code before it runs, every level of three dials: the revenue floor at nothing, five or ten per cent, the margin either, both or the operating alone, and the cash at three multiples of the income. It walks the pullback's base listings over the history as it stood, five a night with one open trade a stock under the pullback's own exit, keeping a listing where every check passes on its session, each trade after its round trip and against the same plan on every member that session, and a setting passes the family floors, its trades and its years above nothing, with two of the last three years above nothing; the report states what luck alone passes of the 27. The search reads the store and writes nothing, and what it finds is put to the operator with no freeze (see: No family on any index is set aside or hidden by a test result without the operator's word). Judgement: three levels a dial, the brief's own words at the loosest of the revenue floor and the margin and the middle of the cash, so the grid reads a stricter version of each.

13.16 Approval and the live alarm

A proposal that passes the tester changes nothing until the operator approves it on the Loop page (see: Every change to a rule waits for the operator's approval on the Loop page, and the automatic mode ships off). The page offers Approve and Decline on each proposal of an index's newest run that passed and states a change, one approval a family a run, and a press writes one row of the decisions under the page's own header and nothing else, a decline with its reason. Before the next night the night's own build applies each approval no apply has answered (see: An approved change is applied before the next night from the night's own build, on the index it was approved on alone). On the S&P 400 or 600 a swing family's change is written on top of the setting the family stands at, as a new row of the provisional settings that is never edited, and the family is read at it from that night on, on that index alone: its list kept and ordered by the hooks the setting stores, its trades walked under the exit it names, its breakouts forming read at its setting, its card stating the change, and the record replayed at the setting before it drawn as no record of the rule as it stands. The tester from then on tests every proposal for the family against the rule as it stands, a proposal's hooks set on top of those it stores as an approval sets them. An S&P 500 rule's page is drawn by its family's own code, and a sector heavyweights book changes its setting by a freeze alone, so a change to either is refused with why and waits on the operator's ruling of how it reaches its page; so is a change to a family whose live rule stands registered on its index, since that rule draws the page. A declined proposal changes nothing and is put again only once a later run reads a new complete block and it passes with that block (see: A declined proposal is put again once a new complete block has been added since the decline and it passes with that block). The adopt setting ships reading on approval, and reads automatic only where the operator sets it so; then the strongest proposal that passed in a family of an index's newest run is applied with no word, one a family a run.

The live alarm watches what an approval cannot: a rule that stops working (see: The live alarm flags a rule whose edge stood under its reference's fifth percentile two periods running). Each tester run stores beside its proposals the rule today's trades over its test years with their edge after costs, the rule's reference. Each night the alarm reads each live rule's trades by the month they ended in, a sector heavyweights book's holdings by quarter, once the month has closed and every trade in it holds its edge: their mean against the fifth percentile of ten thousand means of as many of the reference's trades, drawn at a fixed seed by a stationary bootstrap over the reference's weeks. A month of fewer than five trades neither counts nor breaks a run, and two counted months running under that floor flag the rule on its index's Tonight and Loop page, with a restore of the setting before the newest approved change waiting for the operator's approval where an approval changed the rule. The flag changes nothing by itself. The reference reads high, since the rule today was chosen on its own test years, so the alarm catches a rule that has broken, a drop of about half a risk a trade or more, and not one drifting a little.

Key. Read each column downward, one month, one index: the large caps are the S&P 500, the mid caps the S&P 400 and the small caps the S&P 600. The blue-topped boxes are what the night recorded on each index, its own ledger setups and its rules' own trades. Green boxes compute: the tester judges each index's proposals against that index's rules today on the years they never saw, and an approved change is applied by the worker before the next night, on the S&P 400 or 600 as a stored setting of that index alone, while a change to an S&P 500 rule waits on the operator's ruling of how it reaches a page its family's code draws. Teal boxes serve pages: each index's Loop page draws its own proposals and computes nothing. Orange boxes are the operator. Nothing crosses from one column to another: a proposal tested on one index says nothing of another's, and an approval changes its own index's rule alone.

14. The nightly run, in order

What the night is built from

Each night is built from a clean copy of the main checkout's own commit, read with no fetch, and never from its working tree: the commit is exported whole into a folder of its own under the data root, one a commit, built once and run by every try of the night, the rest of one and the drain it starts, so no night mixes two versions of the code. A checkout off main, or holding a commit the remote's main does not have, is refused before any worker exists, with the reason written where tonight's page and the Run page read it; a checkout behind the remote's main runs and says so; an uncommitted or untracked file is never built and costs no night. The store and the data folder are the checkout's by absolute path, the secrets file is read from the checkout by path and never copied into the build, and the night records the commit it ran on its run log, which the Run page shows (see: Each night is built from a clean copy of the main checkout's own commit and never from its working tree, and refuses only a checkout off main or ahead of the remote's main).

Before the first nightly run, once

A single day of bars computes nothing: no averages, no swings, no bands, no ladder and no list. So the first run backfills one year of daily bars for every current index member before any of the steps below, either one request per ticker or one bulk request per past session. It is a few hundred requests in one afternoon and it never repeats for a name that already has its year. One year is what the bar store keeps, and the history the operator pulls before it is read by no step below (see: The bar store holds one year for every night's work, and the history pulled beside it is read by measurements alone). The same backfill runs for a single name on the first night the membership feed carries its join, which is before the join takes effect, so the name joins with its year whole.

Every night after that

  1. Load index membership and record any joins and leaves.
  2. Backfill one year for any member with no stored history, which on the first run is every name and afterwards is only a new joiner.
  3. Fetch the day's bulk bar file, one request, and store the bars for every name that has not left the index by the session, a name announced to join included, first fetching in bulk, one request each, any session the store is missing since the last night that ran (see: A session the night finds missing is fetched in bulk before tonight's) (see: An announced index change takes effect on its effective date, and a joining name is stored from the announcement). Then ask for the index's, the VIX's, the eleven sector funds' and the four index and credit funds' daily series over the days before the session that section 17 states, one request a series, and store each session no night has stored apart from the bars, a fund's held session written again where the answer restates its close, a series the provider does not serve storing nothing and stopping nothing (see: The night asks for the market series' daily closes once a series, and keeps them apart from the members' bars).
  4. Check splits and dividends, and refetch the full year for any name affected.
  5. Fetch the index's dated events for the horizon, one request, and store what the provider files (see: A calendar event is fetched once for the whole index, and the calendar holds provider events only), and each member's declared ex-dividend dates over the 21 sessions after the night, one request a session (see: The night asks the dividend calendar for each of the next 21 sessions, one request a session).
  6. Compute the indicators for every name.
  7. Mark the swings for every name.
  8. Build the volume profile for every name.
  9. Build the levels for every name.
  10. Classify the trend state and build the ladder for every name, writing a row whether or not it carries a tranche (see: A ladder row is written for every index member every night) (see: The trend classifier returns its label to the ladder builder).
  11. Annotate the largest moves for every name.
  12. Compute the swing readings for every member and the night's breadth: each return over 63 and over 126 sessions with its place among the members' returns, the highest high of the last 20 sessions and the pullback from it in typical days' moves, the volume while it came down, the tightness of the range, and the share of the members closing above their own 200-day average, a member read over nothing keeping its row with the reason.
  13. Read the reported quarters of every member, from the quarters fetched on the nights before this one: the trajectory, sales and the operating margin against a year earlier over the two newest quarters; the record against the analysts' estimates; earnings quality, operating cash flow against net income over four quarters; and the valuation position, tonight's multiple in the range of the quarters' own; and the state they give, improving, steady, deteriorating, not enough quarters or no fundamentals yet, read from the trajectory alone, a member holding none written as any other (see: Four readings of a member's reported quarters are worked out every night by rules the measured split settled, and its state is read from sales and operating margin alone). Then store every member's readings of the three indices and the switches beside them, each through the one function the sweeps read it with (see: The 400 and 600 rules start provisional with liquidity floors and a profit gate before any testing).
  14. Evaluate the list reasons for every name.
  15. Evaluate every member through the swing filter: the market gate on the night's breadth, the trend and strength gate, the pullback, the trigger where it first fired within the arrival window, the trade read from the ladder's first tranche, from the swing trade at the nearest bands and from section 10's plan for it, and the exclusions, storing every answer with the values that decided it and ranking the names passing, which are the pullback family's, the estimates of each member a registered rule reading them passes on everything else asked for once a member before any verdict is written (see: The night asks for the estimates of each member a rule reading them passes on everything else, once a member a night), and record the night's session as listed by the swing filter once the rows are stored (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it); then evaluate every member under each other setup family, on the market check the filter stored, storing every answer with the values that decided it (see: The market check closes every swing family's list together, and the sector heavyweights read none); then draw the page's list from what each setup family passed, the families in the page's order and each family's names in its own, at most five a family, a stock once and none whose trade from any family of any index is still open, and record the session as one the families drew (see: Tonight's page is drawn from setup families, each a rule of its own listing at most five a night) (see: A stock holds one trade across every swing family, and one qualifying under two is listed once under the first in the page's order); then end each registered family rule's earlier trades whose closes reached their stop, their target or their cap, write the benchmark of each whose cap's sessions have passed, and list tonight's for each rule, at most five, none it holds a trade on still open (see: A registered family rule is evaluated every night at its own settings and keeps its own list, its trades stored with their benchmark when they end); then carry each sector heavyweight held to tonight's close, in the page's book and in each registered rule's own, sell one whose stock left the index at its last close as a member and, where the setting reads it, one closing under its 200-day average, and on the first night of a month read each sector's largest companies by their values as they stood, their returns against the sector's and their betas, sell each holding the rule would no longer buy and buy each leader it does not hold, reading no market check and waiting for a night the store holds the closes a rebalance reads (see: The sector heavyweights hold the largest companies leading their sectors, rotated on the first session of each month whose stored year holds the closes their readings need) (see: Each registered sector heavyweights rule keeps a book of its own beside the page's, its holdings scored in percent against their size cut); then apply each change the operator approved on the Loop page that no apply has answered, an S&P 400 or 600 swing family's written as the setting the family reads from tonight on that index alone and every other refused with why, a failure named on the step's row while the families read the settings as they stood (see: An approved change is applied before the next night from the night's own build, on the index it was approved on alone); then read the fundamentals-first family on the S&P 500 alone, over the pullback's base listings with each member's readings as the ledger's catalogue reads them tonight, holding back a stock the S&P 500's own families listed tonight (see: The fundamentals-first family buys an improving business in an uptrend at the pullback's buy point); then read the S&P 400's and 600's provisional rules by the sweep's own code over each index's own members, the fundamentals-first family's among them, its swing lists closed together on its own breadth, storing every member's answer, drawing each index's list with none whose trade on any index's list is still open, ending and keeping its trades, and carrying and rebalancing its sector heavyweights, and read each rule registered on an index at its own settings the same way, a family's live rule drawing its list in the provisional rule's place, each swing rule keeping its own list and trades and each heavyweights rule its own book (see: The 400's and 600's provisional picks are computed on the night by the sweep's own code into tables of their own) (see: Each index's market check closes its own swing lists together on its own breadth) (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's swing families is registered as the family on its index and evaluated by their step alone) (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's sector heavyweights keeps a book of its own in either design, read by the index families' step); then write a card for each stock every index's families listed and each stock its books bought, the checklist's lines read from the rows the step stored with the rule's record and the card's values and what could hit the trade, a failure in an index's cards named on its own row while the night goes on (see: A pick's card advises on the trade and removes no pick, and code computes every figure on it); then write every standing rule's night on each index, live or variant, its listed count, its funnel and its empty stretch against its mark, the swing filter variants' own picks walked and kept, and the members forming a breakout under each breakout rule, a failure in an index's part named on the stage's row while the night goes on (see: A variant's picks are shown on its card when chosen and its results only under its tests) (see: The forming list advises and never lists a stock); then read each live rule's periods that have closed with every unit in them settled against the reference of the newest tester run on its index, writing each once and flagging a rule two counted periods running under its floor, a failure named on the step's row while the night goes on (see: The live alarm flags a rule whose edge stood under its reference's fifth percentile two periods running); then follow each trade the operator took over the stored closes under its rule's own management and write the operator's record, a failure named on the follower's own row (see: A taken trade's fill is the next session's open once its bar is stored, and the plan's buy marked provisional until then).
  16. Append tonight's setups to the ledger on every index the night read: every member-session a family's loose gates pass, the pullback's, the breakout's and the drift's, with the live rule's own pass and the night's pick beside it, its plan as prices, its readings as they stood and its path still open, and one row a family an index with the members the gates were read over; and close the windows of the setups stored before whose paths ended on tonight's close or whose benchmark, the same plan on every member of their session, has every member's path ended, a failure in an index's part named on the step's row while the step goes on (see: A setup is every member-session a family's loose gates pass, and its readings are defined once and read as they stood).
  17. Count the ordinary nights stored under the open filter version and, once they reach sixty, propose for each gate the one setting that brings its median count inside its band, writing one proposal for the version and stating the crossed trigger on the night's run log; nothing proposed is applied until the operator's command accepts it.
  18. Write the facts file for every name.
  19. Fill forward returns for past listings that matured today, and recompute the universe base rate, and score every swing filter row on each plan it carries (see: A swing filter row carries both swing plans, each scored from the night's close, and a candidate's setups are scored on the plan its own trade gate reads).
  20. Count today's articles per name from one dated news query, paged until the day is covered and every page counted, fanned out to names in code rather than asked for per name. The page count follows the day's news volume and not the size of the universe (see: News is one dated query, paged to cover the day, and attributed to names locally).
  21. Replay tonight's name-nights under every open version of each ladder rule from the stored bars, and store the plan each version produced, flagging as in sample any score for a session on or before the New York date its version's window opened on so it counts toward no record (see: A version's score counts only for a session after the New York date its window opened on). This makes no request: the bars are already stored, so a version costs the ladder arithmetic run again and, for a version of the merge distance, the level arithmetic as well. A live rule whose parameters or code have moved while a window measuring it is open stops the night at this step and names the rule (see: Adding a candidate later restarts the clock).
  22. Close the arithmetic and record its counts: names computed, names on the list, reasons fired, stale names, duration.
  23. Ask the provider for the reported quarters of the members due, one request for a member's fundamentals and one for three years of its closes where the answer is stored: every member once at the start, at most 260 a night; a member on the first night after it reports; a member whose new quarter the answer does not yet carry on each of the five nights after and weekly after that; and a member joining the index on its first night; bounded by its own limit and by the day's allowance and never by the night's deadline (see: A member's reported quarters are fetched on the night after it reports, and asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that until the quarter is posted).
  24. Read the archive's daily index for each weekday since the refresh last read one, through the night's own session where the archive has posted it, and ask the archive for the facts of each member whose filer filed a quarterly or annual report, an amendment to one, or a results announcement whose own page carries item 2.02, storing each fact not yet stored as first filed; a day the archive posted no index for before the session's own is read as none and the session's own, not yet posted, is read on a later night; bounded by its own limit and never by the night's deadline, a refusal leaving the facts as they were and its days for the next night; then read the business readings of tonight's setups again for the members refreshed (see: The night refreshes the facts of the members that filed since its last read of the archive's daily index, after the close under its own limit).
  25. Run the overnight queue on the local model, writing the sections in the local lane that rest on no document for every name in the indices the night reads whose research is missing or stale, the names on tonight's list first in the order it is drawn in, then the S&P 400's and the S&P 600's lists each in its page's order (see: The overnight queue drafts the three indices' lists before every other member, the S&P 500's first), then the names close to a buy point in the order that list is drawn in, then every other name, the S&P 500's first (see: A member that missed exactly one gate and no exclusion is drawn close to a buy point nearest first, and recommends nothing) (see: The key under each figure is dated by the night whose figures it explains, written for every name each night, and drawn only beside that night's figures), until the configured time limit rather than until a count of names is reached (see: The overnight queue is bounded by time, not by a count of names), a limit of its own rather than the night's deadline (see: The overnight queue is bounded by its own limit rather than the night's deadline, and starts no pass once the limit has passed). It holds the machine awake while it works and reports whether it ran (see: The overnight run holds the machine awake and reports whether it ran). This makes no paid call and no request, and no part of the arithmetic above depends on it (see: The overnight queue writes the local lane's sections that rest on no document for every name, and the paid model is for names you get serious about).
  26. Ask for six reports taken in turn across the S&P 500's, 400's and 600's pages, one name at a time in that order and each page's own order across its families, a sector heavyweight on the night it is bought and never on a night it is carried, a page with no name left passing its turn, one request a name marked as asked by the night unless that name has one outstanding or being written and none on a night no page lists a stock, and start the drain as a press does, whose passes are its own runs at the off-peak rate with their calls and their requests on their own rows (see: The six reports a night are taken in turn across the three indices, one at a time in the page's order).
  27. Start the news labeller as the drain is started, a process of its own that labels the stored admitted articles of the names on tonight's list, newest first and at most twenty a name over the thirty days before the night, through the news job's paid model one article at a time, with every call and every dollar on the labeller's own run and never the night's, bounded by its own time and month limits, and starting none on a night run again for an earlier session (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own).
  28. Start the store's copy as the labeller is started, a process of its own that waits until the night, the drain it started and the labeller have finished, holding the drain's lock while it copies the store through SQLite's own backup into the copies' folder, opens and reads the copy against the store, keeps the newest three after opening and reading each, and writes a row of its own as it starts and one as it ends and nothing else; a night run again for an earlier session starts one that waits for no labeller (see: The store is copied once the night and every process it started have finished and the newest three copies are kept after each is opened and read, and the copy writes a row as it starts and one as it ends).

A step before the close that fails, or that passes the night's deadline, stops the try it is in, and the night writes beside the stop the instant its next try starts. Fifteen minutes later it runs again from that step, under a run id carrying the first try's with -try- and its number and under a deadline of its own, up to three more times. The steps before it are not run again, since every stage reads and writes by the session. A night refused before its first step, one whose day's allowance is spent, and one whose day the exchange calendar cannot place is not tried again, and neither is a step after the close. A night left unfinished is run to its end by the press on tonight's page and the Run page, or by the nightly command run with --resume, from the first step its tries have not finished, as one more try; and a night takes a lock file under the data root before its first step, so a second night, a run of the rest of one among them, is refused while one runs (see: A night that stops before its close is tried again from the step that stopped, three more times fifteen minutes apart, each try under a deadline of its own) (see: A night left unfinished is run to its end from the step it stopped at by a press or a command, and one night runs at a time under a lock file).

The computations from the indicators to the facts file were one step until 4.0, reading "For every name: indicators, swings, volume profile, levels, trend state, ladder, moves, list reasons, facts file". They are one step each because the night runs them stage by stage over the whole universe rather than name by name, which is what the components do, and because the order inside them is load bearing: the levels cannot be built before the swings and the ladder cannot be built before the levels. Written as one step the order was invisible and so was the fact that three of the stages, having shipped in phase 3, were not run by any night at all. That is the case for a claim per stage rather than one claim over all of them, and it is contradiction F's argument applied to a list instead of a row. The trend state and the ladder are one stage rather than two, because the classifier writes nothing and hands its label to the builder that writes the row it sits on.

The arithmetic, being steps 1 to 22, calls no model and makes no per-name network request. Step 23 is carved out of the second of those by name and calls no model: it asks the provider for one member's quarters at a time on the nights after the member reports, which the reporting calendar sets rather than the index, and it is bounded by its own limit and by the day's allowance (see: A member's reported quarters are fetched on the night after it reports, and asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that until the quarter is posted). Step 24 is carved out of the second by name and calls no model: it reads the archive's daily index, one request a day since it last read one, and asks the archive for the facts of the members whose filer filed, free and from the SEC rather than the provider, which the filings calendar sets rather than the index, and it is bounded by its own limit (see: The night refreshes the facts of the members that filed since its last read of the archive's daily index, after the close under its own limit). Step 25 is carved out of the first by name and calls the local model only (see: The night's zero-model-call rule bounds the arithmetic, and the overnight queue is carved out of it by name). The night's own requests, after the queue, call no model and make no request: the night writes a row a name and starts one process, and the passes they lead to are the drain's own runs, at most six paid passes a night taken in turn across the three indices' pages, a number the indices' sizes do not move (see: The six reports a night are taken in turn across the three indices, one at a time in the page's order). A feed that answers in pages counts every page it fetched, so a page count that grows with the index is a per-name call whatever the request count says (see: A feed that pages counts every page, and a page count that grows with the index is a per-name call). The run is idempotent in what it records about the market: running it twice on one night produces the same bars, the same membership spans and the same computed values, and where a second run computes different values than the first, because a refetch moved the prices between them, the second run's are what the store holds, the facts file included (see: A re-run replaces a night's facts file where the store now computes a different one). It does not produce a byte-identical store, and is not meant to. Each row carries the instant it was observed, and the run log gains a row per stage per run, so the store also records that the night ran twice. That is the evidence the run page reads, and a run that left no trace of having repeated would be the thing to fix rather than the thing to claim. The schedule is a UTC instant after the provider posts the day's bulk file, moved later only by a night that finds the file not yet posted, and registered with whatever scheduler the machine has, because scheduling lives outside the application and a schedule written in local time moves twice a year with nothing to announce it (see: Queued work runs off-peak, and every schedule is written in UTC) (see: The night runs at a fixed UTC instant, moved only when a night finds the day's file not yet posted) (see: Nothing is written against one operating system).

15. The screens

This section is the specification for what the operator looks at. It is here rather than in a document of its own because a mockup file and a built page are two answers to one question, and the day they disagree nothing says which is the specification.

15.1 What these screens are for

A full report for one name is a long document. It is read in the evening by one person deciding which of a handful of names is worth the next half hour, and the sections that answer that question sit among sections that answer different ones. Every screen below replaces reading with looking. None of them replaces the prose: the researched sections are kept in full, one disclosure down, because the screen answers which name and the prose answers why. There are seven: tonight at 15.7, the universe at 15.8, a name at 15.9, the run at 15.10, the queue at 15.15, the watch list at 15.16 and the past picks at 15.17. The last three are numbered after the sections that follow the other four rather than among them, because the numbers here are navigation and the record already cites 15.11 to 15.14.

15.2 The rule that governs every screen

Reads and renders, nothing else. No screen computes a level, calls a model, or makes a network request. Every number on every screen is already in the facts file, the ladder, the listings, the research store or the run log, but for two a pick's card works out where it is drawn, each by one function in the core: its plan in the operator's money, from the account they keep in a file no store row may hold, and its sixth line, from their taken trades. A screen that wants any other number the store does not carry is not a screen change; it is a change to a compute component, and it goes through a checkpoint like anything else.

The reason is that a rendering layer which computes is a second implementation of the same arithmetic, and two implementations of one rule disagree eventually; the card's two have one implementation each, and an export draws neither. It also means a screen can be rebuilt or restyled at any time without a chance of moving any other number. (see: A screen reads and renders, and computes only the plan in the operator's money and a pick's open trades in its sector)

A figure is drawn at the places it is read at: a price, a ratio and an amount per share to two places, an amount of money and a count of shares in its scale, a fraction as a percentage to one place and a multiple to one. The element it is drawn in carries the stored value whole, and that is what the checks read, so rounding a figure to be read never makes a value the store does not hold. Prose a model wrote is drawn as the claim checker accepted it. (see: A figure is drawn at the places it is read at, and its element carries the stored value whole)

A screen is read at the width of the screen it is read on. The column every screen is drawn in is that width, up to a ceiling which is the widest picture a screen draws with the card's own padding and the page's gutter around it, so a wide screen is filled by the page rather than by the space beside it and a narrow one is filled rather than shown a page laid out for a wide one. A table cannot be narrowed past its columns, so every table a screen draws is read in a box of its own that scrolls sideways rather than moving the page. A picture is narrowed instead: the chart and the volume profile beside it are drawn at a size of their own, which is what the ceiling holds, and below it the pair is scaled down together so that a price is at one height in both at every width. (see: A screen is read at the width of the screen it is read on)

15.3 One document, no pages

One file, and the reader never loads a second one. Views are hash routes resolved in the browser: #/, #/night/<date>, #/watch, #/universe, #/ledger, #/loop, #/picks, #/researched, #/name/<ticker>, #/name/<ticker>/<date>, #/run/<date>. Back and forward work because the router listens for the hash changing and pushes no state the browser did not ask for. A route is a link, and the selected name is part of the route, so what is on screen can be sent to another machine and be the same thing.

No framework, no build step, no package manager. The nightly run already writes one store and the read API already serves it; adding a front-end toolchain would put a second source of formatted numbers into a project whose whole argument is that there is one. (see: One application, not a file per report)

15.4 The two surfaces

SurfaceWhat it isBuilt how
The appthe single page, with routing, filters and selectionthe server writes the shell and the marks; the browser routes
The exported reportone name, as a flat file to hand to someonethe same marks, the same data, rendered without the router and with every disclosure open

The export is the surface that constrains the marks. It has no scripting and no shared state, so every mark has to be a picture that renders from values alone. That is why marks are server-rendered SVG rather than drawn by a charting library in the browser: one source of numbers, two documents. (see: A single report can still be exported as a self-contained file)

15.5 The mark vocabulary

Twenty marks. They are defined once and every screen draws from this list. Nothing on any screen is a one-off drawing, for the same reason the palette is one set of variables: parity by construction rather than by remembering. Each mark takes stored values and returns an SVG string, so no script is needed to render any of them and the export carries the same pictures as the app. (see: Marks are defined once and every screen draws from that list)

MarkWhat it is, and what it earnsUsed by
Level chartDaily candles with the level bands shaded behind them, the moving averages drawn, and a volume pane beneath on a shared time axis. The bands are the point: a table of levels is a list of numbers, and the same levels drawn behind the price show at a glance which ones the price has actually respected.Name
Volume profileShares traded in each price band, drawn horizontally against the same price axis as the chart beside it. It is what lets the report say that a support band holds a fifth of the period's volume in a twentieth of its price range, and that almost nothing traded above the current price. Neither statement is available from a candle chart.Name
Plan columnOne vertical price axis with the current price marked in the middle of it. Everything above the marker is a sale, everything below is a purchase, stops are horizontal rules, and the invalidation is the lowest one. This is the mark the whole plan section rests on, and it is drawn as one column rather than two facing sides because a reader should not have to learn a convention before reading it. (see: The plan figure is one vertical price column with the current price marked in it)Name, Tonight
Momentum panelThe momentum readings beneath the chart on two small axes. Relative strength has one to itself with its neutral rule at 50 and its edges at 70 and 30 drawn and named. The convergence line and its signal line share the other with the gap between them drawn as bars about its zero rule, so a crossing is drawn where it happens. Each axis is headed by what it reads and where each reading stood at the last session drawn and what it means in words. A number like 53 means nothing without the band it sits in. The rules are reading conventions this panel draws and no component applies (see: The momentum panel is context a reader weighs, and nothing computes with it).Name
Distance rowA name's close between its nearest support and its nearest resistance, sized for a table cell, with the distances in typical days. The mark that turns a column of numbers into a shape, so a scan down five hundred rows shows which names are near an edge without reading any of them.Universe, Tonight
Reason trackPer reason, out of one denominator: setups resolved as a win, resolved as a loss, and unresolved. The third state is drawn as a dashed outline and never as a third colour, because unresolved is not a smaller amount of losing and must not read as one.Run, Tonight
Listing stripOne column per session over the last sixty, marked on the evenings a name was on the list and by which side of the chart the reason came from. A name that keeps returning to its levels is visible without a number.Name, Universe
Trade lineOne trade the live list recommended, drawn from its stop at the left as a green tick to its target at the right as an orange tick. The buy is a short neutral tick between them and the dot is the price: hollow while the trade is open and filled where it finished, with a price beyond either end sitting at that end. It is placed by the prices' ratios to the buy, so a split since the listing moves none of it. The mark that turns a row of prices into where a trade stands, so a column of trades shows which are near their stop or their target without reading a price (see: Every trade the live list recommended is shown, and their share waits for the minimum the reason records wait for).Past picks, Name
Year lineA name's stored closes as one line with its nearest support and its nearest resistance drawn across it in their own hues and named with their prices. It is drawn beside a ticker in a peers table and in the universe table while the pointer is over it or it has the focus, so a name's year is read without leaving the page (see: Peers are shown by price alone, ten at most with the name's industry first and then the members whose daily moves followed it most closely).Name, Universe
Night statusA night's state drawn as a ring beside its headline. A tick in blue is a night that finished and a clock in blue one still running; a clock in violet is a night not run yet or waiting to try again and a mark in red is a failure. Beneath it the night's steps lie along a time bar in their six groups, a group not reached drawn as a dashed outline and the group a stopped night stopped in outlined in red (see: Status is drawn in blues with violet for a wait and red for a failure alone).Run
Market gaugeThe share of the members above their 200-day average on a half circle with the market gate's floor marked across it and the share in figures at its centre. The word above it names the market by the rule section 17 states.Run
Breadth lineThat share over the sessions before the night that the store holds averages for, with the market gate's floor dashed across it and the newest session marked. A line over fewer sessions than it draws says how many it holds.Run
Funnel barsOne bar for the whole index and one for the members through each of the swing filter's checks in turn, each as long as its count against the index and named in words with its count beside it.Run
Trades ringThe trades decided at the target or the stop as an arc around a ring against the minimum a share waits on. The ring's track is a dashed outline until the minimum is met.Run
Freshness barsOne bar for each evening of the list with the names new that evening stacked on those the evening before also listed.Run
Clock linesThe shape clock as a bar of the ordinary nights against those its calibration waits on with each check's typical pass count as a dot on its range, the range dashed and holding no dot until measured. The edge clock as a line from today to its two checkpoints, the stretch run drawn solid.Run
Overlap ringsTwo overlapping rings for the live list and one version holding as three counts the names only the live list picked and those both picked and those only the version picked.Run
Checkpoint scaleOne row per version on a scale from nought to a hundred. Before the version's first look the row is a locked dashed outline. From it the share of its trades that reached the target is a dot, the break-even they needed a rule and what no skill scored a smaller dot with how far luck alone could move it drawn as a band from there.Run
Research barsThe month's spend as a bar against the month cap and one bar for each of the last seven nights as tall as the reports the paid model wrote that night.Run
ChecklistEach item of the Run page's checklist beside a ring holding a tick in blue where it held and a cross in red where it failed with its reason. An item the night stored nothing to read from is a dashed ring.Run

Every mark degrades by saying what it has rather than by drawing through nothing. A chart over fewer than the bars a mark needs returns a sentence stating the bar count. A profile over a window with a gap says so on its axis. A sparse series is never allowed to look like a quiet one.

15.6 Colour

The document you are reading and the application share one palette, in light and dark, with both designed rather than one inverted from the other. The theme is a stamp on the root element, remembered between visits, with the machine's own preference as the default.

Support and resistance own two hues, and nothing else uses them

Green means a level below the price, orange means a level above it, on every screen and in every mark. Nothing else is allowed those two hues, and in particular a day's price change is not: a green day and a support band would then be the same colour meaning two things, and a reader cannot hold that. Direction of the day is carried by the sign on the number and by which side of a zero rule a bar sits on. (see: Support and resistance own two hues and nothing else uses them)

Hue is never the only channel

Every band carries its role in words as well as its colour. Every reason carries its name. A reader who cannot separate the two hues loses nothing, which is a property to hold rather than to test for once: the two hues in the palette measure far enough apart under the commonest form of colour blindness to be told apart, and the words are there whether they do or not.

Magnitude is one ramp, never a rainbow

Where a mark needs to show more or less, it uses four steps of a single hue, stepped for the surface it sits on and validated against it. More is darker in light and lighter in dark. A second hue is never introduced to tell two bars apart: if a chart needs two hues to be readable it is the wrong chart.

Not yet measured is a dashed outline

Anywhere a figure has not earned a number yet, the space is drawn as a dashed outline carrying its count against its minimum, and never as a pale version of a value. The record column in 15.11 is in that state for the first year, and a pale number would read as a small one. (see: Not yet measured is drawn as a dashed outline, never as a pale value) (see: The record column stays empty until it has earned a number)

Status is drawn in blues, a wait in violet and a failure in red

The Run page states how a night went and pictures its counts. A night that finished or is running, and every picture of a count there, is drawn in two steps of one blue; a night not run yet, which is waiting, in violet; and a night that stopped, was left unfinished or never ran in red, which means a failure and nothing else, never a fall in price. None of the three is a level's hue, and each carries its state in words beside it. (see: Status is drawn in blues with violet for a wait and red for a failure alone)

Every region is a card

Each region is a card on one paper palette. A region computed from the nightly store is ruled in slate and stamped with the night its figures are from, and a section written by research or taken from a filing is ruled in plum-grey with the day it was written or filed in a column at its left. Every picture carries a key that says how to read it and closes on what to take from it. The stylesheet the app and the exported report share opens with the rule each colour token is held to: the two hues for a level below and above the price, the dashed outline's ink for not yet measured and for nothing else, slate for what was computed tonight, plum-grey for what was written or filed, and four steps of one neutral for more or less. (see: Every region is a card that states where its figures came from and how to read them)

15.7 Tonight

Answers: which names the swing filter passed tonight, each at a buy point its own chart and plan make for a swing trade of a few weeks, and how busy the evening was.

Route: #/, resolving to the newest night, and #/night/<date> for an earlier one. On a store the swing filter has listed, the page opens from the first night it listed: an earlier date draws one line saying the record starts on that night, with a link opening it (see: The dated screens open from the swing filter's first night, and no evening before it is drawn). A calendar beside the night drawn opens another: its arrows open the night before and the night after among those the page draws, and its month grid, newest month first, underlines each day holding one of them and opens it on a click, marks the night drawn, and draws every other day as no link.

Reads: the listings, the rule that listed the night, the gate results, the fundamental readings, ladders, levels and facts for that night, the settings of the filter version each gate result was stored under and a member's gate results on the sessions before the night for the second list, the run log for the header, and series state for the rows whose prices may not reflect a dividend or split, which this list did not name until 7.0, and from 14.3 the sector heavyweights' holdings, their last rebalance's reading and each holding's close and 200-day average for their card.

From 15.1 the page reads the index chosen under Universe, and what this section describes is the S&P 500's. The S&P 400's or 600's draws, under the heading "Tonight: S&P 400" or "Tonight: S&P 600", the line its setups open on with the index's own breadth against the floor and how many of its members a setup passed, one card a swing family in the page's order and the index's sector heavyweights' card, each provisional and read from the rows the index families stored for the night: the index's night, every member's answer, its list, its trades and its book (see: The 400's and 600's provisional picks are computed on the night by the sweep's own code into tables of their own). A card's rule is written by code from the settings its index's rule holds and never by hand, so a setting changed changes its words: the S&P 500's from the settings its live rules run at, and the S&P 400's and 600's from the settings their night stored, stating each way they differ from the S&P 500's, the minimum price, the dollar volume floor, the profit check and the cost taken off each trade. Its status line reads "Provisional: not yet frozen" until the rule's freeze and "Live rule since" the day it registered after. The drift's card on the S&P 400 and 600 carries its line of evidence (see: The 400's and 600's earnings drift lists from the first night with the evidence against it on its card), and the heavyweights' card names its design and the sector comparison its index reads (see: The 400 and 600 each sweep two heavyweight designs and keep the stronger after costs), and draws each holding's lead over its sector's members' mean at the rebalance that bought it, a holding bought before its book stored one saying so (see: An S&P 400 or 600 heavyweights holding keeps the lead it was bought on). A note under a card naming a stock held back for a trade still open names the index whose list holds that trade, since one trade a stock holds across every card of every index (see: A stock holds one trade across every swing family, and one qualifying under two is listed once under the first in the page's order). On a night whose S&P 400 or 600 part failed, that index's page opens on "Not computed tonight" in place of its market line, every card of it says the same and lists nothing, and its Run page names the failure (see: A failure in the S&P 400's or 600's part of the night is caught and named, and the S&P 500's night is built regardless).

From 15.4 a family's card on any index, the sector heavyweights' among them, carries beneath its status line the words "Its sweep found no setting that passed the floors" where the newest sweep answer recorded before the night's end for each of the family's designs on that index says none passed and no freeze of the family on that index was registered after it, and nothing where none is recorded; the card lists its picks whatever the line says (see: A sweep passes where a setting it read meets the floors, and a card says none passed only where every design's newest answer does) (see: No family on any index is set aside or hidden by a test result without the operator's word).

From 15.5 a swing family frozen on the S&P 400 or 600 is drawn by its live rule from the night its freeze registered on: its status line reads "Live rule since" the day it registered with the variants scored beside it, its rule is the sentence the live rule's registration carries, written by code from its settings, and its list is the one the night read by that rule, so its sweep's line goes from that night and not before (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's swing families is registered as the family on its index and evaluated by their step alone). The sector heavyweights frozen on either index are drawn the same way from their live rule's own book: its holdings, its last rebalance and what that bought and sold, its look-back and its next rebalance read at the rule's own settings, live since the day it registered with its variants kept in books of their own, a design (b) rule's card saying in its keys and its rows that it reads no lead over a sector, and the index's own book drawn on any night the live rule's was not kept (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's sector heavyweights keeps a book of its own in either design, read by the index families' step) (see: An S&P 400 or 600 heavyweights holding keeps the lead it was bought on).

RegionWhat is in it
Night headernames in the index, names the swing filter listed, names that fired, the night's breadth with the share above the 50-day average beside it as context, reports carrying fresh prose against reused, spend, run duration, and the harness verdict. The count the swing filter listed is the headline and the fired count stands beside it as context, because it is the one number the twenty drawn rows cannot tell you; before the switch the fired count was the headline
The night's statea notice at the top naming the night's state as the Run page's headline names it; each try so far with the step it stopped at and its reason while the night waits to try again or is left unfinished; a press running the rest of a night left unfinished; a one-line note where the night finished; a refusal before its first step with its reason (see: A night's state is read off its own run log rows and its tries, and the pages that state it read that one state) (see: A night left unfinished is run to its end from the step it stopped at by a press or a command, and one night runs at a time under a lock file) (see: Each night is built from a clean copy of the main checkout's own commit and never from its working tree, and refuses only a checkout off main or ahead of the remote's main)
Watch listone line above the list saying how many names the operator watches, with a link to the watch list page (section 15.16)
The live alarm's linefrom 17.9 on the newest night above an index's page a line for each family whose live rule the alarm flags on the index naming its newest period and linking the Loop page (see: The live alarm flags a rule whose edge stood under its reference's fifth percentile two periods running)
The listone row per name on the list, ordered by the state its reported quarters give it and within a state by the swing filter's reward to risk then strength then band strength, the state-first order from the first night whose readings are stored and a night before it in the filter's own order, at most twenty drawn, each numbered by its place in that order, a line above them stating how many are drawn of how many are listed, and a line naming the rule that listed the evening. Each row: name, close, day change, trend state in a word, the state its reported quarters give it beside the trend, what the numbers say while the state is under the pointer or holds focus, the distance row mark, the reward to risk or the plan's reason for none, the gates with the values that decided them, the reasons as context, and beside the name a line saying so where its prices may not reflect a dividend or split, and the positive and negative stories of the thirty days before the night as the name page's bar counts them; the stories are counted on the first list alone (see: The news labels alone name the model that wrote them); each column heading saying what its column holds while the pointer is over it (see: Every figure carries a plain-language key)
Still openbeneath the list on an evening the swing filter listed: one row per stock that passed every gate on the night with nothing excluding it but an open trade while a trade the live list recommended for it on an earlier night is still open on this one, the night that trade was listed on, the trade line, where the price stands against that trade's stop and target, and whether the trade ended at this night's own close and frees the stock from the next night; before the rule reaches the filter the stock stands on the list as well and is marked as listed again while that trade is open; once the rule reaches the filter the stock is excluded there and drawn here alone; a line where there is none; and a key saying it is not a new trade
A family's cardon a night the setup families drew the page's list, in place of the list and of Still open: one card a family in the page's order, the family's rule in a sentence, the day its rule went live or the words saying it is provisional, and how many it lists tonight with how many variants are scored beside it. Each row: its place down the page, the stock with a label for each other family it qualified under, the state its reported quarters give it, the buy and the stop and the target, where the buy sits between the stop and the target, the reward to risk, why it is listed tonight in the figures its family stored, and the positive and negative stories of the thirty days before. Beneath the rows: a note for each stock it passed that a trade still open holds back, a note for each stock the page lists under an earlier family, and a note counting the stocks past its five; a line saying why where it lists none; and a key saying how to read it (see: Tonight's page is drawn from setup families, each a rule of its own listing at most five a night) (see: A stock holds one trade across every swing family, and one qualifying under two is listed once under the first in the page's order) (see: A family lists on provisional settings until its freeze, and nothing before the freeze counts toward a checkpoint)
A family's card's rulefrom 17.2, on every index's cards: a selector beside the card's state line listing the live rule or the provisional rule first and then each registered variant by the number of its first registration with the register's words; the choice kept in the link under the family's own key by a handler merging the key into the query the link holds; the live rule drawn where the link names none or names a rule that does not stand; a variant chosen redraws the card from that rule's rows under the band saying it is scored in the background and not the live rule and its picks are not tonight's list; its words written by code from its parameters with the clauses the live rule's words lack marked; its own picks with their plans in place of the live rule's rows; the chosen rule's funnel with each gate and how many members passed it and every gate before, or that the night did not evaluate the rule; the stretch line saying how many nights the rule has listed nothing for against the mark its own past empty nights set and flagged past it, or how far the floors are from being met while no mark is drawn; under a breakout card the breakouts forming with the count forming and the rows drawn and the nearest misses first; each forming member with the price it would have to close above and the volume the rule would need against tonight's; its ranges' ratio and the gates it still fails and its next report where one falls within the window; a line where the market check closed the rule's list; the closing line that the rule reads its other gates that night as on any other and lists five at most; on the S&P 400 or 600 before a freeze the provisional rule alone with the line that no variant is registered before its freeze (see: A variant's picks are shown on its card when chosen and its results only under its tests) (see: The forming list advises and never lists a stock) (see: A card's stretch line counts its mark over past empty nights and draws none under thirty completed stretches)
The fundamentals-first family's cardfrom 17.8 on every index after the index's own families' cards and numbered among them: the family's rule in words from the setting its night stored; its picks with their plans and why each passed; where it lists none how many members stopped at each check of the rule; and on the S&P 500 drawn from the rows the S&P 400's and 600's step writes there and saying so (see: The fundamentals-first family buys an improving business in an uptrend at the pullback's buy point)
The market lineabove the cards on a night the setup families drew the page's list: whether the market check left the lists open with the breadth and its floor, the buy points the page lists and how many setups list one, the stocks close to a buy point; and the trades still open linking to Past picks (see: The market check closes every swing family's list together, and the sector heavyweights read none)
The sector heavyweights' cardafter the setup families' cards on a night they drew the page's list, whatever the market check read: the family's rule in a sentence and the day its live rule registered with the variants kept beside it or the words saying it is provisional where no freeze registered it; one row a holding at the night's close, the sectors in order, each with its sector, the session it was bought on, its lead over its sector at the rebalance that last read it, its close against its 200-day average, and held while leading in place of a stop and a target; the stocks the last rebalance bought; each holding sold at it or since, with the session and why; the next rebalance's date; and a line saying why where it holds none (see: The sector heavyweights hold the largest companies leading their sectors, rotated on the first session of each month whose stored year holds the closes their readings need) (see: The market check closes every swing family's list together, and the sector heavyweights read none)
The sector heavyweights' card's rulefrom 17.5 on every index: the selector the swing cards carry beside the card's state line with the live rule or the provisional rule first and then each registered heavyweights rule by the number of its first registration with the register's words; the choice kept in the link under the family's own key; a rule chosen redraws the card from that rule's own book with its holdings at the night's close and the reading of its last rebalance under the band saying it is scored in the background and not the live rule with the clauses the live rule's words lack marked and no pick's card beneath it; the live rule drawn where the link names none or names a rule that does not stand; and on an index whose heavyweights no freeze registered the provisional rule alone with the line that no variant is registered before its freeze (see: A variant's picks are shown on its card when chosen and its results only under its tests)
Close to a buy point across the setupsbeneath the cards on such a night, in place of the swing filter's own list of them and in the page's order of setups: one row a stock and setup with the setup's label; the one gate it missed in the gate's words; and the count shown of the count there are (see: Tonight's page is drawn from setup families, each a rule of its own listing at most five a night)
Close to a buy pointbeneath the list on an evening the swing filter listed: one row per member whose stored result missed exactly one of the five gates and carries no exclusion, nearest to qualifying first with a tie in the list's own order, drawing the places the list leaves of the twenty, and a line above them stating how many are drawn of how many are one gate short. Each row: what a row of the list carries, the gate it missed in place of the gates, what it had against the bar it needed in plain words, how far short that is as a share of the bar, and the trade its plan states. On a night the market gate closed: one line above the rows stated once saying they would qualify if the market turned, with the breadth and its bar; and a key saying it recommends nothing (see: A member that missed exactly one gate and no exclusion is drawn close to a buy point nearest first, and recommends nothing)
An evening before the switchdrawn as it was listed, one row per name that fired, ordered by how many fired then by the plan's reward to risk
Reasons, per roweach reason named, with its measured record beside it under 15.11, and the values that made it true drawn beside it while it is under the pointer or holds focus
Research, per rowwhether the name holds a researched section besides the key under each figure
Ask for a reporta control on a row whose name holds none and has none queued and in the selected name's region beside a line saying none is written, which writes a request and starts the worker's drain to write it at the off-peak rate
The report's stateon a row and in the selected name's region, what the queue holds for the name: written with the day it was written; being written since the instant its pass started; queued with the instant it will start; or not written with the control asking for one (see: The queue page states when each request will be written)
Selected namethe plan column and the level summary for whichever row is selected, so the common case of checking a plan needs no navigation
Reason totalseach reason's count of tonight's fired names drawn as a bar out of the fired count with the count on it, which says whether the evening is one thing happening to many names or many things happening to a few

The list draws each reason in a column of its own, in a set order, headed by one word with the reason's full name on it, so an evening that is one thing happening to many names reads as one stripe down one column. Each reason's record sits once at the foot of its column and inside the reason on each row, and never beside a name. On an evening the swing filter listed, the order is the state the members' reported quarters give them, improving first, then steady, then the members reading no state, then deteriorating, and within each state the trade's reward to risk, then strength, then band strength, facts about the chart and the plan; the state orders what comes first and never what is recommended, since no gate reads it and every member the filter passes is listed whatever its state, and an evening whose night stored no readings keeps the filter's own order, since each night keeps the order it was drawn in; and the reasons stand beside each row as context (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it); a night the market gate closed draws no row and one line with the breadth and its floor, and a night no name passed one line with how many reached each gate, as section 18 states. Beneath it, on an evening the swing filter listed, the second list draws the members one gate short, nearest to qualifying first by how far the deciding value sits from its bar as a share of the bar, so a tenth short reads the same on every gate whatever its unit: a strength, a breadth, a depth, a dry-up, a reward to risk or a stop outside its bounds reads as its shortfall over the bar; a trigger that first fired on the Nth session back, tonight the first, against an arrival window of W sessions reads (N - W) / W; a condition not met at all counts as one whole bar, being no firing among the stored results, no band to set a target or a stop at, or a close outside an anchored support band; a trend that is not an uptrend adds half a bar for a range and a whole bar for a downtrend, the classifier's range sitting between the two; and shortfalls within one gate add. Each bar is the setting of the filter version the member's result was stored under. It reads what the night stored and stores nothing, so the edge clock and Past picks, which read the stored rows of the names the filter passed, never count a row of it, and a name on it opens to its page, whose Why it is here names the gate it missed and by how much (see: A member that missed exactly one gate and no exclusion is drawn close to a buy point nearest first, and recommends nothing). On an evening before the switch the order is how many reasons fired and then the plan's reward to risk, and a row whose plan computes no reward to risk is drawn after every row with one in its group, saying why (see: Tonight's list breaks a tie in fired count by the plan's reward to risk, and a row with none is drawn after every row with one and says why). Each row carries its place in that order, counted from one, and a line above the rows says how many are drawn of how many are listed, so the list says how long it is before a row of it is read (see: The page shows twenty and states the true count). Selecting a row, anywhere on it but its links, draws its plan beneath the list and brings it into view, and its ticker is a link opening the name's own page (see: Selecting a row draws its plan beneath the list and is no navigation). Its link names what it opens, the report with the day it was written where the name holds one and the name's page where it holds none (see: A researched name is one holding an accepted section besides the key under each figure). The reason totals are tonight's counts, and a reason's record over time is the run page's (see: Tonight's reason totals are counts, and a reason's record is the run page's).

The sector heavyweights' card names as its next rebalance the first session with no rebalance read in its month whose stored year holds the closes the live setting's readings need, so a month whose first session is a Monday names the Tuesday after it. On a night in a month whose rebalance the book has not read, a line beneath the card's standing says the rebalance waits, with the sessions the store's year holds and the sessions its readings need where it holds too few, and the session the book reads it on (see: The sector heavyweights hold the largest companies leading their sectors, rotated on the first session of each month whose stored year holds the closes their readings need).

15.8 Universe

Answers: where does everything sit, including the names nothing happened to.

Route: #/universe, with filters in the hash so a filtered view is a link.

Reads: the listings, levels and indicators for the night, membership, and the researched sections.

From 15.1 the table reads the index chosen under Universe, each of its members with its close, its typical move and its bands; the trend, the swing readings and the listing strip are read for the S&P 500's members alone, so the S&P 400's and 600's tables say so and draw those columns empty, and the filters and the pages keep the choice in their links. The researched names' route lists the chosen index's members holding research, the S&P 500's every researched name the S&P 400 and 600 do not hold, a former member among them (see: Every page reads one index at a time chosen under Universe, and every figure names its index).

RegionWhat is in it
Sector stripone line per sector: names, how many are on tonight's list, how many are in an uptrend. Clicking one filters the table
The tableevery name in the index, paged, sorted by distance to the nearest level ascending, so the top is what nearly fired.
