Columns: name, sector, close, trend state, the distance row mark, sessions until earnings, relative strength, the pullback from the recent high in typical days, the volume while it came down, the tightness of the range, the evening last on the list, and the listing strip over sixty sessions; each ticker a link to its own page that draws its year line while the pointer is over it (see: Marks are defined once and every screen draws from that list); each column heading saying what its column holds while the pointer is over it (see: Every figure carries a plain-language key)
Filterstrend state and sector, as chips
Researchedevery name holding a researched section with the day its newest one was written, on #/researched and linked from the masthead

The two right-hand columns count evenings a name appeared on the list, each evening read by the rule that listed it (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it). They say nothing about index membership, which every name in this table has by definition. That sentence is here because the columns were misread that way once.

A researched name is one holding a section the claim checker accepted besides the key under each figure, which the overnight queue writes for every name each night (see: A researched name is one holding an accepted section besides the key under each figure).

15.9 Name

Answers: what is this company's situation, and what is the plan at tonight's price.

Route: #/name/<ticker> for tonight, #/name/<ticker>/<date> for an earlier night.

Reads: the facts, ladder, levels, volume profile, moves and fundamentals for that name and date, the night's fundamental reading with the reported quarters of the fetch it read, every stored research section with its own date and model, the industry cycle the theme store holds for the industry the membership row names for the name, which is the theme's section rather than one of the name's and is read that way from 6.9, the source documents those sections cite, which the dates-and-sources region draws and this list did not name until 6.0, the calendar that region draws beside them, and the run log, for what research has spent and cost and what the newest pass for the name came to, which the page has read since 6.6 and this list did not name until 6.8, and series state, for whether the name's prices may not reflect a dividend or split, which the page reads from 7.0, and the sector heavyweights' holdings, for whether they hold the name, from 14.3.

RegionWhat is in it
Contentsat the head of the page: a numbered link to each region the page drew and to no other, in the order the page drew them. A link is followed to its region on the same page below the masthead as every link to a place on the page is, where one read as a screen's address would open tonight's list
Prices may be out of datepresent only when the name's stored series is suspect: one line saying its prices may not reflect a recent dividend or split, with when the refetch was last tried and why it failed, above everything the page draws from those prices
Why it is herepresent only when the name is on the list of the page's evening or close to a buy point on it: where the swing filter listed it, the rule and each gate with why it passed and the reasons that fired on it as context; where the reasons listed it, each reason in a full sentence rather than a label and with the values that made it true; where it is one gate short, the gate it missed with what it had against the bar it needed and how far short of it and the trade its plan states and a line saying it is not a pick
Fact stripclose, market capitalisation, the high and low of the move, next earnings date, the multiples, the averages, momentum and the typical daily move
Swing readingsthe return over 63 sessions and over 126 sessions with each one's place among the members' returns, the highest high of the last 20 sessions and how far the close sits below it in typical days' moves, the median volume of the sessions since that high against the fifty-day average, the mean true range of the last ten sessions against the last fifty, and a key saying how to read it
Member readingspresent for every member of the three indices where the night stored its readings, under the index that held it: the readings section 4 names for the region with each stored figure whole on its element and each the store holds none of saying why, and a key saying how to read it
Gateseach of the five gates with whether it passed and why, the setup's family and whether the trigger's event happened, the trade read from the ladder's first tranche and from the one swing plan that night's live rule used with that plan marked and no candidate's plan drawn whichever filter version the night ran under, and the exclusions with a key saying how to read it
The short versionthe narrative verdict, with the date it was written beneath it; where no accepted one stands, a summary code writes from the night's computed parts alone and headed by why it stands there (see: The short version is written last from the sections that passed, and one left out is replaced by a summary code writes)
How it got herethe twelve-month picture, and the table of the biggest moves with the cause of each where research has been written
Each move beside its groupon every row of the table of the biggest moves: the median move of the name's group over the same sessions; the group named as an industry or a sector with how many members it counted; a key saying how to read it (see: A large move is shown beside its group's median move over the same sessions)
Peersbeneath the table of the biggest moves: the name's own row marked and then at most ten members of its group by price alone, those sharing its industry first and then by how closely each one's daily moves followed the name's; each row carrying how closely it moved with the name, whether it shares the name's industry, the close, how far it sits below the stored year's high, its return over sixty sessions, its trend state, and the distance row mark; each ticker a link to its own page that draws its year line while the pointer is over it; each column heading saying what its column holds while the pointer is over it (see: Every figure carries a plain-language key); and a key saying how to read it (see: Peers are shown by price alone, ten at most with the name's industry first and then the members whose daily moves followed it most closely)
The chartthe level chart, the volume profile beside it on the same price axis, the momentum panel beneath, and the level summary table with each band's members and dates
How far each band ison every row of the level summary: the gap from tonight's close to the nearer edge of that band, counted in the moves the name usually makes in a session (see: Distances are stated as typical days' moves)
Level evidencethe level summary reads from the highest band to the lowest with the close as a row between the resistance and the support, as the plan column beside it does; each band's line says what its evidence is, the swings and visits by kind with the first and last of their dates or the one date they share; an average and a shelf are named by kind with no date, being recomputed every night; and each strength carries a bar a point long, with a key saying what a point is (see: A member's date is the session its evidence occurred on, and a figure recomputed nightly has none of its own)
The planthe plan column mark, the tranche table with conditions and stops, the exit table with actions, the earnings setups, and the sizing arithmetic. The region is headed Entry and exit plan; the mark's price line and stop rules cross the column and none of the words beside it; the tranches are headed Entries with what each zone is bought on and its stop in columns of their own and the stop the invalidation sits at saying so, and the exits are headed Exits; the last two prints' moves against the first tranche's stop stand under a heading of their own
Earnings reactionsbeside the earnings setups: one row per print over the calendar's year behind; each row carrying its report date, its timing, the session it moved on, the estimate, the actual, the provider's surprise, and that session's move; a print with no filed estimate saying none was filed; and a key saying how to read it
On the list beforepresent only where the live list picked the name on a night before the page's own: a line with how many times it was picked and how each group ended; a row per earlier listing, as the Past picks screen draws it and as it stood on the page's night; and a key saying how to read it (see: Every trade the live list recommended is shown, and their share waits for the minimum the reason records wait for)
Newspresent for every member: what was written about the company in the thirty days before the page's night; each article newest first with its kind as a small tag beside its source and its date and its link; its one-sentence reason while it is under the pointer or holds focus; above them a bar of positive against negative stories over the window counted over the newest label of each article with opinion pieces in neither; tabs for all and for each of the three directions and for opinion, an opinion piece in the opinion tab alone; a row refused by admissibility or answered unreadably saying so; the model that wrote the labels named once in small type; where the name holds no label for the night one line saying why, whether the labeller has not run for the night or was refused before it asked with its key missing or its model not answering or the name was not on the list or the month's limit or the day or month cap or the time limit or a peak window came before it; and a name with nothing stored in the window saying so (see: The news labels alone name the model that wrote them) (see: A news article is stored once per member with its admissibility judged, and a label is never overwritten) (see: A label's reason is one sentence holding no digit, and an answer code cannot read is asked once more and then kept as unreadable with its cause)
What it sells, the numbers, the cycle, the two cases, the risksthe researched and computed sections in the order section 4 specifies, each carrying its own date
Dividendin the numbers section, from the newest filing alone as the newest fetch of the company's figures states it: the forward annual rate, the forward yield as the provider states it, the payout ratio, the ex-dividend date and the pay date, and nothing where the provider files none
The numbers snapshotat the head of the numbers: twelve figures of the newest filing and the newest fetch a figure to a row in two columns, each with what it is measured against beneath it and its element carrying the stored value; the five quarters under a heading of their own; management's passage folded shut and a point to an item where the release marks its points; the other filed tables folded under one heading and each under its own, the segments with each group's label once over its lines; no provider named in the words (see: The numbers open on a snapshot of the newest filing with every other filed figure folded beneath it, and the report names no provider)
What the numbers sayat the head of the numbers where the page's night stored readings of the member's reported quarters: a heading carrying the state and the quarter it was read from; one sentence per reading written from section 4's patterns; a sentence saying so where a reading is absent or read over too few quarters; folded beneath, the quarters the readings read with the dates each was filed and reported on; and the full numbers table folded beneath them (see: Four readings of a member's reported quarters are worked out every night by rules the measured split settled, and its state is read from sales and operating margin alone)
The case for and the case againsta claim to a row; each case under its own label where the prose opens on the bull case, the case against from the first sentence opening on the bear case; the rows unlabelled where the prose opens on neither (see: A written section is drawn a claim to a row, and the two cases and the risks are asked for in the parts the page draws)
The risks as partsa table of each risk beside what would confirm it where every part the prose states opens its confirmation apart; one part per risk with what would confirm it set beneath where a part does not; a claim to a row where the prose states no part (see: A written section is drawn a claim to a row, and the two cases and the risks are asked for in the parts the page draws)
Dates and sourcesthe calendar, and every document the research read with its date and link
Research not yet writtenwhere no record exists for the name: the researched sections absent with one line saying they have not been written and a control that writes them with its cost stated before it is pressed, beside the computed sections rendered whole
Research stalewhere a record exists and a trigger has fired: the stored sections rendered with their own dates and one line naming which of the four triggers fired, with the option to have them rewritten
Regenerate Reportwhere a record stands or has gone stale and no pass has run for the name on the day in New York the page is read on: the control that has the paid model write every section again from the company's figures fetched again that day, its cost stated before it is pressed; a press writing a request that carries the ask; and the drain answering it with such a pass at most once a name a day, a request reaching it for a name a pass already wrote that day starting nothing and fetching nothing (see: A regenerated report is written whole by the paid model from the company's figures as they stand on the day it runs, once a name a day)
Research pausedwhere the spend cap has stopped research for the period: one line saying that research is paused and when it resumes, with the stored sections still rendered under their own dates
A pass as it runspresent only while a pass this page started is running: one line saying what the pass is doing and how many sections are written, redrawn in place as each section lands (see: A pass the page starts is watched until it ends and the page redraws as each section lands)
Sections left outone line per section the checker left out or the newest pass did not write, each naming what refused it and never the words of the draft that was refused (see: A refused draft's own words are kept on the row and drawn on the evidence page, and never on the name page)
Walkprevious and next on tonight's list, so an evening's reading is one pass through with no return to the list
The setup the page lists the name underbeneath the contents, on a night the setup families drew the page's list and a setup passed the name: the setup that lists it with its place and the other setups it qualified under, and a sentence for a setup that passed it and holds it back (see: A stock holds one trade across every swing family, and one qualifying under two is listed once under the first in the page's order)
Held by the sector heavyweightsbeneath the contents, on a night the sector heavyweights hold the name at its close: a line saying so with the session it was bought on and the sector it leads, and nothing where they do not (see: The sector heavyweights hold the largest companies leading their sectors, rotated on the first session of each month whose stored year holds the closes their readings need)

The page opens with the line the masthead carries, being the ticker, the company's name, the last stored close as of the session it closed on with its change on the day, and the sector and industry (see: The masthead carries the last stored close and the session it is from), and with a paragraph saying what the page is for, its three refusals, being that it does not predict where the price will go, that it ranks no company as an investment, and the one rank it draws is a return's place among the members' returns, a fact about the chart, and that it does not say how much to buy (see: A page ranks no company as an investment, and the one reading of a company that orders a list is the direction of its reported quarters), and the ten words it uses one disclosure down. The sizing arithmetic states the risk a share carries and leaves the budget to the reader, which is what keeps the third refusal true (see: The sizing arithmetic states the risk a share carries and holds no account of the reader's).

The key under each figure is drawn beneath the chart only where it was written for the night whose figures the page draws. A key written for another night is not drawn: its card names the night it was written for and says so, because a paragraph explaining another night's close beside these figures explains figures the page does not show (see: The key under each figure is dated by the night whose figures it explains, written for every name each night, and drawn only beside that night's figures).

Four parts are display only on this page, reaching no reason, no gate of the swing filter, no plan and no candidate: each move beside its group's median, drawn in the table of the biggest moves; the peers, a region of their own beneath that table; the earnings reactions, a region of their own after the plan, beside its earnings setups, which the earnings drift family alone reads as a rule; and the dividend, drawn in the numbers. Each is drawn in a card with a key saying how to read it (see: Every region is a card that states where its figures came from and how to read them). A name's group is read by one rule wherever it is used (see: A name's group is its industry where at least five other members share it on the session, and its sector otherwise, and every surface that uses it says which and how many). A print's reaction is read off the calendar and the stored bars, its session the one the earnings rule takes for it (see: Each print's reaction is read from the nightly calendar and the stored bars, and the earnings drift is the one rule that reads it). The dividend is the provider's, as it files it (see: The numbers section draws the dividend the provider files from the newest filing alone, and nothing for a company paying none). The exported report draws the four as the page does, from the same code path (see: A single report can still be exported as a self-contained file).

15.10 Run

Answers: how did last night go, how did the market stand, how did the index come down to the list, and what did it cost; top down, one question to a region, each a picture with a line or two of plain words beneath it.

Route: #/run/<date>. With no date it opens on the newest night the run log carries a stage for, whether or not that night wrote a list, so a night that stopped before its list is the one a person sees first. A night on a day with no session is not one it opens on, and neither is a day whose only rows are the version or register verb run by hand, whose rows the operational header draws marked as run by hand, apart from the night's own stage time and never among the stages that failed. The same calendar as tonight's page sits beside the night drawn and opens the run page of the night it picks, and like tonight's page it opens from the swing filter's first night.

Reads: the run log, the listings with the rule that listed each evening, the forward returns, the research store, which the stale-and-failed region draws sections from and this list did not name until 6.0. How each report did reads the theme store beside the research store, for the versions of the industry cycle a theme pass wrote under a report's run.

From 15.1 the page reads the index chosen under Universe, and what this section describes is the S&P 500's. The S&P 400's or 600's states how that index's night went, read off the rows its families stored: the members read, the index's own breadth against the floor and whether its swing lists were open, the members a setup passed, those listed and those held back by a trade still open on any index's list, the trades kept and ended, and its sector heavyweights' rebalance and holdings; and its setups, each provisional with what it listed and its trades so far. The night's steps are one list for every index and are drawn under the S&P 500, which the page links to (see: Every page reads one index at a time chosen under Universe, and every figure names its index).

From 15.5, once a freeze has registered a swing family's rules on the S&P 400 or 600, that index's Run page draws the family's setup row live with the day its live rule registered, the variants beside it and its live rule's record in words, and beneath the setups one row a registered rule of the index, each family's live rule first: the trades its own list kept, those decided with their edge, each trade's result less its own round trip at the published table less the same plan on every member of the index that night, in multiples of the risk, its whole blocks against the look they wait for, and the level its looks are read at, its family's own share over its own rules on that index (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's swing families is registered as the family on its index and evaluated by their step alone). A registered heavyweights rule's row is read over its own book's holdings, each holding's result less its round trip less its size cut's return over the same sessions in percentage points, counted in the block of the session it ended on (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's sector heavyweights keeps a book of its own in either design, read by the index families' step). An index no freeze has registered a rule on draws no such rows.

RegionWhat is in it
How last night wenta status mark and a headline naming the night's state as its own run log rows give it; four headline figures being the stocks read and the provider requests with the research spend and the steps run again; a time bar of the night's steps in six named groups showing where a stopped night stopped; each try so far with the step it stopped at and its reason while the night waits to try again or is left unfinished; a press running the rest of a night left unfinished; the commit the night was built from; each index's members beside the time to the close on a night that read more than one index (see: A night's state is read off its own run log rows and its tries, and the pages that state it read that one state) (see: A night left unfinished is run to its end from the step it stopped at by a press or a command, and one night runs at a time under a lock file) (see: Each night is built from a clean copy of the main checkout's own commit and never from its working tree, and refuses only a checkout off main or ahead of the remote's main)
The marketa one-word label read by a stated rule; a gauge of the share of members above their 200-day average with the market gate's floor marked; the share above the 50-day average and the index's volume against its fifty-day average; a line of that share over the sixty sessions before the night that the store holds averages for (see: The market on the Run page is named in one word by a stated rule that moves no gate)
From the index to tonight's lista funnel of how many members passed each of the filter's checks in turn down to those left after the exclusions; the count listed with a link opening tonight's list
How the list's trades are goingthe live list's trades still open and those that reached the target or were stopped out or ran out of time; a ring of the trades decided against the minimum a share waits on; the share and the break-even and the average result together once both minimums are met as Past picks draws them; a link opening Past picks (see: Every trade the live list recommended is shown, and their share waits for the minimum the reason records wait for)
Is the list finding new stocksa bar for each of the last twenty evenings split into the names new that evening and those the evening before also listed; the night's split in words
How the system learnsthe shape clock as the ordinary nights under the open filter version against the sixty its calibration waits on; each check's typical pass count against its range drawn dashed until measured; the edge clock as a line from today to its two checkpoints with the blocks the live list has gathered; each version running beside the live list with what it changes and the stocks it has picked and the share the live list also picked and its blocks against the floor; a link comparing tonight's picks (see: Candidate conditions are registered before they are scored, and a candidate's picks are shown on the Run page while its outcomes wait for a look)
Compare tonight's picksa choice of the versions running beside the live list kept in the link; the names only the live list picked and those both picked and those only the version picked with the setting that made the difference beside each name only one side picked; two overlapping rings holding the three counts; the version's picks over the last twenty evenings with the share the live list also picked and the evenings it picked a stock the live list did not; picks alone with no figure from how a pick turned out (see: Candidate conditions are registered before they are scored, and a candidate's picks are shown on the Run page while its outcomes wait for a look)
At a checkpointone row per version on a scale from nought to a hundred; before its first look a locked dashed outline with its trades and blocks so far; from its first look the share of its trades that reached the target with the break-even they needed and what no skill scored from the same starts and how far luck alone could move it; the verdict in words (see: A candidate's verdict is read only at looks fixed when it is registered, with each look's boundary found over every sign vector its blocks allow)
Research and spendthe month's spend against the month cap; the reports the paid model wrote on each of the last seven nights; the reports and the overnight drafts written over those nights; the news labeller's line with what the night's labelling cost and the month's against its limit and the articles labelled and the unreadable answers by cause and what stopped it (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own)
Anything to worry abouta checklist of plain items each turning red with its reason where it fails; every stock holding the night's prices and every step of the night finished; no research document refused and no section fallen back; every company awaiting a quarter asked on schedule; no paid model a job uses within thirty days of its retirement date, and where one is its profile named with its job and date (see: A profile carries its provider's earliest retirement date, and the run page names it from thirty days before); no report whose pass ran on the night's session costing more than section 17 names, and where one did its stock named with its cost (see: A report costing more than two dollars is named on the run page the morning after it was written); no drain stopped on an error, and where one did the time it started named with its error (see: A drain that stops on an error writes a row of its own, and the queue page states it until a pass starts after it); the store copied after the night began or a copy started since waiting or copying, and where one was ended before it finished or none was started its start or the night's named; every copy the newest copy's row before it kept still in the folder, and where any is gone each named; no live rule gone longer without a pick than its own past empty nights say it does, and where one has its family named with its stretch against its mark; the four harness counts beneath; the store's newest copy beneath them with the time it was made and its folder and the copies kept and the newest attempt that made none with why, with a copy started since that has written no end and whether it was ended before it finished and the copies the newest copy found gone from its folder that no copy removed (see: The store is copied once the night and every process it started have finished and the newest three copies are kept after each is opened and read, and the copy writes a row as it starts and one as it ends)
The detailevery region below this row, each in a section folded shut beneath the pictures so a table the page drew before is kept whole
Operational headerwhat ran, the instant each stage started and how long it took, model calls, network requests, spend, and what each stage said about itself, in a cell rather than behind a pointer
How each report didone row per report over the seven nights with its stock and day and what it cost; a cell per section saying whether it passed first time or on retry or was left out with why or was not warranted, with what its own calls cost and none of a trial's; the two cases' cell marked where a draft of the pass carried a figure on both sides, with how many of the newest twenty reports' two cases did; each section's share passed first time and its share left out over the newest twenty reports that warranted it (see: The run page draws how each report's sections came out and each section's rates over the newest twenty reports, and no trial's drafts)
Market readingthe night's breadth with how many members it was counted over, the share above the 50-day average beside it as context, and the index's median volume against its fifty-day average
Swing filter funnelhow many members each gate passed in order and how many it removed, the setup's families on a night that held a breakout, what each exclusion removed and how many pass, and the version the night ran under
Reason recordsone row per reason with the reason track mark, the resolved count, the never-entered count, the share that reached target before stop, and the break-even those setups demanded. A pinned first row gives the base rate over every name-night, so no figure stands on its own
The shape clockthe ordinary nights under the open filter version against the sixty the calibration waits on, every event night with what made it one, each gate's median count through it against its band, the list's median size against its band, drawn as not yet measured until the trigger, said at the top of the page once the trigger is crossed, and each reason's share of the index as context
The shape proposaleach gate's setting held and proposed with its median count and the list's under each against their bands, every gate no value in its range brings inside its band named as a finding, and beside it the non-empty blocks accepting it would restart
The edge clockeach swing family candidate's non-empty blocks against the 8 its first look is read at, its resolved setups, its share against its planned break-even and calibrated null from the floor on and nothing below it, that the first look can retire or leave a candidate and never promote one, when the earliest promotion can come, and each variant with the filter version it was defined against and the settings the live filter has since moved
Near missesthe setups the filter admitted, beside each gate and each exclusion the setups it alone rejected with every other gate passing, each group against its own planned break-even and calibrated null, and every figure withheld below the block floor
What the two clocks can dothe sentence section 13.8 opens with, word for word
What else is waiting on a countthe nights run for the session the clock fell on against five, the research passes carrying a recorded cost against twenty, the nights the version step replayed both kinds against five, the resolved event-book setups against 250, and the nights of trend labels under the third trend version against sixty, and the nights the news labeller ran against twenty with its measured duration and its month's spend and the share of answers refused for a digit, and the mid and small cap indices' members holding four dated rating counts against nine in ten of them; the labeller's nights are what its three operating rows wait on (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own)
The list from night to nighthow many of the night's names were on the list the evening before, how many at least once over the five evenings before, and how many over the twenty evenings before; each evening is read by the rule that listed it (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it)
Shadow candidateshow many candidate conditions are registered, the family's divisor that number sets, the count of distinct trials and the level each starts at beside it, and one line saying each candidate's record is withheld until it is promoted. No candidate's pick of a name appears here. A candidate's picks are drawn in the comparison of tonight's picks and counted among the versions of how the system learns and nowhere else (see: Candidate conditions are registered before they are scored, and a candidate's picks are shown on the Run page while its outcomes wait for a look) (see: Holm's level passes between the candidates by a graph fixed when they are registered, and its first step is 0.05 over the distinct trials read at a look or still running)
Candidates' recordsone entry for each registered candidate: the verdict field stating what the last look read and what triggers the next, the nightly figure beside it labelled as monitoring, the Poisson-binomial tail labelled and deciding nothing, each look's setups and the share they won against the bar the calibration set, the level that look spent and whether it crossed its boundary, the smallest excess that look could have detected, the design effect and what a loss cost in multiples of the planned risk, the setups entered and stopped on one session and those stopped out on a session the name reported on, the step the graph stands at with its level and the count of distinct trials, and no name anywhere in it. The verdict field changes at a look and never at a nightly reading (see: A candidate's verdict is read only at looks fixed when it is registered, with each look's boundary found over every sign vector its blocks allow) (see: The nightly running figure is monitoring and never the verdict)
Tonight's orderthe three orders of tonight's list over the twenty each would draw, the old order named as the benchmark, the setups each order drew, the setups whose whole window has closed, the blocks holding one against the floor, and no comparison drawn before every order reaches it. Each order is read over the nights whose listings recorded the band strength (see: A listing records the band strength the old order read, and the three orders are compared over the nights that recorded it)
Stale and failednames carrying yesterday's bars, the stage a night stopped on with its outcome and the reason, sections that fell back, documents refused by admissibility with the category that refused each
Overnight queuewhether the queue ran on the previous night and on which night it did not, with how many queued passes completed and how many were left for the next night
Harnessthe verdict counts from the last phase report: passed, failed, unexamined, each separately
The setup familieson a night the setup families drew the page's list: one row a setup in the page's order, live with the day its rule was registered or provisional, the variants scored beside it, what it lists on the night and the trades listed under it so far; and its record against what it waits for or the words saying it starts at the freeze (see: A family lists on provisional settings until its freeze, and nothing before the freeze counts toward a checkpoint). Beneath it, once a new setup's freeze has registered its rules: one row a registered rule, each setup's live rule first, the trades its own list kept, those decided with their edge over their benchmark in multiples of the risk, its whole blocks against the look they wait for, and the level its looks are read at; that level is its setup's own share over its own rules (see: A registered family rule is evaluated every night at its own settings and keeps its own list, its trades stored with their benchmark when they end) (see: Each setup family's correction for luck counts its own rules alone, at most nine a family); the sector heavyweights' registered rules among them, each holding's edge its percent return less its size cut's and counted in the block of the session it ended on (see: Each registered sector heavyweights rule keeps a book of its own beside the page's, its holdings scored in percent against their size cut); beside each rule the session its record counts from; where a replay at its registration found a trade differing, that it restarted there and why (see: A family rule registered again keeps its record from its first registration where a replay of its stored nights reproduces every trade, and restarts at the change otherwise); and beside each rule's edge its edge after each trade's own round trip at the published table over the trades priced (see: A 400 or 600 trade pays the published effective spread for its size and price, and its pass tests read the edge after it)

The page answers its questions top down, one region to a question, the picture first and a line or two of plain words beneath it, and every table it drew before is kept whole in a section folded shut beneath the pictures, so a reader glancing and a reader checking the arithmetic read the same page. Status is drawn in blues, a wait in violet and a failure in red, because green and orange are the levels' (see: Status is drawn in blues with violet for a wait and red for a failure alone). Every figure is read from the store by the read API, and nothing is computed at night for the page.

For each registered candidate the run page states the verdict field, the last look, the looks remaining and what triggers the next, and beside it the running figure labelled as monitoring; the block count against its floor of 8; the estimated design effect, labelled noisy near 8 blocks; the Holm step and its level; the count of distinct trials; the same-session losses counted; and, in its own region, the three orders of tonight's list with the old order named as the benchmark and no comparison shown before its block count is reached (see: The nightly running figure is monitoring and never the verdict). Judgement: each is stated where the verdict is read, because a verdict whose floor, dependence and multiplicity a reader cannot see is a number without its denominator.

15.11 How a reason's record is displayed

A reason's record is shown beside the reason wherever the reason appears, and it is a property of the reason rather than of the name beside it. The number says how this reason has done across every name it ever fired for, and it is not a statement about tonight's name.

StateWhat is shownWhy
Below the minimuma dashed outline carrying the count of resolved setups that set a bar against the minimum, and no ratea rate over a handful of resolved setups is consistent with almost any truth, and a pale number would read as a small one rather than as an absent one
At or above the minimumthe share that reached the target before the stop, the number resolved, and the break-even those setups demanded, always the three togethera share without its denominator hides how much was checked, and a share without the break-even hides whether it was any good, since a setup with a distant target needs to be right rarely
Unresolved setupstheir own segment of the reason track, never folded into the ratea setup that has done nothing is neither right nor wrong
Never showna single number beside the ticker with no denominator and no barit would be read as this name's chance of going up, and it is a historical frequency of a reason

This column is a dashed outline for the first year, and that is the correct behaviour rather than a defect. The list surfaces roughly fifteen names a night, so a reason accumulates a few hundred listings a year and rather fewer resolved setups. A verdict that can separate a reason clearing its break-even by ten points from one that does not needs a few hundred resolved setups at a threshold corrected for the family, and clustering by sector and by date means the effective count is lower than the row count. Setting the minimum low enough to fill the column sooner would produce a figure that looks like evidence and is not, and a figure on a screen gets acted on. (see: The record column stays empty until it has earned a number)

The last row is a prohibition rather than a state: a record is drawn in one of the first two states, with its unresolved setups as the track's own segment in either (see: A reason's record is drawn in two states, and a bare number beside a ticker is a prohibition rather than a third).

15.12 Opening a name, in order

  1. The computed sections render immediately from the nightly store, each move's group median, the peers and the earnings reactions among them.
  2. The numbers section renders from the filings the store holds, the dividend from the newest filing alone, and the parts that are as of a fetch from the newest fetch's copy. Opening a name fetches nothing: where a name holds none, the research pass fetches them before it writes and assembles that night's facts file again where it stored a filing the night had not seen, and a regenerate fetches them again whatever is held and assembles the facts file again after it (see: A regenerated report is written whole by the paid model from the company's figures as they stand on the day it runs, once a name a day).
  3. The staleness judge answers its four questions from stored data.
  4. Whatever sections are stored render with the date each was written. The page offers to have the paid model write again what the local model drafted. Nothing is spent for any of this.
  5. Sections the local lane does not own are absent until asked for, which on the current machine means the two cases, the risks and the short version. Asking runs a paid pass for those sections only, with progress shown, and the sections stream in as they are checked and stored.

15.13 Routing and state

  • Hash routes only. No server-side routing, no history API, no build step.
  • A route is a link. The selected name and any filters live in the hash, so a filtered universe view and a selected candidate can both be sent to another machine.
  • Back and forward work, because the router listens for the hash changing and pushes nothing the browser did not ask for.
  • The theme is a stamp on the root element, remembered between visits, with the machine's preference as the default and both themes designed rather than one inverted.
  • An unknown route resolves to tonight with a line saying what was asked for, rather than to a blank page.
  • Any name is found from a search box in the masthead of every screen, by its ticker or its company's name, and a name found is opened on its own route. Text matching no name says so rather than opening an empty page.
  • Every page reads one index at a time, chosen under Universe at its top: Tonight, Past picks, Run, Universe and Researched each open with a selector offering the S&P 500, the S&P 400 and the S&P 600, each with its members on the night, and the choice lives in the hash as ?universe=400, the S&P 500 read where the hash names none. The heading names the index, and every count, the breadth line and the market line say the index they are over, so no figure on a page mixes two (see: Every page reads one index at a time chosen under Universe, and every figure names its index).

15.14 What no screen does

  • No screen fetches from a provider or calls a model. The only thing a screen can trigger is a research pass, and that is an explicit action with a visible cost, not a side effect of navigation.
  • No screen computes a level, a stop or a rate. Every figure is read, and every part of a page states where it came from and as of when. (see: A screen reads and renders, and computes only the plan in the operator's money and a pick's open trades in its sector) (see: Every part of a page states where it came from and as of when, and a written section when it was written rather than which model wrote it)
  • No screen shows a figure without its denominator where the figure is a share.
  • No screen shows a number beside a ticker that could be read as that name's probability of rising.
  • No screen orders names by an opinion about the company; the one reading of a company that orders anything is the direction of its reported quarters, by a stated rule. The universe orders by distance to a level and tonight's list by the state each company's reported quarters give it, improving first and deteriorating last, then by the trade's reward to risk, then strength, then band strength, a night that stored no readings by the filter's own order, and an evening before the swing filter's list by how many reasons fired and then the plan's reward to risk, each a fact about the chart, the plan or the reported quarters (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it) (see: A page ranks no company as an investment, and the one reading of a company that orders a list is the direction of its reported quarters). (see: Tonight's list selects the stocks worth buying or paying attention to that evening, and the improvement loop exists to make that selection better) (see: Tonight's list breaks a tie in fired count by the plan's reward to risk, and a row with none is drawn after every row with one and says why)
  • A screen ranks no company as an investment, and the one rank it draws is a return's place among the members' returns, a fact about the chart (see: A page ranks no company as an investment, and the one reading of a company that orders a list is the direction of its reported quarters).

15.15 Queue

Answers: which reports have been asked for, which one is being written now, and what came of the rest.

Route: #/queue, the fifth entry in the masthead. It is numbered after the sections that follow the other four screens rather than among them, because a heading number here is navigation and the record already cites 15.11 to 15.14.

Reads: the request store, and the run log for the pass a claimed request is being written under and for the newest drain that stopped on an error.

RegionWhat is in it
Outstandingevery request nobody has started, drawn in the order the worker takes them in and naming who asked
Being writtenthe request the worker has claimed, with the pass it is running under
Settledwhat each request came to, with the reason where there is one
Take it outa control on an outstanding request, refused once the worker has claimed it
When each will be writtenwhen the pass of every request will start or started and when it is expected to end or ended, in New York's time with the offset named and UTC beside it; a request with nothing ahead of it starts now, or at the end of the peak window it was asked in or that the longest pass the store holds would carry it into; one behind others starts after them on the median of the passes the store holds that ran to their end, which the page names with how many it is over; the page names the longest of them too, and takes every start from the one function the drain calls; and a store holding none says it cannot estimate (see: The queue page states when each request will be written)
Which lane would write onethe two words at the head of every page, the choice that is not offered drawn beside the one that is and what it waits on stated here
A drain that stoppedthe newest drain that stopped on an error outside a pass; the time it started in New York's time and UTC and the error it stopped on; stated above the requests until a pass starts after it; nothing where no drain stopped (see: A drain that stops on an error writes a row of its own, and the queue page states it until a pass starts after it)

A request is asked for from a row on tonight's list, from a name's own page, or by the night for six names taken in turn across the three indices' pages, and all three write the same row, so this screen is where each is read (see: The six reports a night are taken in turn across the three indices, one at a time in the page's order). A press that writes a request starts the worker's drain as a process of its own, from a copy of the worker's build, and the drain takes what is here oldest first, waiting for the off-peak rate before a pass where it starts inside a peak window or reaches one between passes. Drains run one at a time over a store, one started while another runs waiting for it to end, so the order this screen states is the order passes run in. Nothing on this screen starts one, and a drain that could not be started leaves a request outstanding rather than losing it, for the next press or the drain run by hand (see: A press writes a request and starts the worker's drain as a process of its own, and every pass waits for the off-peak hours) (see: Queued work runs off-peak, and every schedule is written in UTC).

Taking a report out is what the operator asked for and it is bounded by what they asked for. A report that has not been generated is one nobody has started, so a withdrawal moves a request that is still outstanding and is refused on one the worker holds, with the refusal naming the state that refused it. Nothing is deleted: a withdrawn request stays a row, because what is asked of this screen is what was asked for and what came of it, and removing the row would answer the second question by erasing the first.

15.16 Watch list

Answers: how each name the operator follows stands on the newest night, whether or not the list holds it.

Route: #/watch, the second entry in the masthead. It is numbered after the queue rather than beside tonight's list, because a heading number here is navigation and the record already cites the numbers before it.

Reads: the watch list, and for the newest night the listings, the bars, the gate results and the membership. Writes: the watch list, on the operator's press alone.

RegionWhat is in it
Add a namea box offering the names of the index, which adds one while the list holds fewer than twenty and otherwise gives way to a line saying the limit is reached, the same press beside a name on its own page, and a refusal with the line saying why for a name not of the index tonight or already watched or a twenty-first
Each name watchedin the order it was added, its company, its close and the day's change, its trend in a word, the reward to risk of its trade, the day it was added and a link to its page, drawn for the newest night whether or not the list holds it
What the swing filter said of itlisted and its number, the first gate that stopped it with that gate's reason, what excluded it, or that no answer is stored for the night
Take it outa press on each name, which takes it off the list

The watch list is the operator's own and decides nothing: the night, the list, the queue and every record read no row of it. It holds up to twenty names of the index, each put there or taken off by a press on this page or beside the name on its own page, and a press is refused without the page's own header, as every press is (see: The watch list is the operator's own, up to twenty names of the index, on a page of its own) (see: A pass is started only by a request carrying the name page's own header).

15.17 Past picks

Answers: how each trade the live list recommended turned out, one trade at a time, and how they have done together once there are enough of them to say.

Route: #/picks, between the universe and the researched names in the masthead, with its status filter in the hash so a filtered view is a link. It is numbered after the watch list rather than beside the other screens, because a heading number here is navigation and the record already cites the numbers before it.

Reads: for the newest night, the gate results with the rule that listed each evening and the filter version each night ran under, the fundamental readings each night stored, the forward returns, the bars and the membership, and from 14.3 the sector heavyweights' holdings.

From 15.1 the page reads the index chosen under Universe, and what this section describes is the S&P 500's. The S&P 400's or 600's draws every trade its lists kept, newest first, each named with its setup and its index, with its result before its cost, its cost at the published spread and its result after, in multiples of its risk, and its sector heavyweights' holdings in percent; every rule of those indices is provisional, so no share and no average is drawn (see: A 400 or 600 trade pays the published effective spread for its size and price, and its pass tests read the edge after it).

RegionWhat is in it
How the list's picks have donethe trades listed with the nights they were listed on; how many are still open and how many finished; how many reached the target and how many were stopped out or ran out of time; a line saying how many carry no outcome row; below the minimum a dashed outline stating the trades decided at the target or the stop and their listing nights against the numbers needed with no share; at or above it a bar of the finished trades in three steps of one neutral hue with a line at the decided trades' average break-even; the share that reached the target first beside the share needed to break even and the average result in multiples of the risk taken, the three always together; a line saying how many were listed again while an earlier trade was open, drawn and not counted (see: A repeat listing made before the rule reached the filter is marked and counted once); a key saying how to read it
Filtersa chip for all and one for each status a trade can stand in with its count; none by setup
Every tradenewest first; within a night the order that night's list was drawn in, improving businesses first where it stored readings and the filter's own order where it stored none; a line above the rows stating how many are shown of how many were listed; the night listed; the stock with a link to its page for that night; the state its reported quarters gave it on the night it was listed, or not read that night; the buy and the stop and the target; the trade line; the status in words; the sessions held to its resolution or to the newest night; the result as a signed multiple of the risk or open; a repeat listing made while the trade from an earlier night was open marked as listed again and counted once (see: A repeat listing made before the rule reached the filter is marked and counted once); each column heading saying what its column holds while the pointer is over it (see: Every figure carries a plain-language key); a key saying how to read the trade line and that only the live list's trades appear with the alternatives hidden until one is promoted
The setup filterabove the status chips, once the page has listed a trade under more than one setup: one chip a setup with its trades and the counts following the setup chosen (see: Tonight's page is drawn from setup families, each a rule of its own listing at most five a night)
The setup a trade was listed undera label on its row
A trailing tradedrawn with no target and its result in multiples of its risk (see: A breakout is a close above the year's high on heavy volume after its ranges narrowed, sold on a trailing stop with no target)
A provisional setup's tradesmarked and counted in no share (see: A family lists on provisional settings until its freeze, and nothing before the freeze counts toward a checkpoint)
The sector heavyweights' holdingsbeneath the trades, every holding the sector heavyweights bought, newest first: its sector; the session it was bought on with its close; the session it was sold on with its close, or held; why it ended; its result in percent of the buy; its size cut's return over the same sessions and the difference between them; the words saying these are the page's own book and each registered rule's record is its own; and nothing where the book has bought none (see: A sector heavyweight's trade is scored by its percent return less the equal-weighted return of the size cut it was chosen from) (see: Each registered sector heavyweights rule keeps a book of its own beside the page's, its holdings scored in percent against their size cut)

A trade is a name the swing filter passed on a night it listed, from its first night on, with the plan that night's trade gate read: section 10's plan where the night's filter version reads it and the plan at the nearest bands otherwise, the choice the near misses make (see: A swing filter row carries both swing plans, each scored from the night's close, and a candidate's setups are scored on the plan its own trade gate reads). A candidate's plan, a member one gate short of passing and an evening the reasons listed are not trades the list recommended, and none appears here. Each is bought at the close of the night it was listed, so none goes unentered, and is followed on its forward return: open while the row carries no outcome, reached target on a win, stopped out on a loss and ran out of time where the cap passed first. Its result is the stored return over the risk as a share of the buy, measured on closes as the outcome is, so a close through the stop can read below minus one.

A trade is a fact about one recommendation and is drawn whatever became of it. The share that reached the target waits for the minimum the run page's reason records wait for, counted over the trades decided at the target or the stop and the nights they were listed on, and a trade that ran out of time is counted and drawn and never in the share (see: Every trade the live list recommended is shown, and their share waits for the minimum the reason records wait for) (see: An unresolved setup is never a win). Everything is read from stored rows, and the four figures the screen states that no row holds, what became of a trade as of the night drawn, the sessions it was held, its result and where its dot sits, are worked out by the read surface's projection for the screen and by nothing at night (see: A screen reads and renders, and computes only the plan in the operator's money and a pick's open trades in its sector).

15.18 The decision card

Tonight's page says which stocks the rules picked; the card says, beside each pick, what a decision on it needs: whether anything is against the trade, and what the rule that picked it has done before. It gathers what the store already holds into one card a pick, every figure computed by code from stored rows as they stood on the night and naming its index, and it advises and removes, reorders or hides no pick: no list, pick, queue, report request or record reads it (see: A pick's card advises on the trade and removes no pick, and code computes every figure on it). The night writes a card for each stock every index's families listed and each stock its sector heavyweights' book bought, with the card's values it was read with, so a value moved later never rewrites an earlier card.

Each pick's row on Tonight carries a control that opens its card in place beneath the row, for every family on every index, and each holding of a sector heavyweights' book opens the card of the night it was bought; a stock's page opens with the card of the family that listed it on the page's night. On a screen narrower than 640 pixels each line stacks its mark, its name and its words in one column, and the card keeps to the screen's width when the table it sits in scrolls sideways.

The checklist is six lines, each a tick, a note or a warning with its reason in words. Trend and strength names the gates the family read: the S&P 500's with the reasons its rows stored, and the S&P 400's and 600's as their nights' settings state their rules, since those rows store the rule and not its values; a pick passed every gate to be listed, so this line is a tick on every card and says which. The business reads the four newest quarters filed before the night and the night's state, and warns where their net income sums to nothing or less, where operating income covers interest under the card's floor, a financial company's and one filing no interest expense not read, where the state reads deteriorating, and where any of the three is not held. The market and sector line states the index's breadth against its floor and the stock's sector's place among the index's sectors by their members' mean return over the window, and warns where the sector stands among the bottom places, since industry momentum carries much of a stock's own (Moskowitz and Grinblatt (1999)). The earnings line takes the next report on file and the session it moves by the earnings rule's own reading, warns where that session falls inside the time by which the card's share of the rule's replayed trades had ended, notes it where it falls inside the rule's cap alone, and warns where no report date is on file (see: The card warns of a report inside the time three in four of the rule's trades had ended by, and notes one inside the cap alone). The liquidity and cost line states the dollar volume over the window the floors read and the round trip at the published table in the trade's risk, and warns at the card's value or over; a rule with no stop reads it in per cent of the buy. The concentration line counts the operator's open taken trades in the stock's sector on the S&P 500, 400 and 600 together, the stock's own left out, says it counted across the three, and warns at two or more; it is the one figure on a card reading every index, and it is worked out where the card is drawn from the trades open then, so the night stores the first five lines and a page drawing the card's presses adds the sixth (see: A pick's concentration line counts the operator's open trades in its sector across the three indices and names them).

Beneath the checklist the rule's record is drawn under the rule's own heading, naming the rule and its index and never the stock, opening with the line that it is the rule's record over every stock it bought and not this stock's chance (see: A rule's record is drawn under the rule's own heading, beside its reason or on a pick's card and never as the stock's own). It is the rule replayed at its one setting over the pulled history by the sweep's own walk, each trade after its cost: the trades with the history's span and whether membership was read as it stood, the share that ended at its target where the rule sets one, the mean result, the median sessions held and the sessions by which the card's share had ended, and the median worst close before the end. The settings were chosen on that same history, so the figures read high, and the record says so (Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado and Zhu (2014)) (see: A rule's record is replayed at its one setting by the sweep's own code over the pulled history, after costs on every index). Below the rules' minimum only the trades against it are drawn, and a rule not yet replayed draws a dashed outline saying so.

From 17.7, on a card of a family a learned score reaches, the breakout and the drift on every index and the pullback on the S&P 400 and 600, a part beneath the record draws the setups like the pick under its rule, under the rule's heading and opening with the line that they are setups like this one under this rule on its index and not this stock's chance. The night matches them from the ledger and stores the part on the card: among the finished setups the rule's own setting passed on the index, the nearest to the pick on the readings weighing most in the index's newest score, each taken as its place among those setups, the pick's own stock left out and a stock matched once within a run of sessions. It draws how many were matched of how many and their median distance, their mean edge against the same plan on every member that session with its ninety per cent interval, and the mean of every one the rule passed beside it, both before costs, and where the interval holds that mean it says "Not distinguishable from the rule's record", the figures drawn either way. The pick's rank under the score is drawn there only once one of the score's proposals has passed the tester on the index, and until then the part reads "Score not yet validated on this index"; a part the night could not match names why in its place, and the card is written regardless (see: A pick's card draws the setups like it under its rule beneath the rule's record, and the score's rank only once the score passed on its index).

RegionWhat is in it
A rule standing at an approved changefrom 17.9 on an S&P 400 or 600 card whose family stands at a change an approval stored the change named among the rule's gates and in the record's place the line that the record stored for it replays the setting before the change and so is not this rule's (see: An approved change is applied before the next night from the night's own build, on the index it was approved on alone)
The score's partfrom 17.7 beneath the rule's record on a card of a family a learned score reaches: the setups like the pick under its rule on its index with how many were matched and their mean edge and its interval beside the rule's own mean and the sentence saying where the interval holds that mean that it is not distinguishable from the rule's record; and the pick's rank under the score only once the score passed the tester on the index with the words saying it is not yet validated before (see: A pick's card draws the setups like it under its rule beneath the rule's record, and the score's rank only once the score passed on its index)

Beneath the record the card draws the plan in the operator's money, worked out where it is drawn by one function in the core from the account the operator keeps on a page of its own reached from the masthead: the account's size, the risk a trade in per cent and the position cap, a fifth of the account where the page proposes it (see: A pick's card sizes its plan from the operator's own settings, and the report's plan still sizes none). The shares are the risk over the stop's distance rounded down, and no more than the cap buys, rounded down; the card states them with the position's value, its share of the account, what is at risk and the round trip at the published table bought and sold at the buy, and says where the cap cut the shares. A holding with no stop is an equal share of the account across the most holdings its book can hold, its leaders in each of the eleven sectors, capped the same way, and the card says the whole position is at risk (see: A holding with no stop is sized at an equal share of the account across the most holdings its book can hold). The settings live in a file of their own under the data root, written whole, and no store row, log line, run log row or exported report carries them (see: The account settings live in a file of their own under the data root and in nothing the store or the logs hold); with none kept, the card draws its plan in prices and risks and one line linking the account page. Under the plan the card states how the trade is managed in its rule's own terms and no others: the stop as a sale at the close of a session that closes below it, since every rule here reads its stop on closes and none on a price touched during a session, a trailing rule's stop raised after each close to that close less the plan's distance and never lowered, the target as a close at or above it where the rule sets one, the cap in sessions after the buy, and the sector heavyweights held while they lead and sold at the close of a later month's rebalance where the rule would no longer buy them; no step a rule lacks, a move of the stop to the buy among them, is named.

A card drawn on Tonight, for whichever night the page shows, or on a stock's page for tonight, carries a Taken press with an optional fill price and date, the date the session after the pick's night where none is entered. With no price entered, the fill is the plan's buy marked provisional until the next session's open is stored; an entered price is never replaced (see: A taken trade's fill is the next session's open once its bar is stored, and the plan's buy marked provisional until then). A fill at or under the stop, a stock already holding an open taken trade, a card stating no buy and a press without the page's own header are refused, the reason drawn on the card and nothing written. Each trade taken from the card is listed on it with its fill and its exit; Not taken removes one only while no night has followed it and no exit is recorded, and after that the operator records an exit with its price and its date. A stock's page for an earlier night, which offers no control, and an exported report draw no press, no plan in money and no sixth line on its card, since each reads the operator's own account or trades.

Beside the plan the card names what could hit the trade before its hold ends, the hold being the cap's count of sessions after the night, or a month for a holding with no cap, each figure written by the night from stored rows. The stock's stored earnings reactions: how many, their median move in its typical moves and in this plan's risk, and how many moved further than the stop's distance, since every rule here sells on a close through its stop and a report can carry a trade past it in one session. The next ex-dividend date inside the hold, declared where the night's ask of the provider's dividend calendar found one and otherwise estimated from the company's last declared date and its usual interval, with the payment a share in the plan's risk (see: A pick's next ex-dividend date is the calendar's where it declares one and the last declared date plus the usual interval where it does not). Where the calendar declares none and the store keeps none of the company's dividend yet, which the quarters fetch keeps from the night after the company next reports, a hold running past the sessions the calendar is asked for says a later date is not ruled out, rather than that there is none. And each FOMC decision and CPI release inside the hold, from the table committed at the repository's root, each naming the page it was read from, a hold running past a kind's last date saying so, since the days they are announced carry much higher market returns than other days (Savor and Wilson (2013)) (see: Market events inside a hold are read from a committed table of the Fed's and the BLS's own dates, and asked of no provider).

Each night a follower follows every trade the operator took over the stored closes from its fill's session under its rule's own management, replaces a provisional fill with its session's stored open, and ends a trade at its stop, its target, its cap, its book's sale, the operator's exit or its last close as a member, its result in the plan's risk from the fill, or in per cent for a holding with no stop; it reads every price at the series' scale on the night, so a split inside a trade ends nothing. On Tonight the card draws the operator's own record of its family on its index under the rule's heading and never the stock's: won, lost and open, or ended for a rule setting no target, and the average result once twenty have ended, a dashed outline saying how many have before (see: The operator's own record states its average result once twenty of its trades in a family and index have ended). Beneath it stand the rule's own picks listed on the same nights, each followed from the plan's buy under the same management and counted the same way, so what differs between the two is the operator's choices and fills and not the market of those weeks. Past picks lists them for the chosen index under Your trades, open ones first, each with its exit press. No component that makes a pick, keeps a list or a record, or asks for a report reads them.

Key. The card as Tonight draws it beneath a pick's row, its parts in the order it draws them. Parts 3, 6 and 7 are drawn only where the operator's own settings and trades are read, on Tonight and on a stock's page for tonight, and an exported report carries none of them.

  1. The checklist: six lines, each a tick, a note or a warning with its reason in words and naming its index; trend and strength, business, market and sector, earnings in the hold, liquidity and cost, and concentration.
  2. The rule's record, under the rule's own heading and never the stock's: its one setting replayed over the pulled history after each trade's cost, with its trades, the share won, the average result, the sessions held and the worst close, and below the minimum only the count against it.
  3. The plan in the operator's money: shares from the account's size and its risk a trade over the stop's distance, rounded down and capped, with what is at risk, the position's value and share of the account, and the round trip.
  4. The management, exactly the rule's own: each exit a closing rule, the stop or the raised trail, the target where the rule sets one, and the cap.
  5. What could hit the trade before its hold ends: the stock's stored earnings reactions in the plan's risks, the next ex-dividend date declared or estimated, and each FOMC decision and CPI release inside the hold.
  6. The operator's own trades of the rule on its index, won, lost and open with the average once twenty have ended, and beneath them the rule's own picks on the same nights, each bought at the plan's buy.
  7. The Taken press, recording a trade at an entered fill or at the plan's buy marked provisional until the next session's open is stored.

15.19 The setup ledger

Answers: what every near-setup on an index came to, not only the ones a rule picked: how many each family's loose gates pass a year, how many of those the live rule passes and the night's list picked, and how the settled ones turned out against the same plan on every member.

Route: #/ledger, reached from the Universe page and drawn under it, with the index, the family and the chosen setup in the hash so a view is a link.

Reads: the ledger's summary for the index chosen, which the ledger's writers refresh after each night and each build, the family's newest settled setups and the chosen setup's closes from the bar store and the kept bars. The page draws them and computes none (see: A setup is every member-session a family's loose gates pass, and its readings are defined once and read as they stood).

RegionWhat is in it
A family's setupsa card a family drawing each year's setups and the deciles of their results from the summary the ledger refreshes
Settled setupsthe newest settled setups of the family the hash names with each stock a link drawing its path
A setup's paththe chosen setup's closes drawn with its plan's lines and its session marked

A family's card draws each year's setups with the share the live rule passes, the share the night's list picked of the rows a night wrote, and the settled ones with their mean result and edge, then the cut points between the deciles of result and edge of the newest year holding settled setups, each with a key saying how to read it. The settled setups name each one's session, stock, the live rule's pass, end, result and edge, the first family drawn where the hash names none. A setup's path is its closes from about ten sessions before it to the session its path ended, with its buy, its stop and its target drawn across where the plan holds them, and a line saying so where the store holds its bars only in the pulled history. A heavyweights' setup is read as a fraction of its buy and every other family's in multiples of its risk, each named in its column's heading, so no figure on the page mixes the two (see: A heavyweights' setup is each member of its sector's size cut on a rebalance of the S&P 500's book, held as the rule holds a buy). An index whose ledger holds nothing yet says so in one line.

15.20 The Loop page

Answers: what each family's rule on an index is today, what the loop proposed to change in it, and whether the change held on years it never saw: each proposal's verdict part by part and its test years against the rule.

Route: #/loop, reached from the Universe page and drawn under it, with the index and the month in the hash so a view is a link.

Reads: the newest tester run for the index and the month chosen, its proposals and their test years, from 17.5 the autopsy's figures of each family, from 17.6 each reading's spread, from 17.7 each family's learned score and the ranks tonight's cards carry under it, from 17.9 the words given on the index with what the apply step did with each and the settings approvals stored and the live alarm's periods, and the months the index's runs are for. The page draws them and computes none (see: A proposal passes the tester on a block sign-flip test of its total edge after costs against the current rule, corrected within a run and held to a fixed bar across runs).

RegionWhat is in it
A family's rule todaya card a family opening on its rule in the words the run stored
The readings, winners against losersfrom 17.6 beneath a family's proposals each reading's spread over its finished listings in a section folded shut: the listings holding it and the winners and the losers among them with each side's median and the mean edge of each tenth in the reading's order (see: Winners against losers proposes a condition only where it beats a within-night shuffle of its own search)
The autopsy's findingsfrom 17.5 beneath a family's rule today the figures the autopsy read off its finished trades with a line each and the trades it was read over; and beneath each exit the autopsy proposes the finding naming why: the figures where it read the rule's trades and the exit's edge on the years it learned on against the rule's (see: The trade autopsy proposes exits of a fixed menu, each tested as the procedure that chose it)
The learned scorefrom 17.7 beneath a family's proposals of the score the score fitted on all finished data with its weight in words and its hash; and the words saying the score is not yet validated on this index until one of its proposals passed and from then the rank each of tonight's cards carries under it (see: A pick's card draws the setups like it under its rule beneath the rule's record, and the score's rank only once the score passed on its index)
A proposal's verdicteach proposal's change or that it proposes none and its four parts each with its figure and whether it held
A proposal's test yearseach test year with the setting its fold chose and the rule's and the proposal's totals
Your word on a proposalfrom 17.9 beneath each passing proposal of the index's newest run that states a change its Approve and Decline presses or the word given with what the apply step did with it or why no press is offered there (see: An approved change is applied before the next night from the night's own build, on the index it was approved on alone)
Your decisionsfrom 17.9 every word given on the index newest first with what the apply step did with it and every setting an approval stored (see: A declined proposal is put again once a new complete block has been added since the decline and it passes with that block)
