The live alarmfrom 17.9 each family's months or a book's quarters against the floor its reference gives with the flag on two counted periods running and the restore waiting for approval where an approval changed the rule (see: The live alarm flags a rule whose edge stood under its reference's fifth percentile two periods running)

A family's card opens on its rule today, read from the words its run stored for the rule the proposals were tested against, and says so in one line where the run tested no procedure for the family. Each proposal under it states the change the procedure makes run on all finished data, or that it chose no setting and proposes none, then its four parts: the gate's adjusted p-value over its blocks against the bar, or that its blocks are under the floor; the stability screen's better years of those counted; the paired total with the five largest results left out of each side; and its units against the count its family is judged on, each saying whether it held. Its test years follow, a row each, with the setting the fold chose on the trades that ended before the year began, or that none met the floors and the year reads the rule today, each side's total edge after costs over its units, and whether the year is counted and better. Beneath them the difference the gate detects four times in five at the bar, read from the blocks' own scatter, and how many folds chose within a grid step of the proposal; and the key says the rule today was chosen on these same test years, so a proposal reads understated against it (see: A change is adopted only on test years the proposal never saw, and a search is judged as a procedure run year by year). A swing family's figures are in risks and the heavyweights' in points of the buy, each a month's, and a page for an index with no run says so in one line. From 17.5 a family the autopsy read stands its figures beneath its rule today, each in words with the trades it was read over, and an exit the autopsy proposes carries its finding beneath its change; a family the run read no figure for draws none, and a proposal naming no change carries no finding. From 17.6 the conditions winners against losers proposes stand among the proposals, each with its finding, and beneath them each reading's spread is drawn in a section folded shut, a row a reading.

16. Data stores and the read and write matrix

StoreOne row isKept
Membershipindex, ticker, joined, leftforever; without it a name added last month would appear in a window it was never part of
Bar storeticker, date, open, high, low, close, volume, sourceone year; older bars are dropped nightly
Setupsone row per index, family, stock and session a family's loose gates passed the stock on: the words of the live rule's setting and whether it passes, whether the night's list held it, the plan as prices with the risk in typical moves, a heavyweights' setup holding no stop, the forty-five readings as they stood, and the path's result, benchmark, cost, edge, sessions, end and whether it is settled, with its source and the readings' pinforever, written by the night's step and by the history build, each replacing its own rows, and a row updated as its window closes; a reading the inputs do not reach is null and never nought (see: A setup is every member-session a family's loose gates pass, and its readings are defined once and read as they stood)
Setup nightsone row per index, family and session the ledger read: the members the gates were read over, the setups they passed and those the live rule passesforever, beside the setups, replaced by the night or the build that wrote them; an index the night held no member of has no row (see: A setup is every member-session a family's loose gates pass, and its readings are defined once and read as they stood)
Ledger summariesone row per index, family and year of the setups: how many, how many the live rule passes, how many the night wrote and of those how many its list picked, how many settled, their mean result and edge, and the cut points between the deciles of eachrewritten whole for an index by the setup ledger after each night and each build, so the Ledger page draws counts and computes none (see: A setup is every member-session a family's loose gates pass, and its readings are defined once and read as they stood)
Filed factsone row per filer, concept and period of the six measures, revenue, gross profit, operating income, net income, cash from operations and interest expense, each a quarter, nine months or a year, with the figure, the day and the form and accession of the first filing stating itforever, written by the filings refresh, the night's and the whole one by hand, a period inserted only where none is stored, so a later filing stating it again changes nothing; read by the night's ledger (see: The SEC's facts are stored as first filed in a table the night reads, and a setup's business readings read those filed before its session)
Facts pullsone row per filer each time the refresh asked for its facts: the instant, the filing that set the ask off and the facts the answer addedforever, append-only, written by the filings refresh (see: The night refreshes the facts of the members that filed since its last read of the archive's daily index, after the close under its own limit)
Filing daysone row per day of the archive's daily index the refresh read: whether the archive posted one, its filings, the member filers it set off and how many were refreshedforever, written once every member a day set off was refreshed, the newest the day the next read starts after (see: The night refreshes the facts of the members that filed since its last read of the archive's daily index, after the close under its own limit)
Loop runsone row per tester run on an index: the month it is for, the newest session it read, when it started and ended, and how many folds it testedforever, append-only, written by the walk-forward tester; the Loop page reads a month's newest run (see: A change is adopted only on test years the proposal never saw, and a search is judged as a procedure run year by year)
Loop proposalsone row per run, family and proposal tested: the change in words or none, the rule today in words, its unit and units, its blocks, its adjusted p-value and whether it is at or under the bar, the stability screen's counted and better years and whether it held, the paired total with the five largest left out of each side, whether its units are enough, the difference the gate detects four times in five, the folds choosing within a step, and whether it passed, and from 17.5 an exit proposal's finding in wordsforever, append-only, written by the walk-forward tester with its run (see: A proposal passes the tester on a block sign-flip test of its total edge after costs against the current rule, corrected within a run and held to a fixed bar across runs)
Loop testsone row per run, proposal and test year: whether the year is complete, the setting its fold's learning years chose or none, and each side's units and total edge after costs over the yearforever, append-only, written by the walk-forward tester with its run (see: A change is adopted only on test years the proposal never saw, and a search is judged as a procedure run year by year)
Loop findingsone row per run, family and figure of the trade autopsy: the figure's name, its value, the trades it was read over and its words, read off the rule's own finished trades over the whole historyforever, append-only, written by the walk-forward tester with its run (see: The trade autopsy proposes exits of a fixed menu, each tested as the procedure that chose it)
Loop readingsone row per run, family and reading of the ledger's catalogue: the finished listings holding the reading, the winners and the losers among them, each side's median and the mean edge of each tenth of them in the reading's orderforever, append-only, written by the walk-forward tester with its run (see: Winners against losers proposes a condition only where it beats a within-night shuffle of its own search)
Loop modelsone row per run, family and fold of the learned score: the year the fold tests or the year after the history's for the score fitted on all finished data, the first session of the setups it learned on and the session it was cut at, how many it was fitted over, the readings it weighs, its parameters whole as their canonical text with that text's hash, the pin of the code that fitted it and its weight in wordsforever, append-only, written by the walk-forward tester with its run, and read by the decision cards and the Loop page (see: A fitted statistical model is a rule)
Loop referencesone row per run, family and trade of the rule today over the run's test years: the session it was entered on and its edge after costsforever, append-only, written by the walk-forward tester with its run, and read by the live alarm as the rule's reference (see: The live alarm flags a rule whose edge stood under its reference's fifth percentile two periods running)
Loop decisionsone row per word the operator gave on a proposal of a run or on a restore: approved or declined, the reason a decline gave and whenforever, append-only, written by the read surface on the Loop page's presses, and read by the apply step and the Loop page (see: An approved change is applied before the next night from the night's own build, on the index it was approved on alone)
Loop applicationsone row per word the apply step answered: applied or refused, its words and whenforever, append-only, written by the apply step, and read by the Loop page
Provisional settingsone row per change an approval made to an S&P 400 or 600 family: the setting the family stands at from then in the form an approval applies, its words, when it was set and the run and proposal it came fromforever, append-only and never edited, written by the apply step, the newest a family the setting its night reads, and read by the index families, the rule cards, the tester and the Loop page
Alarm periodsone row per index, family and closed period the live alarm read: its units, their mean edge after costs, the floor its reference gave at their count, whether it counted and stood under the floor, the run of counted periods under it, whether the rule was flagged, the reference's run and the night that read itforever, append-only and each written once, by the live alarm, and read by the Loop page and Tonight (see: The live alarm flags a rule whose edge stood under its reference's fifth percentile two periods running)
Kept barsone row per ticker and session the fetcher dropped as it fell out of the year: the bar as it stood, its raw close, and the night that kept itforever, append-only, written in the transaction that drops the bar and read by no night; a setup's path, replayed from them under any exit from the anchor the setup stores (see: The bars the fetcher drops are kept in a table of their own that no night reads, and a setup is stored as its anchor)
Market seriesfor each session a night stored, one row per series holding the index's, the VIX's, a sector fund's or an index or credit fund's open, high, low and close as the provider sent them, and the run that wrote itkept whole, seventeen rows a session, a session held keeping its first row but a fund's, written again where the provider restates its close; apart from the bar store, since no series is a member's, and read by the family evaluator for the registered rules whose market switch reads it and by the heavyweight book for the betas and the funds' returns (see: The night asks for the market series' daily closes once a series, and keeps them apart from the members' bars)
Calendarticker, event date, kind, and the timing the provider files, being before the session, after it, or unstatedthe horizon the fetcher asks for, each night's answer replacing what the window held, so a row the provider no longer files goes; rows fall out as the window moves. What the provider files for the index's own listing and never a date a research pass found (see: A calendar event is fetched once for the whole index, and the calendar holds provider events only)
Pulled historyfor each session a pull reached, one row per name holding its bar in the adjusted form the bar store holds with the unadjusted close beside it, one row per name and earnings print holding the report date and its timing, and, from a surprise pull, one row per name and print holding the figures as filed and the provider's surprise in per cent, and, from a market pull, one row per series and session holding the index's or the VIX's open, high, low and close as the provider sent them, and from a sector funds pull each fund's the same way, and, from a companies pull, one row per name holding its filer, its GICS classification and the day it was delisted and one row per name and quarter holding its share count, the day its balance sheet was filed and the session whose split basis the count is on, and from 15.2 one row per name and quarter holding its net income, operating income and interest expense as filed and the day its income statement was filed, and, from a splits pull, one row per name and split holding its first session on the new basis and the shares one block became, and, from a revenue pull, one row per filer, revenue concept, period and filing holding the figure stated, the day it was filed, its form and its accession, and, from a members pull, one row per wider index and member holding the listing's exchange and the company's name, sector and industry as that index's answer lists them today, and, from a holdings pull, one row per wider index and quarter end holding its fund's filing, the day it was filed and the holdings it listed, and one row per wider index, quarter end and holding of common stock holding the name, CUSIP and ISIN as filed and the provider's code it matched with the key it matched by, the two matched again by a later pull reading its quarter, each row carrying the run id of the pull that wrote ituntil the operator removes the pull, whole, by that id; no night reads any of the twelve tables, so removing one moves nothing a night, a listing, a score or a page read (see: The history pulled before the store's year sits apart from its bars, marked by the pull that wrote it, read by no night and removed whole by that pull) (see: The surprises pulled before the store's year sit beside the pulled prints and are read by no night) (see: The index's and the VIX's daily series are pulled beside the pulled bars, marked by their pull and read by no night) (see: The pulls behind the heavyweights and the context checks store into tables of their own and are read by no night) (see: A wider universe is tested first on today's members, and widened only where a family's edge improves even so and holds on membership as it stood)
Indicators, swings, volume profile, levels, ladders, movesticker, as-of date, the computed valuesone year, recomputed nightly and kept for the harness, each table's own writer dropping the rows that fall out of the window on the night they fall out (see: Every computed table's writer is its own deleter)
Listingsone row per name per night, for every name in the index and not only the listed ones: which reasons fired if any, the values that made each true or false, and the plan as it stood that nightforever; this is your own record and no provider can sell it back
List rulesone row per session the swing filter drew the list for: the session and the rule, an evening holding no row having been listed by the six reasonsforever; recorded by the night close in the filter's step, so a night that stops at a later step still reads as the filter drew it (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it)
Family resultsone row per session, member and setup family but the pullback: whether the member passed, how many of the family's gates it missed, its place among the names the family passed, the trade it is bought on, the figure the family's order reads, the exclusions its series carries, the family's gates in order with their reasons and values, and from 13.9 each registered rule of the family's verdict in shadow with the values that made ita row that passed forever, since it is a trade its family's record counts; a row that did not, until its session is older than the bars the store keeps, since nothing reads a near miss whose bars are gone; a night run again replaces its own rows, and the pullback's answers are the swing filter's gate results (see: Tonight's page is drawn from setup families, each a rule of its own listing at most five a night)
Family nightsone row per session the setup families drew the page's list for: the session and the families on the page that night, in the page's orderforever; recorded by the family lister in the swing filter's step whether or not any stock is listed, so a night the families drew and listed nothing on is told from one drawn before them, and an earlier night's page is drawn with the families it held (see: Tonight's page is drawn from setup families, each a rule of its own listing at most five a night)
Family picksone row per session, stock and family that passed it: listed, with its place down the page and the other families it qualified under, or held back, being listed under an earlier family, holding a trade still open with the family and the night that listed it, or past its family's fiveforever; a night run again replaces its own rows, and a trade's outcome is the forward return of its stock and session under its family's horizon (see: A stock holds one trade across every swing family, and one qualifying under two is listed once under the first in the page's order)
Family tradesone row per registered family rule, stock and session it was kept on: the family, its place on the rule's own list, the buy, the stop and the target where its plan names one, the stop's distance in the night's typical moves, the reward to risk, its cap, and once it ends the session it ended on and its result in multiples of its risk, with the benchmark of the same plan on every member that night and how many members it was read over once the cap's sessions have passed, and from 15.2 its round trip at the published table in multiples of its risk, its company valued as the member readings read it on its night, beside its result and never in it, and from 17.5 the exit of the menu it is walked under where its rule names one (see: Every engine's settings hooks land together and all default off, so the families' pins move once)forever, since a rule's record is its trades; a night run again replaces the trades it kept that night and no other night's, and a trade's end and benchmark are written once (see: A registered family rule is evaluated every night at its own settings and keeps its own list, its trades stored with their benchmark when they end)
Heavyweight nightsone row per rebalance session, sector and place among the sector's largest companies: the listing held for the company and the company it belongs to, its value, its return over the look-back, the sector's, its lead, whether it passed the trend gate, whether it was bought as one of the sector's leaders, and its betaforever; recorded by the heavyweight book in the swing filter's step on each rebalance of the page's book, a night run again replacing its own session's rows and no other's (see: The sector heavyweights hold the largest companies leading their sectors, rotated on the first session of each month whose stored year holds the closes their readings need)
Heavyweight holdingsone row per stock and the session the sector heavyweights bought it on: its sector and company, the close it was bought at, its growth and its size cut's carried each night with the session each was carried to, and once sold the session, the close, why, its result and its size cut's returnforever, the page's book, which the card and Past picks draw; a night run again deletes what it bought that night and opens again what it sold that night (see: A heavyweight's result is the product of its daily close ratios since its buy, carried each night)
Heavyweight rule nightsone row per registered heavyweights rule, rebalance session, sector and place among the sector's largest companies at the rule's size cut, the same as a heavyweight night'sforever; recorded by the heavyweight book for each registered rule's own book on each of its rebalances, a night run again replacing its own session's rows and no other's (see: Each registered sector heavyweights rule keeps a book of its own beside the page's, its holdings scored in percent against their size cut)
Heavyweight rule holdingsone row per registered heavyweights rule, stock and the session the rule bought it on, the same as a heavyweight holding'sforever, each rule's record, which the run page reads over blocks of 63 sessions by the session each holding ended on; a night run again deletes what each rule bought that night and opens again what each sold that night (see: Each registered sector heavyweights rule keeps a book of its own beside the page's, its holdings scored in percent against their size cut)
Forward returnsticker, listing date, five and twenty-one session outcomes, and the base rate for the same window; the setup's outcome on the listing's plan; and for every swing filter row, each plan it carries scored over the setup's cap and over twenty sessions as context (see: A swing filter row carries both swing plans, each scored from the night's close, and a candidate's setups are scored on the plan its own trade gate reads)forever
Factsticker, as-of date, the facts file, its hashkept whole for every night the name was listed, each night read by the rule that listed it (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it); every other night keeps the hash and the material changes, with the payload emptied by the change detector. Being opened is not one of the conditions, because nothing records that a name was read
Fundamentalsticker, the quarters, balance sheet, segments, guidance, with the filing date each came from; and beside the filings one copy a fetch of the parts that are as of the fetch rather than a filing, the newest of which is read over the newest filing's ownforever, because providers restate and this is what you knew at the time, and a copy is what a price-dependent figure was on the day it was fetched (see: A regenerated report is written whole by the paid model from the company's figures as they stand on the day it runs, once a name a day)
Reported quartersone row per member per fetch per quarter, over the twelve newest a fetch returns: the period end, the filing and report dates, the revenue, operating income, net income and operating cash flow, the earnings a share and its estimate, and the figures worked out at the fetch from the whole answer, being the four quarters' earnings a share, sales and the operating margin against a year earlier with the same quarter's figures a year before, and the close on the first session after the report, with the fetch's newest session and its close, and the shares the quarter's balance sheet files, on the fetch's split basis, and from 15.2 the interest expense the quarter files with whether the fetch read one, a quarter stored before reading noneforever; a fetch's rows are read together and never mixed with another's, because the provider restates per-share figures and adjusts its closes as of the day it is asked (see: Reported quarters are stored per fetch, so every quarter a reading reads shares one fetch's per-share basis)
Quarter asksone row per member per night asked: why it was asked, being the fill, its first night in the index, the first night after a report or an ask again, the quarter awaited, what came of it, the quarters it stored and the weighted calls it spentforever; the schedule reads it, and a night run again keeps the ask it made (see: A member's reported quarters are fetched on the night after it reports, and asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that until the quarter is posted)
Member companiesone row per member per storing quarters fetch: its filer at the filings archive and its GICS sector, industry group, industry and sub-industry, as the provider files them, and from 15.2 the analysts' five rating counts the same answer filesforever, never updated; the sector heavyweights read each member's newest (see: The night values a member from its newest fetch, tonight's close brought to the count's basis by the fetch's own close)
Fundamental readingsone row per member per night: the state, the newest quarter read from, the fetch read from, a newer quarter awaited, and the four readings, each with the quarters it was read over and what was absent where it could not be readforever; Past picks draws the state a trade carried on its night and a night's list is ordered by its own rows, and a night run again replaces its own set whole (see: Four readings of a member's reported quarters are worked out every night by rules the measured split settled, and its state is read from sales and operating margin alone)
Member readingsone row per index, session and member of the S&P 500, 400 and 600: its close as traded, its dollar volume, its company's value, a round trip at its close in per cent at the published table and at double, the profit gate, the coverage, its quarters' state, its year's high with the sessions since it and the close's nearness to it, its volume over its average, and its industry with that industry's S&P 500 members' return over a month and a quarter and their mean surprise before the nightforever; a night run again replaces its own session's rows and no other's, and a member whose series holds a hole keeps its row with none of the readings its bars give (see: A 400 or 600 trade pays the published effective spread for its size and price, and its pass tests read the edge after it)
Switch readingsone row per session: IJH's and IJR's adjusted closes against SPY's over half a year and a year of sessions, and HYG's against its average over the fifty sessions to it and against its close a quarter before, each none where a close it reads is missingforever; a night run again replaces its own row (see: The 400 and 600 rules start provisional with liquidity floors and a profit gate before any testing)
Index heavyweight rule nightsone row per registered sector heavyweights rule of the S&P 400 or 600 and each session its own book rebalanced on: how many it bought and how many it sold there for no longer being boughtforever; a rule's last row is its last rebalance, a rebalance waiting for what its design reads writes none, and a night run again replaces its own row (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's sector heavyweights keeps a book of its own in either design, read by the index families' step)
Index heavyweight rule holdingsone row per registered sector heavyweights rule of the S&P 400 or 600, stock and the session its own book bought it on, the same as an index heavyweight holding's, with its round trip at the published table its company's value as the member readings read it on its buyforever, each rule's record, which the index's Run page reads by the session each holding ended on; a night run again deletes what each rule bought that night and opens again what each sold that night (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's sector heavyweights keeps a book of its own in either design, read by the index families' step)
Index rule tradesone row per registered rule of an S&P 400's or 600's swing family, stock and session it was kept on: the index, the family, its place on the rule's own list, the buy, the stop, the target or the trail its plan names, its cap, the stop's distance in the night's typical moves and the reward to risk, and once it ends the session it ended on, its result in multiples of its risk and its round trip at the published table beside it and never in it, with the benchmark of the same plan on every member of the index that night and how many members it was read over once the cap's sessions have passed, and from 17.5 the exit of the menu it is walked under where its rule names oneforever, since a rule's record is its trades; a night run again replaces the trades it kept that night and no other night's, and a trade's end and benchmark are written once (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's swing families is registered as the family on its index and evaluated by their step alone)
Decision cardsone row per index, night, family and stock a family listed or an index's sector heavyweights' book bought: its place, the plan's prices, the rule it names, the card's values it was read with, its checklist's lines each with its verdict and words, the rule's record as the card read it, and from 17.7 the pick's rank under its index's learned score where the score passed there and its part of setups like the pick or why none were matchedforever, each night's cards as they were read; a night run again replaces its own cards and no other night's (see: A pick's card advises on the trade and removes no pick, and code computes every figure on it)
Rule nightsone row per index, night, family and rule standing when the night started, live or variant, or replayed by the record command: whether the night evaluated it, how many it listed with zeros, how many members passed each of its gates and every gate before, its empty stretch and the mark its past empty nights set with the completed stretches and the sessions the mark was counted over, and whether the row came from the night or the historyforever; a night run again replaces its own rows and the record command's replay writes over the history's (see: A card's stretch line counts its mark over past empty nights and draws none under thirty completed stretches)
Rule picksone row per index, rule, stock and night a rule whose list no other table keeps, the swing filter's variants, kept a pick on: its place, the plan's prices and reward to risk, its cap, the figures that listed it, and its end and result as the walk ends itforever; a night run again replaces its own picks and the ends it wrote (see: A variant's picks are shown on its card when chosen and its results only under its tests)
Forming rowsone row per index, night, breakout rule and place a member forming a breakout stands at: the member, its close, the price it would have to close above, how far under it in its typical moves, the volume the rule would need and tonight's, its ranges' ratio, the gates it still fails, its next report where one falls within the window, and how many were formingforever, at most the stated rows a rule a night; a night run again replaces its own (see: The forming list advises and never lists a stock)
Rule recordsone row per index and family a card names: the rule replayed and its one setting, when, the history's first and last session and its membership, the unit, the trades, the share that ended at its target, the mean result after costs, the median sessions held, how many ended at each session held, and the median worst closeuntil the rule recorder runs again for its index, which writes over it, as a freeze's remedy does (see: A rule's record is replayed at its one setting by the sweep's own code over the pulled history, after costs on every index)
Taken tradesone row per trade the operator took from a pick's card: the card it came from, the stock's sector, its fill and the session it is for, whether the fill is still the plan's buy and whether the operator entered it, the stop, target, trail and cap it is managed by, and the exit the operator recorded; never the account's size, its risk or its capforever, the operator's own record, written by the card's presses alone; a row is removed only by the Not taken press before a night has followed it (see: A taken trade's fill is the next session's open once its bar is stored, and the plan's buy marked provisional until then)
Taken recordsone row per index and family the operator took a trade under: the unit, the trades won at the target and lost at the stop where the rule sets a target, every trade ended, those open, and the average result once twenty have ended; and the same over the rule's own picks listed on the nights the operator took one, each followed from the plan's buywritten whole each night by the follower over every trade taken (see: The operator's own record states its average result once twenty of its trades in a family and index have ended)
Dividend readingsone row per member and quarters fetch whose answer files a dividend: the forward rate a share, the last declared ex-date and each year's count of dividendsforever, each fetch's as it answered (see: A pick's next ex-dividend date is the calendar's where it declares one and the last declared date plus the usual interval where it does not)
Estimate readingsone row per member per night the night asked for its estimates: the end of its current fiscal year, the consensus estimate of the year's earnings a share and the same estimate 30 days before as the answer filed them, or why it read none, and the run that askedforever, never updated, the only history of what the revisions variant read since the provider keeps none; a night run again reads its row back and asks nothing (see: The night asks for the estimates of each member a rule reading them passes on everything else, once a member a night)
News pulseticker, date, article countone year, enough to hold a baseline
News articlesticker, article id, link, title, source, published instant, text cut at the instruction's length, length as delivered, admissibility, session first storedthirty-one days, a day past the thirty the labeller reads
News labelsticker, article id, profile, instruction version, model as the provider answered, outcome, cause of an unreadable answer, kind, direction, reason, labelled at, runwith its article; never overwritten, a switch writing rows of its own
Research storeticker, and one row per section holding its prose, its own as-of date, the model that wrote it, its source list, the version it replaced, and for the risks the fields its prose was composed fromforever, every version
Theme storetheme, as-of date, prose, sources, and which industries map to itforever, every version
Source documentsurl, fetched date, title, textforever; a claim whose source is missing is not rendered
Candidate registercandidate, its rule, its test, the evaluator the code carries that will run it, the parameters it will be run with, that evaluator's version, the date registered, and for a retirement a new row naming what it retiresforever; append-only, no update and no delete, refused by the table itself and not only by what writes to it
Rule versionsrule, version, the parameters it is replayed with, a hash of those with the code version, when its window opened and, once closed, when, the evidence it was closed on and what replaced it where a version didforever; a closed window is kept beside the one that replaced it, because the scores written under it are of the rule as it stood then
Version scoresticker, night, rule, version, the window it belongs to, the plan that version produced, and whether the score counts or was written in sample by a backfillone year, dropped by the scorer on the night the rows fall out of the window
Peer readingsone row per name: the session the readings were taken at, the group its moves are read against, the year's high and how far the close sits below it, the return over sixty sessions and the bars both were read overthe newest night alone, written again every night by the move annotator, which deletes the row of a name holding no bars or whose series has a gap (see: Every computed table's writer is its own deleter)
Earnings reactionsone row per name and print: the report date, when in the session it was reported, the session it moved on, the estimate and the actual as the provider filed them, the provider's surprise and that session's movethe calendar's year behind, written again every night by the move annotator, which deletes a print that falls out of the calendar or out of the stored bars' reach (see: Every computed table's writer is its own deleter)
Swing readingsone row per member per night: the bars read, each return over 63 and 126 sessions with its place among the members' returns and the mean of the two, the highest high of the last 20 sessions with the session making it and the sessions since, the pullback from it in typical days' moves, the volume while it came down, the tightness of the range, and the reason where a member was read over nothingone year, written again whole for its night on every run and dropped by the swing reader on the night the rows fall out of the window (see: Every computed table's writer is its own deleter)
Market readingsone row per night: the members, the share of those read closing above their own 200-day average with how many it was counted over, the same over the 50-day average as context, and the median of their volume against the fifty-day averageone year, dropped by the swing reader with the name rows
Gate resultsone row per member per night: each gate's pass, the setup's family, whether the trigger's event happened and whether it arrived, the trade read from the ladder's first tranche, from the swing trade at the nearest bands with its entry, stop and target, and from section 10's plan for it with its stop and target, each with its reward to risk and the stop's distance in typical moves, the exclusions, whether it passes and its rank among the names passing, the filter version and the code it ran under, and each gate's reason and values, and from 12.5 each standing swing family candidate's verdict in shadow with the values that made itforever; a gate's near misses are read over the years the edge clock needs, and the readings behind them are dropped after one. A night run again replaces its own rows and no other night's
Filter versionsone row per version of the swing filter's settings: the settings, when it was opened and closed, and the evidence it was opened onforever; none is open until the operator's shape command opens the first, and the filter runs on section 17's proposed values until then

Key. The single page app, the report exporter and the comparison files have empty rows because they touch no store directly; everything they show arrives through the read API, which is the only component allowed to read across all of them. Three further facts carry the integrity argument. Only the bar fetcher and the corporate action checker write bars, so price history cannot be altered by anything downstream. The pulled history column holds bars the operator pulled for the years before the store's own, and no component but the history pull touches it, which is what lets a pull be removed whole without moving any figure a night computed. Only the research components write research, and the claim checker sits between the runner and what is served. That gate is the status on the row and the split of one table's operations between two owners, not a column of its own: the writers insert a section as pending and only the checker updates its status, which `writer-ownership` asserts in both directions. It was written in the catalogue as a research store pending and a research store until 6.0, which is two stores in a sentence and one column here, so the property a reader most needs to see was the one the matrix could not carry. The read API and the app write nothing but the log, so no rendering bug can corrupt stored data. Its cell under the candidate register was the one store it did not read, because at 8.3 nothing drew a registered candidate on any screen and a read declared before there is a surface for it is a permission nobody exercised; 8.4 built the run page's region that states how many candidates are registered and the divisor that number sets, and the cell filled with it. What it reads there is the register and never a shadow evaluation of a name, which is what keeps the row full and the screens empty of one. The registrar's own row reads the register as well as writing it, which is what refusing a change to a candidate that stands registered requires: the refusal is a question about what the register already holds. The read API's two cells under rule versions and version scores were blank for the reason its register cell was blank at 8.3, and 10.4 built the run page's versions region, which draws each open window, what each version labelled tonight's names and the record of its difference from the live rule, so the two cells filled with it. The cells stayed blank through 10.4 and the 10.4 correction filled them. A read the code makes and the declaration leaves out passes every reconciliation that starts from the declaration, and the ladder builder's read of the membership stood that way from 4.1 to its correction, so `component-access` also reads each component's own queries and holds every table they read to what the component declares it reads. What reaches a screen there is a count of names and a record over blocks, never a counterfactual plan and never a name. The scorer reads the versions it writes, because opening a window is a question about which windows are already open. The forward returns column holds the family trades beside the forward returns, each a record of what became of a trade: the family recorder alone writes the family trades, and the read API reads them for the run page. The run log is a store rather than a component and so has no row of its own. The verification harness reads none of the stores in this matrix: it reads this document, the code and the fixture, including the fixture's own store, and never a store under the data root. The distinction is written here because it is the one a later reader would otherwise widen back, and a check that reads the live store is a check whose result depends on last night.

The bars column holds the index's, the VIX's, the sector funds' and the index and credit funds' daily series beside the members' bars, each a fetched series of sessions. The market series fetcher alone writes the series, the family evaluator reads the index's and the VIX's and the heavyweight book reads the index's and the funds', so no stage that reads a member's bars for its own figures finds any, and the read API reads none (see: The night asks for the market series' daily closes once a series, and keeps them apart from the members' bars). The listings column holds each registered heavyweights rule's rebalance readings beside the page's book's, and the forward returns column each rule's holdings beside the page's, which the heavyweight book alone writes and the read API reads for the run page's records (see: Each registered sector heavyweights rule keeps a book of its own beside the page's, its holdings scored in percent against their size cut). The fundamentals column holds the estimates the night asked for, which the estimates fetcher alone writes (see: The night asks for the estimates of each member a rule reading them passes on everything else, once a member a night). The watch list column holds the operator's taken trades beside the watch list, each the operator's own record written by a press, which the read API alone writes and no component that picks a stock reads (see: A taken trade's fill is the next session's open once its bar is stored, and the plan's buy marked provisional until then).

17. Limits, spend and the numbers the harness asserts

Each row is a claim this document makes about the code. The harness parses this table and fails a build that exceeds any of them. Values marked as proposed are not yet confirmed and must be settled before the phase that depends on them.

LimitValueReasonAsserted by
Model calls in the nightly run0 in the arithmetic, being every step up to the close, and none in the quarters step after it, with the queue carved out by name and making local calls only, and the night's own request after it making none, and the labeller the night starts after the close being a process of its own whose calls are on its own run and never the night's (see: The nightly run is arithmetic only) (see: The night's zero-model-call rule bounds the arithmetic, and the overnight queue is carved out of it by name) (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own)the whole design rests on the nightly half being free, and the carve is what keeps that true where the queue makes it false as written. The queue's calls are local and cost nothing, it runs after the arithmetic has closed and recorded its counts, and no figure above it moves whether it ran or not. Carved rather than loosened, for the reason the per-name row's own carve-outs state: a night that called a paid model for every name would satisfy a loosened rule and defeat the designrun log, on the arithmetic's stages
Per-name network calls in the nightly run0 in the steady state, with the backfill, the corporate action refetch, the quarters fetch after the close, the night's own requests and the estimates of each member a rule reading them passes on everything else carved out of it, the requests making none on the night's own rows and their passes making their own on the drain's runs (see: The six reports a night are taken in turn across the three indices, one at a time in the page's order) (see: A member's reported quarters are fetched on the night after it reports, and asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that until the quarter is posted) (see: The night asks for the estimates of each member a rule reading them passes on everything else, once a member a night)bars arrive in one bulk file and news in one feed request, so a night does not grow with the universe. The backfill is the one exception and is bounded rather than nightly: it makes one request per name holding no history, which is every name on the first run and a new joiner afterwards, and never again for a name that already holds its year. A name it stored nothing for is asked for again on each of the 5 nights after the first and then every 7 days until one stores its year or the name leaves the index, which is bounded by the names the provider cannot serve rather than by the universe (see: A name the backfill stored nothing for is asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that, and its page and the run page say so until one stores its year). Written here because the limit as first stated forbade the step the run order carries at position two, and a check reading it would have failed on a rule nobody meant. The corporate action refetch is the second exception and was found at 1.6 by the same route: it makes one request per name whose adjusted prices an action moved, and a name whose refetch failed is asked for again on each of the 5 nights after the one that marked it and then every 7 days until a refetch succeeds or the name leaves the index, a failure on a night an action lands on it starting the count again, so one action costs 6 requests over the 6 nights from the one it lands on and 1 every 7 days after that however long its failure lasts. That is bounded by the actions of the day and of the 5 nights before it, and by one request every 7 days for each name whose retries are spent, rather than by the universe, and on the fixture's captured day it is one name in five hundred. A member back after sessions in no index the night reads is asked for once on its first night back, its year replaced as an action's is, which is bounded by the names returning rather than by the universe (see: A member that returns after sessions in no index the night reads has its year asked for again whole). A member whose stored year misses a session the exchange traded before its newest stored bar is asked for once for the newest session missing, which is bounded by the sessions the price file did not carry rather than by the universe, one member of the 1,506 on the morning of 2026-10-05 (see: A member missing a session the exchange traded has its year asked for again whole, once for the newest session missing). A name whose retries are spent stays suspect, and its name page, its row on tonight's list and the run page say so until a refetch succeeds (see: A suspect name is asked for again on the five nights after it is marked and weekly after that, and its own page, its row on tonight's list and the run page say so until a refetch succeeds). It is carved rather than the rule loosened, because a night that refetched every name would satisfy a loosened rule and defeat the whole design. The quarters fetch is the fourth exception and follows the reporting calendar rather than the index: a member is asked on the first night after it reports, again on each of the 5 nights after while its new quarter is not yet posted and then every 7 days until it is, and every member once at the start, at most 260 a night, so over the 1,994 reports the calendar held for the 262 weekdays before 2026-09-27 it asks about four times a member a year. It runs after the close, bounded by its own limit and by the day's allowance rather than by the night's deadline, and no figure the arithmetic computes moves whether it ran. The estimates are the sixth exception and follow what a rule reading them passes rather than the index: once a member a night, in the swing filter's step, one to three members on the pullback's nights so far, each stored and read back rather than asked for againrun log, on the steady-state stages

Judged in the opposite order to the one that sentence reads in, being the kind first and the date second, because three of the five refusable pages the 6.3 measurement read carried no publish date at all, so a build that judged the date first would refuse most of what it refuses for the cheapest reason available and would report almost nothing about the kinds (see: Each denied category is refused by a marker the document carries, and the domain is never one of them). A page carries an article where one paragraph of it runs to at least 3 sentences and at least 40 words, and a page exists to open an account where it carries at least 1 regulatory risk warning, or a leveraged-product term beside at least 1 invitation to open one. Invitation language alone is not a marker, which 411 articles from one live request measured: one of them is an article about saving that says both opening an account and sign up, and none of the five carrying a leveraged-product term carries any invitation at alla search by company name returns all four kinds, and each would satisfy the bare rule that a claim must name a stored source. Provenance shows where a sentence came from, not whether the document deserved belief. The test is applied per document after the fetch and never per publisher (see: Admissibility is judged per document, after the fetch, and never per publisher)a fixture of denied documents, each of which must be refused and must therefore leave its claim unwritten
Nightly row coveragea listings row is written for every name in the index every night, whether or not a reason fired (see: Candidate conditions are registered before they are scored, and a candidate's picks are shown on the Run page while its outcomes wait for a look)a shadow candidate has to be evaluated on the nights it would have fired, and most of those are nights no live reason surfaced that name. Writing rows only for listed names would make section 13's shadow mechanism impossible without anything announcing it. The cost is about twelve megabytes a yearrow count per night equals the index size
Reason record displaya reason's measured record is shown beside the reason, and a rule's on a pick's card under the rule's own heading naming the rule and its index, and neither as the stock's own; below the minimum only the count of resolved setups that set a bar against the minimum is shown; at or above it, the share, the denominator and the break-even are shown together or not at all (see: A rule's record is drawn under the rule's own heading, beside its reason or on a pick's card and never as the stock's own)a bare number next to a stock is read as that stock's chance of going up, when it is a historical frequency of the rule across every name it pickedan app test at each of the three states
Setup resolutiona listed setup starts on the first close at or below its entry zone's top edge and resolves when its target is reached, its stop is closed through, or 63 sessions pass from the listing; a timed-out setup and one whose price never reached that entry are each counted in their own column and never as a win (see: An unresolved setup is never a win) (see: A setup is scored from its entry, and a target reached before the entry is never a win); the plan is read at the listing session's adjustment, so a split or dividend restating the closes moves the plan with them, and an outcome once decided is never written again (see: An outcome once decided is never rewritten, and a setup still in play is scored with its plan scaled by its listing session's adjustment factor)a setup that has done nothing is neither right nor wrong, and scoring it either way flatters or punishes a condition for a trade that never happened. Same principle as unexamined never counting as a passresolution unit tests, one per outcome, and the filler's stored rows over constructed stores restated and cut back after the listing
Minimum resolved setups250 resolved setups that set a bar, spread over at least 60 distinct listing sessions, each contributing at least one, before a verdict is reported at all, and the same two before the Past picks screen draws the share of the live list's trades that reached their target, counted over its trades decided at the target or the stop and the nights they were listed on (see: Every trade the live list recommended is shown, and their share waits for the minimum the reason records wait for); 400 before a live condition may be retired (see: An unresolved setup is never a win) (see: A reason's share, verdict and both floors are counted over the resolved setups that set a bar) (see: A live reason is added or retired only by a change to section 11 and the code together, and the register holds candidates alone)separating a reason that clears its break-even by ten points from one that does not, at a threshold corrected for a family of nine, needs a few hundred independent resolved setups. Listings cluster by sector and by date, so the effective count is below the row count and these are floors rather than targets, which is why the sessions are a floor of their own: a count of rows alone can be filled by a handful of nights of one market move, and 60 is the quarter of trading the bands look back over. The earlier figures of 50 and 100 were set without this arithmetic and would have licensed verdicts the data cannot support. The retirement bar is higher because removing a reason is harder to undo than leaving one alonethe run page must show the count beside every verdict and withhold the verdict below either floor, naming the one that is short, and the Past picks screen must draw its count against both and no share below either; no page computes the retirement floor, which is read against that count
Family size and correctioncandidate conditions are registered in advance in an append-only table, with a maximum family size of 9, counted over each setup family's own rules; the family's divisor, the candidates of its setup family standing before a window opened, is shown with the verdict beside the count of distinct trials a candidate's level is divided by (see: Candidate conditions are registered before they are scored, and a candidate's picks are shown on the Run page while its outcomes wait for a look) (see: Each setup family's correction for luck counts its own rules alone, at most nine a family)with five worthless candidates the chance one clears an ordinary test is about 23%, with nine 37%, and with twenty it is 64%. Nine is the operator's of 2026-10-02, one past the eight first ruled, to register the night's best three beside the pullback's eight. Correcting is what stops the best of several noise processes being read as a discoverythe harness asserts the register accepts no update, delete or replace, and that the divisor used matches the number of candidates standing before the window opened, a name retired and registered again once (see: A candidate stands by the last row naming it, and a name retired and registered again stands once)
Distinct trialsthe level at Holm's first step is 0.05 over the distinct trials, each a rule whose results a look has read or that is still running: a registration of the same rule where only the version it reads changed is the trial it replaces, a rule with any threshold or condition moved is a trial of its own, a candidate retired with no result of its own read is counted in none, and a look is read at the count as of the night it was read (see: Holm's level passes between the candidates by a graph fixed when they are registered, and its first step is 0.05 over the distinct trials read at a look or still running)the level is shared across every trial for the life of the system rather than given fresh to each window, so at every look the levels the counted trials hold sum to 0.05; a rule nobody read cannot have been chosen on its luckthe harness asserts the count over a register written back from the operator's store, which counts its sixteen names as fifteen rules and six trials, that a re-registration with only its version moved is the trial it replaces and a candidate retired unread leaves the count, and that a look keeps the bar of the count as of its night
Significance threshold0.05, one-sided, divided by the family the reason belongs to, and the divisor is shown with the verdict; the six live reasons are one family of 6 and registered candidates are the other, at most 9 (see: A verdict tests a reason's wins against each of its setups' own break-even at a corrected threshold) (see: The significance threshold is divided by the family size, and the divisor is shown)one-sided because the question is whether a reason beat the bar its own plans set rather than whether it differed from it, and divided because running several conditions and keeping whichever looks best is the standard way a self-improving system makes itself worse while appearing to learn. The null is that each resolved setup wins with the probability its own plan demanded, which makes the wins a Poisson binomial rather than a binomial, and the exact tail is computed from the stored break-evensthe exact tail asserted against cases worked by hand, the binomial at the mean asserted to bound it where a clearing verdict sits, and the divisor read off the run page beside every verdict
Blocks a record is judged over63 consecutive exchange sessions to a block, counted from the first session of the record and keyed on the session a setup was listed on; a block counts once it holds a setup whose whole outcome window has closed, and nothing is compared below a floor of 8 such blocks (see: A candidate is judged by a sign-flip test over blocks of 63 sessions, with at least eight blocks) (see: A listing records the band strength the old order read, and the three orders are compared over the nights that recorded it)setups listed less than a block apart resolve over shared bars and are not independent, and a sign-flip test over a count of blocks cannot give a p-value below one over two to that power, so too few blocks can never rejectrun page test over constructed listings either side of a block edge and of a closed window
Looks a candidate's verdict is read at8, 12 and 16 non-empty blocks, information fractions of a half, three quarters and the whole, triggered by the block count alone; the level is spent across them by a Lan-DeMets function of the O'Brien-Fleming type, and a look's boundary is found over every arrangement of the signs of the blocks it holds. The first look cannot promote, since the level it releases is below the smallest p-value 8 blocks can produce (see: A candidate's verdict is read only at looks fixed when it is registered, with each look's boundary found over every sign vector its blocks allow)a fixed-level test repeated as setups accumulate promotes a worthless condition far more often than its level says, and the looks are what keep the level the level
The calibrated bareach resolved setup's bar is simulated over 4000 paths from the fill it was scored from, under the scatter of its name's last 63 session changes, capped at the sessions its own window left, from a seed of 20260922 taken with the name and the session so a bar is the same whichever night computed it; a round trip of 10 basis points is carried in the bar and 30 is shown beside it (see: A setup's null win probability is calibrated from its own plan, and its planned break-even is shown beside it) (see: The calibrated null carries a round trip of ten basis points, and thirty is shown as a sensitivity)a plan's stated break-even assumes the exit lands exactly on the stop or the target, and both are judged on closes, so a condition with tight stops could clear the planned bar while making nothing
The three candidates' numbersarrived and narrow at a zone no wider than 1 typical daily move, and volume against the night at a ratio above 2 times the night's median ratio and above that multiple on its own, each marked proposed; crossed by a margin at 0.5 of a typical move past the edge the close went through, settled on the per-night counts rather than proposed, so a change to it is a new registration; the three written by one command at one instant, so each opens at a third of the level (see: The three candidates are registered at one instant) (see: Nothing a candidate or a version is registered with changes while it runs, and a proposed number is settled only by a new registration)a number a condition was registered at is what the record afterwards is a record of, so it is written in the register row and in code rather than typed at the promptcandidate-conditions
Power stated at a lookthe smallest excess a look could detect is stated at 80% power, on the level that look spends and the design effect the record measures, beside the excess observed; re-derived before registration on the calibrated null measured over the store's own setups, a mean of 0.43, the second look at a design effect of one detects 3.26 points of excess for arrived and narrow, 2.61 for volume against the night and 1.43 for crossed by a margin, and the first look detects nothing at all, since the smallest p-value eight blocks can produce sits above the level it spends (see: Power is stated for the looks that exist as well as for a single read)a look that found nothing is worth reading only beside how much there would have had to be
Rule versions scored at onceat most 2 windows of the merge distance and 4 of each of the other 4 ladder rules, each rule's live window among them, which is 18 at once, settled by the operator with the night's deadline; a version is opened only beside its rule's live window, and the live window is what the night already computes and is no extra replay (see: A ladder rule's version is measured beside that rule's live window, and both count against a bound of eighteen)the arithmetic is the night of 2026-09-14: 495 seconds over the steps before the close, a level stage of 143 seconds and a ladder stage of 5 at 504 names, so a merge distance version costs 148 seconds and every other version 5. The fullest register the caps admit replays 1 merge distance version and 12 others, 208 seconds, which puts the night at 703 seconds against a deadline of 7200. The merge distance has the lower cap because its versions replay the level stage, each one costing more than every other version the register admits together; the other caps stop one rule taking the whole budget and leaving the rest unversioned. 18 is the sum of the caps. It grows with versions times names and never with a requestthe window past each rule's cap refused and admitted one below, the worst case computed from the night's own stage durations and held inside the deadline, and `nightly-cost` over a recorded night at one version and at the fullest register
