Operator's record minimumthe operator's record of a family on an index draws its average result once 20 of its trades have ended, and before that a dashed outline saying how many have (see: The operator's own record states its average result once twenty of its trades in a family and index have ended)three or four trades' average says more about the weeks they were taken in than about the operator's choices, and the rules' own minimum would take a personal record yearsfixture-expectations, the record worked by hand at nineteen ended and at twenty
Card hold with no capa pick's card reads what could hit a holding with no cap, the sector heavyweights', over the 21 sessions after the night, to the book's next rebalance (see: Market events inside a hold are read from a committed table of the Fed's and the BLS's own dates, and asked of no provider)a heavyweight is read again at the next month's rebalance, its first session or the first after it whose stored year holds the closes its readings need, so a month is the hold the card can speak tofixture-expectations, the hold's end worked by hand at three, twenty-one and sixty-three sessions and with no cap

18. Failure behaviour

Every row is a claim the harness tests by inducing the failure against the fixture.

FailureWhat the system doesWhat you seeWhy this and not the alternative
Bulk price feed unavailablekeeps last night's bars, writes nothing, names the step and the reason on the run log, marks every name stale and still serves the app (see: A feed is unavailable when it does not answer, and wrong when it answers with something else)the run log carries the step that stopped and why; the banner gives the data date, and tonight's list is absent rather than wronga list computed from yesterday's bars would look current and be false. Unavailable is a refused connection, a request past its timeout, a rejected rate or the provider's own fault: every one of those is a night that did not happen, as against an answer that arrived and is wrong, which is refused instead
A feed answers with a session other than the one asked forthe payload is refused before anything is stored, the stored series is left exactly as it was, and the run log names the session that arrived and the one that was asked for (see: A feed is unavailable when it does not answer, and wrong when it answers with something else)the banner gives the data date, which is still last night's, and tonight's list is absent rather than wronga night answered with yesterday's file makes one request and logs no error, and the bars it stores are ones the store already holds, so nothing downstream would notice. It is the failure that reports green. The feed can ask this question because it knows the session it asked for and the payload declares the session it is
A feed answers with none of the index in itthe payload is refused before anything is stored; a file carrying nothing for some members but not all is stored for the members it does carry, and the run log names how many it carried nothing for and the first few of them by ticker (see: A feed is unavailable when it does not answer, and wrong when it answers with something else)the banner gives the data date and tonight's list is absent rather than shorta file holding none of the index is the wrong file or a session the exchange has not traded, and that is not the same as a file with no rows: the payload can be full of symbols this index does not hold. Refusing on any absence at all was the first rule written here and the first live night over five hundred names refuted it, two of 503 being absent from an ordinary day. A name the file carries nothing for has no bar tonight, which is that name's own shorter history. Only the fetcher can ask this, because the feed does not know which names the index holds, which is why it is refused in a different place from the wrong session
A feed answers with a row the reader cannot reada row for a symbol the index does not hold is passed over and counted on the fetch line with its reason kept; a row for a current member refuses the night before anything is stored, naming the ticker and what arrived (see: A feed is unavailable when it does not answer, and wrong when it answers with something else)the run log carries the step that stopped and the member and the reason; the banner gives the data datethe file is the whole exchange and the store holds the index, so a fund's fractional volume is not this index's business, and the provider sends them: six of 50,249 rows on 2026-09-08. Refusing the file for one of them refused the night for every name with a message that named nothing, which read as the provider serving something other than prices for an older session. A volume is never rounded to make a row readable, because a figure the code changed is not the provider's
A session the night finds missingeach session the exchange traded between the newest one a night's bulk file stored and tonight's is fetched in bulk, one request each, and stored with tonight's in one transaction; a missed session whose file cannot be fetched or carries none of the index stops the night by name before anything is stored (see: A session the night finds missing is fetched in bulk before tonight's)the fetch line counts the missed sessions caught up; a stop is on the run page's stale-and-failed region with the session nameda night that did not run leaves every name short the same session, and the calendar the store can observe is the union of its names' dates, so that hole is the one it cannot see. Which weekdays are sessions comes from a table of the exchange's closures pinned in code, checked against the operator's store over the year it holds, which refuses a weekday outside its range rather than guessing. The newest session is read off the rows a bulk file stored, because a backfill writes a joining name's year through tonight and read over every bar it made a missed session look stored
A night on a day the exchange did not tradebefore anything is fetched the night asks the closure table whether its session was traded, and on a weekend or a closure it writes one run log row naming the day, fetches nothing and exits 0 (see: A night on a day the exchange did not trade fetches nothing and exits clean)the run log carries the row, under the closing stage with an outcome of its own that the stale-and-failed region does not count as a failure; the page stays on the last night that listeda night asking the provider for a day with no session is refused at the fetch for a file dated the day before or holding none of the index, which recorded a failure every weekend and rolled back a missed Friday caught up on a Saturday. A weekday the table cannot place is still refused, since the table exists to refuse rather than guess
An index change announced before it takes effecta name is a member on a session when it joined on or before it, or its join date is unknown, and has not left by it; the stages that list, count or show the index read that, and the stages that store bars and their adjustment read every name that has not left by the session, a name announced to join included (see: An announced index change takes effect on its effective date, and a joining name is stored from the announcement)a leaving name keeps its row on the list until its leave date and a joining name gains one on its join datethe membership feed carries a rebalance before it takes effect, and reading a name as a member when its row had no leave date dropped three names still in the index from every stage for seven sessions and listed four that were not yet in it. A joining name is stored from the announcement because its backfill runs once, for a name holding no bars, and a name backfilled early and then not stored until it joins would carry a hole nothing fills
A ticker the index feed stops listingthe night whose membership feed does not list a span still open on its session closes that span on the session, whether the ticker is gone from the feed or listed under another join date, and a span the feed lists again is reopened; a night whose feed stops listing more than 10 tickers in one night closes none of them, and its membership step ends partial (see: A ticker the index feed stops listing leaves the index on the night it goes unlisted). The S&P 400's and 600's funds' files are read the same way, a fund that stops listing more than 8 of the 400's or 12 of the 600's tickers in one night closing none of them, 2 per cent of each index's members, proposed and settled by their first year's nightsthe ticker leaves the universe and tonight's list that night and the run page's membership line names it; a night that closed none has its membership step on the stale-and-failed region with every ticker nameda provider that renames a ticker lists the new one and stops listing the old without a leave date on either, so closing only the spans the feed dates kept one company in the index under two tickers and, from a rebalance, under three. A feed missing that many names at once is a fault in the feed rather than that many departures
A fund's holdings file the night cannot reada fund's file that is refused, does not answer on any try, or answers with something that is not a holdings file, a page stating no date its holdings are as of, carrying no row of column names or no column naming each holding's type, or listing no stock among them, changes no span of its index: the S&P 400's or 600's members of the night before stay its members, and the membership step ends partial (see: The S&P 400's and 600's members are read each night from their funds' own holdings files)the run page's stale-and-failed region names the membership step with the index, the fund and why its file was not read, and every stage reads that index's members as they stooda file that cannot be read is a fault in the file and not the index emptied, so closing every span it no longer lists would take a whole index out of the universe for a night; the S&P 500's members, read from the provider's own answer, are loaded whatever a fund's file did
The provider serves no year for a name the backfill asks fornothing is stored, and the name is asked for again on the refetch's schedule, on each of the nights after the first and then weekly, until a request stores its year or the name leaves the index; the backfill step ends partial on every night a member holds no year (see: A name the backfill stored nothing for is asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that, and its page and the run page say so until one stores its year)the run page's stale-and-failed region names the name on every night it holds no year, with the nights it was asked for and when it is asked next, and its page opens with a line saying the samea name the provider cannot serve one night may be served the next, and asking for it on every night it stays a member is a per-name request a night on a path that carves out one; asking once would leave a new member with no prices for good after one bad answer
A gap in one name's seriesrefuses to store, and computes nothing across the gap for that name (see: Bars are never interpolated)that name's chart shows the gap and its level and plan sections say not computedan interpolated bar produces averages and swings that never happened. A gap is a session the exchange traded and the store does not hold, detected against the trading calendar rather than against the rows (see: A gap is a session the exchange traded and the store does not hold)
A split or dividend not caughtthe corporate action check refetches the year; if the check itself fails the name is marked suspect, and it refetches it again on each of the nights after, with or without an action of its own that day, until one refetch succeeds or the name's retries are spent, and after that on the first night a week or more after it was last asked for, until one succeeds or the name leaves the index; the name stays suspect with the reason its last refetch failed for, and its figures are computed over its stored series (see: Adjusted history is re-fetched after a corporate action) (see: A suspect name is asked for again on the five nights after it is marked and weekly after that, and its own page, its row on tonight's list and the run page say so until a refetch succeeds)the name page opens with a line saying its prices may not reflect a recent dividend or split, with when the refetch was last tried and why it failed, and the exported report carries it; the name's row on tonight's list says so beside the name; and the run page's stale and failed region lists the check as partial, naming the suspect name, on every night the name stays suspect, and on each night its retries are spent and it is not asked for says so with when it was last asked for and whyadjusted history silently diverges from the provider otherwise, and nothing downstream would notice. The stored series is adjusted, one price set per bar, which is what gives the check anything to do (see: The stored series is adjusted). The retries are bounded because a failure that lasts would otherwise make a per-name request on every night it lasts, and asked for weekly once spent because a failure the provider has cleared would otherwise stay in the store until another action landed. A suspect name is named on its own surfaces because its figures are computed over prices that may not carry the action, and rather than dropped because a check that stopped asking in silence would look exactly like one that found nothing
Cloud model unavailablethe research pass does not start; stored research still rendersthe researched sections show their as-of date, or an offer to write them laterthe computed report is complete and useful on its own
A paid job's profile names a key the secrets file does not holdthe job stops before it fetches or asks anything and no other profile answers for it; a research pass writes the plain line saying which profile and which key as its own run log row, which the drain settles the request under as refused (see: A paid model is one interface with an implementation per wire format, and a job never falls back from the profile it names)the run page's stages that failed name the pass in the line's own wordsa profile answering in another's place would leave the model that wrote a section unknowable, and a refusal written only where nobody reads it would leave the request waiting with nothing saying why
A source is returned but its text cannot be retrievedthe result is discarded rather than cited; the run log records the url and the reasonnothing, unless every source for a section fails, in which case the section is absentsome sites refuse automated access, so a search can return a promising result whose document never arrives. Citing it would leave a claim pointing at nothing, which is the failure the stored-source rule exists to prevent. A gated source is out of scope rather than worked around, and access is ranked before reputation (see: Gated sources are out of scope, and access is ranked before reputation)
A pass finds no admissible source for a sectionthe section is omitted and the run log records what was fetched and why each document was refusedthe section is absent with one line saying no admissible source was foundwriting the section from an inadmissible document would produce a confident sentence resting on a price forecast or a year-old article, which is worse than a gap
Claim checker rejects twicethat section is omitted and both attempts are logged with the offending textthe section is absent with one line saying whya wrong sentence in a research report is worse than a missing one
Spend cap reachedresearch pauses for the periodthe name says research is paused and when it resumesquiet overspending is the failure this cap exists to prevent
Filing not yet parsed for a namethe numbers section shows what the provider has and marks the segment table absentan explicit absence rather than a blanka blank cell reads as zero
No band is eligible to carry a trancheno ladder is produced for that name and the report says why; the at-entry-zone condition cannot fire for itthe plan section states that no support band below the price has an anchor other than a moving averageproducing a tranche anyway would place a purchase on a level that exists only because the price is where it is
Earnings date missingthe earnings reason cannot fire and the calendar says the date is not on filean explicit blanka guessed date is a wrong date
Listings written before the 5.4 correctionthe rows are kept as written, and the run page's record counts earnings soon and breakout on volume only off rows carrying the value the corrected rule writes, and states the nights each of their records stands on counted the same way (see: Sessions to a dated event are counted on the exchange calendar and never on stored bars)the tonight, run, universe and name routes for such a session, and the report exported from a name page, carry one line saying earnings soon on those rows counted every future print as tonight's, and breakout on volume could not firea listing records what its night listed and is never rewritten, and a page drawing those rows without the line would present what the defect wrote as that night's reading
A name whose trend state cannot be classifiedthe ladder row is still written, its trend state is recorded as not classified with the input that was missing, and no tranche is placed (see: The trend state is read from the averages and the last two swings, and a name that cannot be classified says so)the plan section states which input the rule needed and did not have, and the trend state reads as not classified rather than as a rangethe label decides whether a plan exists at all, so defaulting it to a range where nothing could be measured would place a purchase on the strength of an absent measurement. Same rule as an average of sixty bars never being labelled 200-day. The row is written rather than withheld because the trend-changed condition compares tonight's label against last night's, and a name with no row has no yesterday
Fewer than 200 bars for a new index memberthe 200-day average is recorded as not available with the bar count"not available, nn bars"an average of sixty bars labelled 200-day is a lie
A name leaves the indexmembership records the leave date; its stored history and research are keptit disappears from the universe and its old reports still opendeleting it would falsify every past night it was part of
A condition has fired but nothing has resolved yetthe run page shows the fired count and the resolved count, and withholds the verdictan explicit "not enough resolved yet, nn of nn" rather than a ratea hit rate over four resolved setups looks like a measurement and is not one
A section is assigned to the local lane that the machine cannot holdthe pass is refused before it starts and the section is left for the paid path; the run log names the section and the reasonthe section is absent as usual, with the option to have it writtenattempting it anyway produces either an out-of-memory failure or, worse, a fluent answer from a model too small for the evidence, which nothing downstream would catch
The machine slept and the overnight queue did not runnothing is written; the next run reports the gapthe run page states that the queue did not run and on which night, and each name's page names the earlier night its key under each figure was written for rather than drawing the keya queue that silently fails looks identical to a quiet night, so the absence has to be stated rather than inferred from an empty result (see: The overnight run holds the machine awake and reports whether it ran) (see: A night the overnight queue did not run is a traded session with no queue row, read on the run page against the exchange calendar)
A search returns snippets rather than full page textthe result is not stored as a document and no claim may rest on it; the run log records the url and that what came back was short of a documentnothing, unless every candidate for a section failed that way, in which case the section is absent with its reasona snippet cannot serve as the document a claim rests on, so storing one would satisfy the provenance rule with a document nobody can check the claim against. The query asks for full page text, and this row is what happens when the answer ignores it (see: A theme search is scoped by parameter, not by hope)
A search returns a site the applicable list does not carrythe result is discarded before its text is read, the tool having returned the text in the same answer, and the run log names the domainnothingthe list decides which sites a search may return and the per-document test decides whether an article may be believed, and neither substitutes for the other, so an off-list result is dropped at the cheaper of the two gates (see: A list of publishers is a noise filter, never a correctness test)
A document's publish date falls outside the window the pass asked foradmissibility refuses it and the row is kept with that reason and no bodynothing, unless every candidate failed, in which case the section is absent with one line saying no admissible source was founda year-old article carrying a previous fiscal year's guidance reads as current to anything that only checks provenance, which is one of the four kinds a trial search actually returned (see: A stored source is not automatically an admissible one)
The search tool is unavailablethe theme pass does not start and the stored theme record is left as it was rather than half-written; a name whose pass wanted a refresh is written from its own filings and news with the cycle section absentthe industry cycle section absent with its reason, and every other section writtenthe theme record is shared by every name in its industry, so its absence must not stop the sections that do not depend on it. Refused inside the feed rather than after it, because only the feed can tell a tool that did not answer from one that answered with nothing (see: A feed is unavailable when it does not answer, and wrong when it answers with something else)
The local model is unavailablethe sections in the local lane are left unwritten, the overnight queue records that it could not run, and a pass on demand writes the paid lane's sections and leaves the local lane's absentthe local-lane sections absent with their reason, and the option to have the paid model write themthe local lane is the free one, so its absence costs a draft rather than a report. It is a separate row from the cloud model's because the two lanes fail into different halves of the report and the answer for each is the other lane (see: The overnight queue writes the local lane's sections that rest on no document for every name, and the paid model is for names you get serious about)
The local model is not loaded or still loading when a pass reaches itbefore the first call of a pass, or of a night's overnight queue, the lane reads the runtime's list of its models, loads one listed and not loaded at the context its profile names, unloading any other model first so the runtime holds one, and calls it once the runtime says the load is done; a model already loaded or loading at its profile's context or more, or at one the list does not state, is not loaded again and its first call carries the profile's load allowance beside its own timeout, while one the list states at a smaller context is unloaded and loaded again at the profile's; a model the runtime does not hold, a load it refuses and one past the allowance are the local model unavailable for the rest of the pass or the night, no later call loading againnothing while it loads and the sections as usual after; where the load failed, the local-lane sections absent with their reasona model still loading answers no section, so a lane that called it at once would leave a pass's sections unwritten on a model about to answer, and a model loaded on demand or by hand comes up at a context other than the one the lane planned its prompts for (see: The local lane loads its model at its profile's context before its first call of a night or a pass, and loads again a model held at a smaller one)
The local lane's settings flag no model as the default or more than onethe lane calls no model and is the local model unavailable, in a line naming the profiles it read, and so for a flagged profile missing a value or holding one that is not a number: the night runs every step and its overnight queue's row says it could not run and why, and a pass on demand writes the paid lane's sections and leaves the local lane's absent; a key on the lane still refuses the night and the pass before they startthe overnight queue's line on the run page, or the local-lane sections absent with that line as their reasonthe lane calls one model and the code names none, so settings flagging none or two name no model it could call, and calling one regardless would be the build choosing the model; the flags are edited by hand to switch models, and a slip in them costing the night's arithmetic would cost far more than the drafts it is about (see: The local lane calls the one model its settings flag as the default, and a profile it cannot read is the local model unavailable)
A theme refresh fails while a name's pass depends on itthe name's other sections are written and stored, the industry cycle section is omitted with its reason, and the theme record is left as it wasevery section but the cycle, and one line saying the theme could not be refreshed, which where the model declined the cycle says it declined for lack of industry sources with the pages the searches found and the sector the list carries no site of its own fora per-name pass reads its own filings and news and needs the theme record for one section, so discarding the pass on a theme failure would throw away work that succeeded and would charge for it twice when it ran again (see: Industry research is per theme, not per name)
Something tries to edit or delete a register rowthe write is refused: one asked of the registrar is refused with the attempt on the run log, and one made against the file, a replace included, is refused by the table, which writes nothing, the run log included, because the refusal rolls back the statement it refuses (see: Candidate conditions are registered before they are scored, and a candidate's picks are shown on the Run page while its outcomes wait for a look)nothing changes; the register still reads as it dida register that can be edited after results are in is not a pre-registration, and the guardrail resting on it quietly stops working
The candidate register and the correction disagreethe harness fails; no verdict is shown until they agreethe condition verdicts are absent with the reason stateda divisor that does not match the number of things being tested silently removes the correction, which is the failure the correction exists to prevent
The harness cannot parse this documentevery claim is reported UNEXAMINED and nothing is signed offa verify page that is all UNEXAMINEDunexamined is never a pass
Breadth not available on a nightthe market gate fails for every member, with how many members held a close and a 200-day average of how many, and every other gate is still evaluated and storedtonight's header and the run page say breadth is not available with the counts, and every name's gates say the samea share read over a handful of members would open or close the list on a handful
A gate's reading is absent for a namethat gate fails with the reason the reading is absent, and never passes on an absencethe name's gates name the reading and why it is absenta gate passing on a missing value is a list built from what nobody measured
The market gate closed on a nightno member passes, every gate is still evaluated and stored for every member, and the night asks for no report and says why on its rowtonight's list draws no row and one line with the night's breadth and the gate's floor, or with breadth not available, and the header's count is 0; close to a buy point draws the members short of the market alone beneath one line stated once that they would qualify if the market turneda list drawn on a night the market's own trend says not to buy is the list the gate exists to stop, and a blank list would read as a night that did not run (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it) (see: A member that missed exactly one gate and no exclusion is drawn close to a buy point nearest first, and recommends nothing)
No name passed the swing filter on a nightthe list is empty, and the night asks for no report and says why on its rowtonight's list draws one line with how many members reached each gate, and the run page's funnel the same countsan empty list that does not say where its names stopped reads as a night that did not run (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it)
Both lists on tonight's page empty on a night the swing filter listedno member passed, and none missed exactly one gate with nothing excluding ittonight's list draws its own line and close to a buy point one line saying no member missed exactly one gate tonight with nothing excluding ittwo empty regions that do not each say why read as a night that did not run, and a second list that vanished on a quiet night would read as one that was never built (see: A member that missed exactly one gate and no exclusion is drawn close to a buy point nearest first, and recommends nothing)
A shape proposal rejectedthe command writes the decision, when it was taken and its reason on the proposal's row, and no setting, version or registration changes; the filter runs on under the open version, and the proposer writes the next proposal for it once sixty more ordinary nights are storedthe run page draws the proposal as rejected with its reasona rejection that moved anything would be an acceptance under another name, and one that deleted the proposal would leave no record of what was turned down
A stock a family passes while a trade for it is still openthe family lister lists it under no family and stores a row for each family that passed it, naming the family and the night that listed the trade still open; the stock is free from the night after that trade endsthe card of each family that passed it says in a note that it qualified again and names the night its open trade was listed on, and no card draws a row for ita stock listed again while its trade is open is one move counted twice, and a card that dropped it without a word would read as a stock that stopped qualifying (see: A stock holds one trade across every swing family, and one qualifying under two is listed once under the first in the page's order)
A stock two families pass on one nightit is listed once, under the first of them in the page's order with a place left, its row carrying the other family's label; the later family stores it as listed under another and gives it none of its own placesone row, on the earlier family's card, with a label naming the other setup, and a note under the later card naming the card that draws ittwo rows for one stock read as two trades, and the night's count of buy points would count it twice (see: A stock holds one trade across every swing family, and one qualifying under two is listed once under the first in the page's order)
A night the families list no stockthe family lister records the session as one the families drew and stores no listed row, and the night asks for no reporteach family's card is drawn with why it lists none: the market check closed every list, no stock passed its gates, or every stock it passed is held back, which the notes beneath saya page holding no card on a quiet night reads as a night that did not run, and a card with no reason reads as a setup that is not being looked for (see: Tonight's page is drawn from setup families, each a rule of its own listing at most five a night)
A member holding too few sessions for a breakout to be readthe gate the sessions are missing for reads not available with the count the store holds, the member does not pass, and its answer is stored with that reason; its other gates are read as they standno row on the breakout's card; where the card lists none, the member is among those its line counts as not passing the gatea year's high read over fewer sessions is a lower bar, and a name that joined the index last month would break out of a year it does not hold (see: A breakout is a close above the year's high on heavy volume after its ranges narrowed, sold on a trailing stop with no target)
A breakout with no typical move to place its stop bythe family's trade gate does not pass, no stop is stored, and the member is not passed whatever its chart; a trade whose night's raw close sits at or under its stored stop is counted as not scorable and is given no outcomeno row on the breakout's carda breakout's whole plan is its stop, and a stop placed by a figure the night does not hold is a guess stored as a price (see: A breakout is a close above the year's high on heavy volume after its ranges narrowed, sold on a trailing stop with no target)
A print whose actual the calendar does not carry yetthe earnings drift reads no surprise for it, its beat gate does not pass, and the member's answer is stored with that reason; a night inside the window on which the actual has been filed reads it then, and buys at that night's closeno row on the earnings drift's card until the actual is filed; the name is counted among those a single gate shorta report after the close reaches the calendar a night later than its reaction, and a surprise assumed from the reaction would be a number the provider never sent (see: Each print's reaction is read from the nightly calendar and the stored bars, and the earnings drift is the one rule that reads it)
A reaction session the stored bars do not reachthe move annotator stores no reaction for the print and counts it, so the earnings drift reads the name's newest stored print, or none; where a stored print's session or the close before it is not among the member's bars, the print gate reads not available and every later gate reads no printno row on the earnings drift's carda reaction is a close against the close before it, and one read across a session the store does not hold is a move nobody measured (see: The earnings drift buys a beat with a strong reaction within five sessions, stopped under the reaction session's low)
A member the membership names no sector forit is counted in no sector's median and ranked in none, and the pullback's variant in the top sectors does not fire on it, its verdict saying it is not ranked; the pullback's own rule reads no sector and judges it as any othernothing on any card; the variant's verdict on the member's row says it is not rankeda stock with no sector cannot lead one, and placing it in a sector by guess would move that sector's rank (see: The sector leaders are a variant of the pullback's starting point and not a family of their own)
A sector too small to ranka sector holding fewer members with a return than the floor is given no rank, the sectors ranked are counted without it, and none of its members leads, the variant's verdict for each saying it is not rankednothing on any card for any of its membersa median over a few stocks would put a sector first on one member's year (see: The sector leaders are a variant of the pullback's starting point and not a family of their own)
A leader sweep name with no sectorit is in no sector's ranking and lists nothing, and the report counts the history's names that carry a sector and those that do not, with how many of the latter the index held on the history's last sessionthe sweep's page states the counts above the proposalthe membership files a sector as it stands today, so a name the index has let go may carry none, and a ranking needs the sector a name was given; the count says how far the record reads the members that stayed (see: A setup family's sweep replays its own rule over the stored history and proposes the best edge among the settings meeting its floors, or brings the strongest where none does)
A rebalance the night's book stored that the heavyweights' replay reads differentlythe report names the session and the sector with the companies each read and the leaders, counts the sectors read as stored against all it compared and goes on, and names a stored session the history does not hold (see: The heavyweights' sweep replays the book over the pulled history across its settings and proposes the best edge among those meeting the family sweeps' floors)the sweep's page lists each difference under its sentence on the replaythe night values a member from its newest fetch and the sweep from the pulled counts and splits, so a dividend since a fetch or a count filed after the pull can move a rank, and a replay differing unseen would propose settings for a rule the night does not run
A heavyweight still held at the history's endit counts in no year and in no figure of its setting's but the count of holdings still held, which the setting's row states (see: An unresolved setup is never a win)the column of holdings held at the end on each setting's rowa holding not yet sold has no result, and reading it at the last close would score a trade the rule has not ended
A wider index's answer lists no member, or cannot be readthe members pull stores nothing for that index and its row says why, and the wider universe's run refuses to start while the store holds no member of either index (see: A wider universe is tested first on today's members, and widened only where a family's edge improves even so and holds on membership as it stood)the members pull's row on the run log, and the run's own refusal naming the pull to makea run over the 500 alone read as the 1,500 would answer the question with the very universe it asks about widening
A member of the S&P 400 or 600 a pull does not servethe name is named on the pull's row and stores nothing, the others are stored and the pull goes on, as a name of the S&P 500's history is; the 1,500 reads it as a member with no bars, so no family lists itthe pull's row names each name not serveda ticker an index files today may be one the provider serves another company's history under, or none, and a pull stopped for one name would leave the test without the rest
A family sweep with no setting meeting its floorsthe report proposes nothing and states the provisional setting's record, the five strongest settings with the floors each falls short of and by how much, what could be tried next and every setting's figures; the family keeps its provisional settings and keeps listing, and nothing is registeredthe sweep's page states the five strongest settings and what could be tried next beneath its provisional record, and never that the family is set asidea starting point the history does not hold steady would be a fit to it, so the family keeps its provisional settings and its picks until the operator rules, and its freeze registers nothing (see: A setup family's sweep replays its own rule over the stored history and proposes the best edge among the settings meeting its floors, or brings the strongest where none does) (see: No family on any index is set aside or hidden by a test result without the operator's word)
A registered family rule whose evaluator the code no longer carries or has movedthe family evaluator evaluates it on no member, stores the reason in its place on every member's row of its family, and writes its stage as failed naming the rule, while every other rule is evaluated and the night goes onthe run page draws the family rules stage failed with the rule and whya rule evaluated under code its registration does not name is evidence about another rule, and a hole in its record is one the correction divides by, so it is named on the night it opens, as the listings stage names a moved candidate (see: A registered family rule is evaluated every night at its own settings and keeps its own list, its trades stored with their benchmark when they end)
A family rule's trade whose stock's closes run out before it endsonce its cap's sessions have passed it is ended on its cap's last session with no result, its stock free on the rule's list from the night after, and its benchmark is written as any other'sthe rule's trades count it, and its decided trades and its edge do nota trade nobody can price has no result, and holding its stock for as long as the record runs would keep the rule from ever listing it again (see: A registered family rule is evaluated every night at its own settings and keeps its own list, its trades stored with their benchmark when they end)
A family rule's benchmark whose night holds no member to enterno member the index held that night carries a bar, a typical move and the closes the cap reaches, or the trade's plan names no typical move to set the same plan by, so the benchmark is stored as none with no member countedthe rule's trades count it, and its decided trades and its edge do notan edge over nothing is the trade's own result passed off as what it added over the market (see: A registered family rule is evaluated every night at its own settings and keeps its own list, its trades stored with their benchmark when they end)
No trade listed yetnothing is computed or written; the Past picks screen reads the swing filter's rows and finds no name it passed on a night it listedthe screen draws one line saying no trade has been listed yet and that every trade the live list recommends is followed there from its night on, and no count, share or tablea table of nothing with six zeros above it reads as a list that recommended trades and all of them came to nothing
A trade whose outcome row is missingthe trade is still drawn, with the plan its night's trade gate read, and counted as listed and in no status; nothing is scored for it on the screenits status reads no outcome stored, its trade line draws the plan and no dot and says no outcome stored, and the counts say how many trades carry no outcome rowa trade left out because its outcome is missing is a recommendation removed from the record, and one drawn as open would be a price the store never said it stood at
A still open trade whose outcome row is missingthe open trade rule reads the trade as open until its cap's sessions have passed, so a stock the filter passes again inside the cap stands on Still open and its listing is marked as a repeat, and is free again once the cap has passed (see: A stock holds one open trade on each rule's list, and it is free the night after its trade ends)the Still open row draws the plan and no dot, says no outcome stored and that the trade is read as open until its sessions run out, and Past picks marks the repeat as listed again while that trade was opena row that is not there says nothing either way; read as a closed trade it would list the stock twice inside the cap, the case the rule exists for, and read as decided it would be an outcome the store never said it had
A member the provider returns no quarter fornothing is stored, the ask is recorded as nothing returned, and the member is marked absent and asked again on the quarters step's schedule; every night reads it as no fundamentals yet, and it is judged and listed as any other member, drawn with the members reading no state (see: Four readings of a member's reported quarters are worked out every night by rules the measured split settled, and its state is read from sales and operating margin alone)its state reads no fundamentals yet and what the numbers say says no reported quarter is stored for it; the quarters step's line in the run page's operational header counts it among the asks that returned nothingabsent is never a failure: a state a gate read would take a member off the list for the provider's silence, and one left out of the order would drop a name the gates passed
A member's new quarter is not yet posted when it is askedthe answer is not stored, the ask is recorded as not yet posted with the newest quarter the answer carried, and the member is asked again on each of the five nights after and weekly after that until an answer carries the quarter or a later report replaces it; its readings stay on the quarters stored, naming the quarter awaited (see: A member's reported quarters are fetched on the night after it reports, and asked for again on the five nights after and weekly after that until the quarter is posted)what the numbers say names the quarter awaited and the quarter the readings were read from; the quarters step's line in the run page's operational header counts it among the asks whose quarter was not yet posteda provider posts a quarter days after the report as often as on the night after it, and an answer stored without the new quarter would be read as the newest quarter's
The provider refuses a quarters asknothing is stored for that member, the ask is recorded as refused with the provider's reason, the member is asked again on the quarters step's schedule, and the step goes on to the next memberthe quarters step's line in the run page's operational header counts the ask among those refused, and the ask's own row keeps the provider's reasonone member's refusal is that member's, and a step stopped by it would leave every other member's quarter for another night
The quarters step reaches its limit or the day's allowanceno ask starts after it, the members left are counted on the step's row and asked on the next night, and the night goes on to the overnight queuethe run page's operational header says how many members were left at the step's limit or at the day's allowancethe step is bounded apart from the arithmetic, so a peak reporting night neither stops the night nor spends the next day's allowance
A night that stored no readings of the reported quarterstonight's page, the overnight queue, the night's own request and Past picks draw that night in the swing filter's own order, and no state is drawn for it (see: Tonight's list is the swing filter's with improving businesses drawn first, and an evening is listed and ordered by the rule that listed it)that night's rows on tonight's page carry no state word, a Past picks trade listed that night reads not read that night, and a name's page for that night draws its numbers without what the numbers sayan evening keeps the order it was drawn in, and a state read from quarters fetched later would reorder a night after the fact
The point-in-time check finds a differencethe run stops before the first stage, keeping its candidates, and writes its report listing every difference, the name, the session, the reading, the sweep's value and the night's, proposing nothing; started again under the same build it reads the saved candidates and runs the check again (see: The sweep ranks on the edge over the same plan entered on every member, with one open trade a stock and seven conditions tested in steps)the sweep's page says the sweep did not read every session as it stood and lists the differencesa run that went on past a reading the night would have computed otherwise would rank settings over a history no night saw, and the point-in-time result is the one figure the whole report rests on
A sweep candidate with no sector labelthe name stays in and reads no sector rank, so a sector condition that is on fails it and a condition that is off reads it as any other candidate; the report states how many candidates carry no rank and how many names the index held carry no sector, most of them departed (see: The sweep ranks on the edge over the same plan entered on every member, with one open trade a stock and seven conditions tested in steps)the sweep's page, in what was read as it stands todayremoving the names with no sector would remove mostly the names that left the index, and a sector condition read over survivors alone reads better than the market was
A stepped plan filled nearer its stop than the stop setting's floorthe listing is counted under that setting as a setup never entered: it is listed, holds its night and holds the stock through its end as the pages' rule holds it, and carries no result, while a setting whose stop floor the fill meets counts it as a trade on the risk its plan stated (see: The stepped plan's result is counted on the risk its plan stated, and a fill nearer its stop than the stop setting's floor is no trade)the sweep's page counts, for each kind of plan, the results beyond its bound either way with the largest and the smallest, and states each record again without its largest results by sizea result counted on a risk near nothing reads an ordinary gain as hundreds of times it: one trade of the stepped plan carried every design the run of 2026-10-01 ranked highest
An ideas' run in which no idea passesthe starting point is the base, holding no idea, and where the base is not better than today's rule by the same test it is today's rule with the base a variant; the variants are read one change from it as everthe ideas' report says no idea passed and states the base beside today's rule with every idea's figures and answersa starting point the history does not hold better than the base would be a fit to it, so the base stands until the operator rules and nothing is registered (see: A new idea is added to the base one at a time and kept only where it is better in six of eight years)
The provider refuses or sends nothing for the index or the VIX on a nightthat series stores nothing that night and the night goes on, as it does where the provider does not answer in time or answers in a form that cannot be read; a market switch reading it is closed on a night its closes do not reach, so the rules holding that switch list nothing that night, and a later night's fetch, which asks for the whole span again, stores the sessions it missedthe fetch step's market series row names the series and why, an answer that cannot be read with the reader's own words, and the family evaluator's row states each switch closed and whya night stopped for a series only two variants read would hold back every list and every record for a figure no live rule reads, and a switch passing on a close it does not hold would list stocks on a night the market was never read (see: The night asks for the market series' daily closes once a series, and keeps them apart from the members' bars)
The store's year holds fewer closes than a heavyweights' rebalance reads, or the rebalance reads no lead or no betathe book does not rebalance that night: its holdings are carried and kept, sold only under their average where the setting reads that and at their last close as members, nothing is bought or sold at a rebalance and no row of the month is stored, and it rebalances on the first night after that whose stored year holds the closes its readings need and reads a lead, and a beta where it reads one; a month whose stored rows read no lead is read again the same way; the S&P 400's and 600's books wait the same waythe heavyweight book's row names the sessions held and needed, or that no sector's largest companies read a lead or a beta, the page's book and each registered rule's apart, the index families' row the same for each index's books, and the card says the month's rebalance waits and names the session the book reads it ona book reading every return or beta as none would store the month as read and sell every holding as no longer the leader on figures it never read, and buy nothing until the next month (see: The sector heavyweights hold the largest companies leading their sectors, rotated on the first session of each month whose stored year holds the closes their readings need)
A sector fund or the index holds no close for a heavyweights' rebalance nighta book whose rule reads the funds or the betas does not rebalance that night: its holdings are carried and kept, nothing is bought or sold at a rebalance and no reading is stored, and it rebalances on the first night after that the store holds the night's close of every fund and of the index; a later night's fetch, which asks for the whole span again, stores what the night missedthe heavyweight book's row names each series it waits for and the night it holds none for, the page's book and each registered rule's aparta sector read as leading nothing because its fund was not fetched would sell its holdings on a figure the night never read, and one read against a stale close would buy on a lead nobody measured (see: The sector heavyweights freeze at their sweep's proposal, the proposal's three passing neighbours registered beside them as variants)
The provider does not serve a member's estimates on the nightthe member is read as not raised, so the variant reading the estimates does not fire on it, and nothing is stored for it, so a run of the rest of the night asks for it again; the other members' answers are stored and the night goes on, as it does where the provider does not answer in time or answers in a form that cannot be readthe estimates fetcher's row names the member and why, the swing filter's row repeats it after the members it asked about, and the variant's verdict on the member says not read and whya variant firing on an estimate it never read would list a stock on a revision nobody saw, and a night stopped for a figure one variant reads would hold back every list (see: The night asks for the estimates of each member a rule reading them passes on everything else, once a member a night)
A market series missing on a session an idea readsthe switch reading it fails that night, as a gate fails on an absent value, and an average with a missing close in its window is unread; a series the store holds none of leaves the switches reading it out of the runthe ideas' report names any switch left out and states each series it read with its sessions, its first and last, and its pulla switch passing on a session it could not read would list stocks on a night the market was never checked (see: The index's and the VIX's daily series are pulled beside the pulled bars, marked by their pull and read by no night)
A chunk of the sweep fails twicethe run stops there, keeping every chunk saved before it, and writes its report saying which chunk failed and why, proposing nothing; started again it reads the history again and goes on from the first chunk it lacks (see: The sweep reads the live store read-only in short reads and writes nothing to it, pausing for every night)the sweep's page names the chunk and the error, the chunks it had saved and the time each stage tooka run that went on past a chunk it could not compute would report figures missing part of the history, and one that started over would lose its saved work to one fault
The night's checkout is off main or holds a commit the remote's main lacksthe night's script refuses before any worker exists, builds nothing and writes nothing to the store; it writes the instant and the reason to a file under the data root, which tonight's page and the Run page read as the night's state for the session the refusal fell on, and exits non-zero so the scheduler records the failure; a checkout behind the remote's main runs its own commit and says so in the line the night records, and an uncommitted or untracked file is never built and costs no night (see: Each night is built from a clean copy of the main checkout's own commit and never from its working tree, and refuses only a checkout off main or ahead of the remote's main)tonight's notice and the Run page's headline say the night was refused before its first step and why, and no press offers to run the rest of ita night built from whatever the working tree held would run an edit meant for a branch as live code, and a refusal recorded nowhere a page reads would show as a night that never ran
The news job's model does not answerthe labeller asks the provider for its model list before anything, which bills nothing, and stops there with its line on its own row, and no other profile answers for it; a model that stops answering partway stops the run where it is, the labels written so far kept, since each is written as it is read (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own) (see: A paid model is one interface with an implementation per wire format, and a job never falls back from the profile it names)the labeller's own row on the run log says the model did not answer, and the listed names' articles stay unlabelled under that profilea fallback would label under a profile the operator did not name, and a label is kept by the profile that wrote it
An answer the labeller cannot readthe article is asked for once more under a round of its own; failing twice it is stored as unreadable with the second answer's cause, one of the seven the instruction names, so it is not paid for again under that profile and the instruction's version, and the run counts it by cause (see: A label's reason is one sentence holding no digit, and an answer code cannot read is asked once more and then kept as unreadable with its cause)the run's row counts the unreadable answers by cause, and the article stays unlabelleda reason holding a digit would put a number in prose no facts file holds, and a third call for the same article buys the same answer
The labeller's month limit reachedno call starts once the labeller's own rows for the month sum to its limit, and the call whose ceiling would pass it is not made; the names left wait for the next night (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own)the run's row names the month limit as its stop and how many names it reacheda limit judged after the call is an allowance, not a limit
The day or month cap pauses a labelthe call is not made and the labeller stops where it is, as research pauses, keeping the labels it wrote (see: The spend cap is a stop, not an allowance)the run's row names the cap as its stopone cap stands over every paid job, and a job going on under a paused cap would spend what the cap exists to stop
The labeller's time limit passesno call starts after it, and the names and articles left wait for the next night, which takes what the window still holds (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own)the run's row names the time limit as its stop and the names it reacheda long list on one night is bounded without losing an article, since one still inside the window is asked for on the next
A peak window of the news profile opens while the labeller runsno call starts inside it: before its next call the labeller waits for the window to end, as the drain does, and then asks, its time limit counted over the time it labels and not the time it waits; a profile naming no windows never waits, and a wait that does not see the window end stops the run there (see: Queued work runs off-peak, and every schedule is written in UTC) (see: The news labeller waits for the end of a peak window rather than stopping at one, and its time limit counts the time it labels)the run's row counts the windows it waited out and the minutes it waitedevery paid call runs off peak where the provider prices a peak, and the labeller is no exception; a night ending inside a window would otherwise label none of its list
An article refused by admissibilitythe article is stored with its verdict and never sent to the model, and the run's row counts it as refused by admissibility (see: A news article is stored once per member with its admissibility judged, and a label is never overwritten) (see: A stored source is not automatically an admissible one)the row counts the refused articles, and the article stays unlabelleda claim resting on a document that failed admissibility cannot be written, and the call it would cost is saved
The labeller failsit is a process of its own, so the night's rows, its list and its order are untouched; a run refused before it asked anything, its key missing, a limit that is not a number or its model not answering, writes its own row saying why, and one that fails partway keeps the labels it wrote, each written as it was read (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the night starts after the close, and its calls and its spend are its own)the night's own row says it started the labeller, and the labeller's row, where there is one, says why it stoppeda labeller failure that changed a night's row would make a free night depend on a paid process
The drain stops on an error outside a passit writes one row under a run of its own named for the instant it started, its stage drain, its outcome failed and the error's words with no path a machine roots, and exits failing; what it left queued stays outstanding, and a request it left being written is put back by the next drain, which a press or the next night starts (see: A drain that stops on an error writes a row of its own, and the queue page states it until a pass starts after it)the queue page states the drain that stopped, the time it started and the error, until a pass starts after it, and the run page's checklist names it on the night its row fell ona drain that ended on an error wrote no row a page reads, so what it left queued waited with nothing saying why, and the queue read a request it had been writing as starting now
A replay at a family rule's registration finds a trade the rule would keep differentlythe rule's record restarts at that registration and counts from its first session, and the replay's row on the run log names the first trade that differed, its stock, its night and what differed; every rule the same replay reproduced carries its record on from where it began (see: A family rule registered again keeps its record from its first registration where a replay of its stored nights reproduces every trade, and restarts at the change otherwise)the run page states beside the rule the session its record counts from, that it restarted at its registration, and whya rule registered again counted its record from the new registration whatever the change altered, so a change that moved no trade still threw its record away and one that moved a trade did so unnamed
A name or a filer a companies, splits or revenue pull asks for is not servedit stores nothing and is named on the pull's row with the provider's refusal, the time it ran out or why its answer could not be read, and the pull goes on and stores the others, its row saying partial, as the night's series fetch reads an answer it cannot read (see: The pulls behind the heavyweights and the context checks store into tables of their own and are read by no night)the pull's printed lines and its run log row name each and whyone name the provider has dropped would otherwise stop a pull of seven hundred, and a company with nothing stored is one the readings say they cannot value or place rather than one read from nothing
A company filing no income statement with its datethe companies pull stores no quarter of income for it and names it on its row, and a statement carrying no filing date stores nothing and is counted; the profit gate and the coverage read such a company as filing fewer than four quarters, so neither passes it (see: The 400 and 600 rules start provisional with liquidity floors and a profit gate before any testing)the pull's line names each company filing none and counts the statements carrying no datea quarter that cannot be dated cannot be read as it stood, and passing a company on figures it never filed is what the gate exists to refuse
A member's quarters fetched before their interest expense was storedthe member readings store its coverage as none, its profit gate and every other reading still read, until the quarters step fetches it again after its next report and stores each quarter's interest expense with the fetch having read it (see: A member's coverage is read on the night only over quarters whose fetch read their interest expense)the member's page says its coverage was not read and whya quarter stored before the interest expense was read would read as a company owing nothing and pass the coverage on a figure no filing states
A rule registered on the S&P 400 or 600 whose evaluator moved, or whose settings its sweep's grid no longer holdsthe night reads it by none and keeps no list for it; a family whose live rule it is draws its list by the provisional rule that night and its card says provisional, until the register --moved command registers it again unchanged at the moved version, its record counting from that registration (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's swing families is registered as the family on its index and evaluated by their step alone)the index families' stage row names each rule not read with why: its evaluator's version as registered and as the code carries it, or the setting its grid refusesa rule read under code that moved since its registration would be a rule the register does not name, and its record a mix of two
A registered heavyweights rule's rebalance on a night missing what its design readsits book carries its holdings and sells where they left the index or, where its rule reads that exit, closed under their 200-day average, and buys and sells nothing for the rebalance, writing no rebalance, until the first night holding the index's fund's close where design (a) reads a beta, or SPY's closes and the industries' returns design (b) reads (see: A rule of the S&P 400's or 600's sector heavyweights keeps a book of its own in either design, read by the index families' step)the rule's card and its row on the Run page read its last rebalance as before, and the stage's row says what the rules' books bought, sold and helda rebalance read without a beta or a lead would sell every holding the rule could no longer read as bought, on a series the night failed to store rather than on the market
A fund's holdings filing the history pull cannot readthe pull names the filing and why, a filing for another of the trust's funds among them and an N-Q or an annual report carrying no complete schedule of the fund as of its quarter's end, a summary alone among them, and stores every other snapshot, its row saying partial; a list of the fund's filings or a symbol list it cannot read stores nothing and says why (see: Membership as it stood is rebuilt from the funds' quarterly holdings filed with the SEC, matched by ISIN and then by name) (see: The funds' holdings before their first public N-PORT are read from their N-Q of 2018-12-31 and their annual report of 2019-03-31)the pull's line and its run log row name each filing not readone quarter's document the archive cannot serve would otherwise stop the history, and a quarter end it skips is one the spans read across, which the pull's line says rather than leaves to be found
A fund's holding matched to no provider codethe holding is stored with no code and named on the pull's row, a holding whose name reads only codes that traded on no day in the six days to the quarter's end among them, one whose codes traded only at a close the fund's value a share stood more than 5 per cent from named apart, and each code matched to none at a holding's quarters because its closes did not move in step with the fund's values a share named with the holding, while a name's code at a steady distance from the value a share, off the level and at no one ratio, is matched to none with the holding among those matched by none (see: A holding's code is kept only where its closes move in step with the fund's values a share, and a match by name is held to the level at each quarter end as well), and a provider's ask it did not answer named beside them; from 17.1 an identifier OpenFIGI finds nothing for, or answers with placeholders alone or with tickers whose closes stand at no level and no one ratio, leaves its holding matched to none, and a mapping request refused or answered in a form that cannot be read is named on the pull's row with the identifiers it carried while the pull goes on (see: A holding the symbol lists carry under no code is mapped to the tickers it traded under through OpenFIGI, each held to the checks a name's code is); the sweeps read it as no member, so a figure on membership as it stood leaves it out, and each snapshot's share matched is read off the stored rows (see: Membership as it stood is rebuilt from the funds' quarterly holdings filed with the SEC, matched by ISIN and then by name) (see: A holding matched by name is kept only where its code traded at the quarter's end)the pull's line counts the holdings matched by ISIN, by name, by a code their fund held by ISIN within a year, carried from the next coded quarter and by none, the codes not in step, the codes asked of the provider and the identifiers mapped through OpenFIGI with the holdings a ticker it answered matched, and names those matched by none, the codes not in step and the asks not answereda code guessed from a ticker or a loose name would put another company's prices in the holding's place, as today's BBBY would for the Bed Bath & Beyond the S&P 600's fund held in 2019
A pull whose stated calls pass the provider stopthe pull prints its statement, the names and months it would ask and their weighted calls, and is refused before any request with the count, the stop and the word that goes past it on the operator's word, writing no row and asking nothing; narrowed with the codes it needs it is stated again and goes (see: Every pull states its provider calls before it runs and stops for the operator at the day's cap)the pull's line carries the statement and the refusal, and the run log holds no row of ita pull whose statement was made by hand and left out the earnings calendar's months took the day past the operator's cap on 2026-10-08, and a remedy of pulls spent the whole allowance on 2026-10-05
A rule the night did not evaluateits row for the night says the night did not evaluate it, with no listed count a stretch reads, so its stretch line and its funnel are drawn from no answer; an index whose part of the night failed has every rule of its families written so, and an index the night did not read at all has none (see: A variant's picks are shown on its card when chosen and its results only under its tests)the card's funnel reads that the night did not evaluate this rule, and the stage's row names the index not computeda rule's empty stretch counted over nights the rule was never read would flag an outage as a drought
A reading the ledger cannot readthe reading is stored as null and the setup is written with every reading the inputs reach; a loose gate that reads it fails, so the setup is not written at all where the gate's own reading is missing (see: A setup is every member-session a family's loose gates pass, and its readings are defined once and read as they stood)a null in the reading's column on the setup's row, and on the night's row the setups counted as the gates passed thema nought stored for a reading the inputs did not reach would read as a figure and move every boundary an engine later places on that reading
An index's setups the ledger could not computethat index's rows of the night are left unwritten and its windows unclosed, the failure is named under the step's row, and the other indices' rows are written while the night goes on to its close (see: A setup is every member-session a family's loose gates pass, and its readings are defined once and read as they stood)the Run page's stage row naming the index and the failurethe ledger is read by no list and no card, so a failure in it should cost the night nothing a reader waits for; the history build fills the night it missed
The archive refuses or does not answer the filings refreshthe refresh stops where it is, the facts already stored stay as they were, the days it had not finished are left unread for the next night, the stage's row names the refusal and the night goes on to the overnight queue (see: The night refreshes the facts of the members that filed since its last read of the archive's daily index, after the close under its own limit)the Run page's stage row, partial, naming the archive's refusal and the facts left as they werethe refresh is bounded apart from the arithmetic, and nothing tonight's list draws waits on it

19. Fixtures and the verification harness

This document is the specification. The harness checks the code against the claims made here, and against a committed set of inputs whose expected outputs are whatever the rules in this document produce. No external document is authoritative, and no hand-written report is treated as a thing to be reproduced. (see: A frozen fixture per checkpoint, and the harness decides sign-off)

19.1 What a fixture holds

A fixture is one folder per name and date. It is committed, never regenerated, and its expected files are derived once from the rules in sections 9 to 13 and then frozen, one per stage's serialised output rather than one over a rendered page (see: The fixture is diffed on each stage's serialised output, of which the facts file is one). The run page is the one exception and is listed as such: it holds the counts a record is drawn from rather than the markup it is drawn into, because the reason record is computed across every night the store holds and belongs to no single stage's output. 5.6 added that file and this table did not name it until the phase 5 sign-off, which is the fault 4.0 reconciled this table for once already. The first fixture uses a year of daily bars for one liquid name; later fixtures add names of different character, as section 20 sets out.

FileWhat it holdsWhy it is frozen
Inputs

19.2 What the harness checks

The harness has no opinion of its own. Every claim it reports comes from a table in this document, and a table it cannot parse makes every claim in that table UNEXAMINED rather than absent.

Claim sourceWhat is checkedHow it fails
Component cataloguea class exists with each catalogue name, spaces removed, and declares exactly the reads and writes its row listsa missing class, or a component touching a store its row leaves blank
Read and write matrixthe same declarations in both directions, so a blank cell is asserted as much as a filled onea write nobody declared, or a declaration with no code behind it
Screens tableseach region of each screen is drawn from stored values and nothing else, asserted by reading the rendered markup back against the store rather than by eyea region absent, or a figure drawn that the store does not carry
The figuresevery figure is placed, a flow figure's boxes are claims like a table's rows, and the system diagram's boxes are asserted to name components and stores the catalogue and the stores table carrya figure nothing placed, or a box naming something no table has
Limits tableeach configured value equals the documented one, and the runtime measurements stay inside the stated boundsa value drifting in configuration without the document being amended
Failure tableeach row with a fixture has its failure induced and the reader-visible outcome checkeda failure that produces something other than what the row promises
Phase tableevery expectation the current phase's row names is PASS before that phase is signed offany expectation reporting FAIL or UNEXAMINED
The fixture, first runthe facts file produced equals the expected one, byte for byteany difference, shown inline as a diff
The fixture, second runzero model calls and zero network requests, and identical stored statea call made, or state that changed on a run with no new input
The research passrun against the frozen news and filings with a recording model endpoint; the poisoned and unsourced paragraphs are rejected, the inadmissible documents are refused, and opening the name a second time spends nothinganything rejected being written, or a second open spending
The candidate registerthe register refuses updates, deletes and a replace, and the correction divisor matches the candidates standing before the window openedan accepted edit, or a divisor that does not match

19.3 What it produces

One row per claim, written twice: as a page for the operator with the diff inline for every failure, and as data for a build session to read back. Each row carries the claim, the table it came from, and one of three verdicts.

VerdictMeaning
PASSthe claim was checked and held
FAILthe claim was checked and did not hold; the diff is shown beside it
UNEXAMINEDthe claim was not checked, because its table could not be parsed, its fixture does not exist, or the code path was never reached. This never counts as a pass, and a phase carrying one is not signed off

The count of each verdict is reported alongside the rows, because a run that checked four claims and passed all four is not the same as one that checked forty, and a summary without the denominator hides the difference.

20. Build phases, each with its visible output

The first checkpoint of every phase produces something to open and look at, and the harness is what turns looking into a verdict (see: Every phase opens with something to look at). Nothing here is built.

Phase 1 carries a measurement that sets the ceiling on every later report, and it must not be replaced by an assumption. The belief that a large-company index guarantees good coverage is plainly true for the largest names and much weaker at the other end, where a mid-cap industrial may draw two or three articles a quarter, mostly wire copy and aggregator summaries. So phase 1 pulls two weeks of news across a sample of thirty names deliberately spread across the market-capitalisation range rather than chosen from the watch list, counts distinct publishers by frequency, and checks each for whether its text can actually be fetched. Two things come out: the evidence-based first draft of the source lists, which are a noise filter rather than a test of whether an article is right (see: A list of publishers is a noise filter, never a correctness test), and a measurement of how sharply coverage thins going down the index. Tuning the lists on the largest names alone would starve the bottom of the index in a way that is invisible while testing on a mega-cap.

PhaseWhat gets builtVisible firstHarness expectations addedDone when
